# SOVITECH App: product requirements document (PRD)

- **As of:** 2026-09-25
- **Status:** Draft for the product owner's review. Nothing here is approved except what is labelled Decided.
- **Built from:** docs/guardrails.md version 1.5 (2026-09-24; no change-log row after 1.5); docs/product/user-stories.md, docs/product/functions.md and docs/product/traceability.md (prompt 1, as of 2026-09-24, written against guardrails v1.5); docs/ifc-input.md; docs/build-readiness.md (as of 2026-09-23, updated 2026-09-24); design/onboarding-spec.md; design/dashboards-spec.md; prompts/sovitech-ai-system.md; company/ (context and brand only).
- **Written by:** docs/dev-prompts/02-prd.md. Prompt 3 (docs/dev-prompts/03-build-interactive-app.md) builds the app from this document.
- **Authority:** docs/guardrails.md overrides this PRD. Where they disagree, the guardrails win and the PRD is wrong.

**Labels.** Every requirement, decision, slice, priority, token, screen and metric carries one label for its basis.

| Label | Meaning | Where it appears |
|---|---|---|
| **Decided** | The owner's own words, quoted with the date | Status "Owner decision 2026-09-24 (OD-n: ...)" |
| **Required** | Follows from the approved design or the guardrails | Status "From approved design"; "Required by guardrails (...)" |
| **Proposed** | A recommendation, not approved: every slice tag and priority, recommended defaults, the dashboards-spec 2.5 navigation, research recommendations, a spec's "Proposed" defaults, and each dashboards-spec 7.2 or ifc-input 6.2 proposal itself | Never a requirement status. Written "Proposed (<file section>)"; listed under "Waiting on approval" and in section 15 |
| **Open** | An open question, with a D id in section 15 | Section 15 |

**Gates** are separate from the basis. A requirement whose content is Decided or Required keeps that label while a proposal or an open question stops it from shipping. Its "Gated by" line uses the contract's words: "Depends on proposal 7.2.N (not approved; D-NN)", "Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.N (not approved; D-NN)", or "Blocked by open question <source id> (D-NN)". Its "Until decided" line says what the app does meanwhile. Live-operations content has its own status, "Out of scope: operations phase".

**Ids.** Requirements R-001 to R-167 (section 7, then section 11), three digits by the owner's decision of 2026-09-24 ("Three-digit ids"), because splitting requirements by identical statuses needs more than 99. Open decisions D-01 to D-94 (section 15). Stories (US-), functions (F-), screens (OB-, DB-, UD-) and owner decisions (OD-1 to OD-8) are prompt 1's ids. Test ids are from docs/guardrails.md section 7. "ifc-input 5.4 IFC-n" cases are proposed, not indexed.

## 1. Summary

**How to read this PRD.** "You" is the product owner. "The owner" is the building owner who uses the app; labels quoted from the app, such as "For you", address that owner.

**What the app is.** A SOVITECH tool for SAUTER-based building management systems (BMS) in Romania. A building owner describes a building, mostly by uploading documents; the app shows what it found, with sources, and produces a preliminary BMS proposal and dashboards. "SOVITECH engineers review everything before it becomes a quotation" (`CLAUDE.md`). Desktop-first and dark, it is a SOVITECH brand tool: Decided (OD-1, 2026-09-24: "treat the app as our brand tool").

**For whom.** Building owners, who are not engineers; SOVITECH engineers, who verify technical facts; SOVITECH's commercial reviewer and admin (section 3). A facility manager belongs to a later operations phase, itself open (D-28).

**The two promises** (`CLAUDE.md` wording; `docs/guardrails.md` section 1, which overrides this PRD):
- "Every value is true or honestly labelled."
- "The owner is asked only what the app cannot find, and only when the answer changes the result."
- "When the two conflict: **block outputs, not people**." Only step 1's four required fields (project name, project type, city, country) block anyone (rule 7).

**The IFC direction.** Decided (OD-8, 2026-09-24): the app is built "based on data from the onboarding flow, based on IFC files from BIM softwares". IFC models exported from design software become a primary input, accepted from S1 (proposed). But a model gives no value and is never counted as searched (rules 1 and 12) until the approver, not yet named (D-05), accepts four IFC proposals (D-37, D-38, D-39, D-40) and approves the mapping tables (how approvals reach the app is D-47), SOVITECH supplies its asset taxonomy (D-92), and you revise build-readiness decision 4, which today reads only PDFs with a text layer and Excel (XLSX) files (D-01). Whether a 3D view shows a stored model is open (D-03, D-04).

**What S1 (proposed) delivers:** 48 of the 167 requirements (section 6.4), on synthetic documents only. The guardrail checks come first. Then: a development sign-in and roles; the intake wizard, asking only what the documents do not say; text PDFs and Excel files read, other formats stored as "Not analysed"; the facts found, each with its source, label and Edit; systems in scope, zones, equipment and floors; and a stored preliminary proposal. Its points (the signals the BMS handles, from which the investment is estimated) and investment figures read "Not available yet" until SOVITECH's datasets arrive with approval records (D-92, D-05, D-47). What only SOVITECH can settle goes to the engineer, never the owner, but no engineer can act on it before the queue page (R-128, S2; D-16), so the results that depend on it stay provisional.

**In practice.** S1 (proposed) is a checkpoint for you to review, not a release to owners. Found values appear only where the AI has been run on the synthetic fixtures (`docs/dev-prompts/03-build-interactive-app.md`, phase 2); every equipment type reads Unknown; and after Generate the only way back into the intake is a "Not available yet" line for a missing owner input (R-012; D-14, D-02). It is less than build-readiness's first slice, which adds points and a CAPEX (investment) range (section 6.1). It stays a proposal until you decide the first slice (D-04). Prompt 3, the build, goes on to S2 and S3 unless you limit it to S1 (proposed); Later waits (section 6). Real owner documents wait for the AI processor route (D-09), rule 13's protections, a production sign-in (D-13) and your decision on malware scanning (D-35) (section 6.11).

**The decisions that block the most**, by the requirements each holds up (section 15):

| D id | The question, in short | Who decides | Holds up |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-05 | Name the approver; accept guardrails v1.5 as the baseline | You | 10 directly; every approval waits for it, so it comes first |
| D-01 | Which formats version 1 reads: IFC, Revit (RVT), ZIP | You | 35 |
| D-92 | SOVITECH's datasets; whether prices are confidential | SOVITECH engineering; you for price confidentiality | 32 |
| D-37, D-38, D-39, D-40 | The four IFC proposals that let model values be kept | The approver | 27, 26, 26 and 26 |
| D-02 | The navigation after Generate | You | 24 |
| D-03 | The model view when no IFC is uploaded; the viewer | You, informed by a short technical trial the build runs | 15 |
| D-41, D-42 | Matching the models of one building; types inferred by code | The approver | 15 each |
| D-04 | What the first slice contains | You | 13 |

Section 15 names every party to each row. Of its 94 open decisions, 36 are yours, 55 the approver's, 2 SOVITECH engineering's and 1 counsel's. Guardrails section 10 makes the approver the product owner, but nobody is named yet, so nothing in the approver's group can be approved today. Next: your review of sections 1, 6 and 15, before prompt 3 builds the app.

## 2. Problem and context

This section is context. It defines no requirement. Rules are cited by number, and `docs/guardrails.md` wins over anything written here.

### 2.1 SOVITECH and its market

SOVITECH designs and integrates building management systems (BMS) built on SAUTER products in Romania (`CLAUDE.md`; `prompts/sovitech-ai-system.md`, opening). The company website, as recorded in `company/`, adds the context below. It is marketing copy, and this PRD uses it as context only (order of authority, level 5).

| Topic | What the current website says | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Service lines | BMS design ("Proiectare BMS"), installation and implementation ("Execuție"), systems integration ("Integrare sisteme") and maintenance ("Mentenanță"). Consultancy appears only as a footer link. | `company/business/services.md` 1 |
| SAUTER relationship | "partener autorizat" / "authorised partner" is the only relationship term the current website uses. | `company/business/company-profile.md` 4 and 10 |
| Market | Romania, with headquarters in Bucharest. | company-profile 6.1 |
| Sectors | Offices, Medical & Pharma, Retail, HoReCa & Wellness, Industrial, Educational. | `company/business/sectors.md`, "Sector list"; company-profile 6.2 |
| Protocols | The protocol names on the website describe what SOVITECH can integrate. They say nothing about a given building. In the app, a building's protocols come only from its documents (rule 1, "Interfaces"). | services 9 |

**Where the app sits in that work.** The owner describes a building, mostly by uploading documents. The app reads them, shows back what it found with sources, and produces a preliminary BMS proposal and dashboards. "SOVITECH engineers review everything before it becomes a quotation" (`CLAUDE.md`). The website's design service lists a budget estimate among its deliverables. In the app, every investment figure instead carries one of the three stage labels of rule 10 (services 9). The demo project is a fictional hotel, working name "Demo Hotel Bucharest": Decided (OD-5, 2026-09-24; asked whether the demo should keep the real hotel's name, the owner answered "no").

**What the PRD takes from `company/`, and what it does not.**
- Names, structure and vocabulary, as design input (`company/README.md`, "How the app may use this").
- The brand, as the app's identity: Decided (OD-1, 2026-09-24: "treat the app as our brand tool"). See section 5.
- No figure. Savings, paybacks, ROI, prices, statistics, case-study numbers, product specs and service lives are website marketing copy. None becomes an app value, default, range or benchmark (`company/README.md`, "Figures: no."; company-profile 10; rule 1, 2.1, section 10; G1-12).
- No client, project, person or testimonial name (company-profile 10; `company/README.md`, "People and clients").
- No SAUTER product name except from an approved, versioned catalogue. `company/products/` is a candidate starting point for one, not the dataset (rule 1; G1-3, G1-12; `docs/build-readiness.md` 4).
- No website copy in app copy, because it uses reserved terms (2.8; company-profile 10; services 9).
- Nothing from the unmerged `redesign-2026` branch: Decided (OD-6, 2026-09-24; asked whether the branch is the company's current position and will be merged, the owner answered "no").

### 2.2 The problem for owners

Owners are "often hotel or office owners who are not engineers". They upload "what they have: architectural and MEP drawings, equipment schedules, specifications, existing BMS point lists, energy bills and certificates". "Most documents are Romanian. Manufacturer tables inside them are often English." (`prompts/sovitech-ai-system.md`, opening.)

A conventional intake questionnaire fails them in four ways. The guardrails name each one in a rule's reason:

| Failure | Why it matters | Source |
|---|---|---|
| It asks for what the documents already say | "Asking for something the owner already uploaded tells them the app did not read their documents." | rule 5, "Why" |
| It stops the owner when data is missing | "An owner who is stuck leaves." | rule 7, "Why" |
| It asks the owner to judge technical facts | "Engineers can use its output only if a non-engineer's click has not quietly turned guesses into facts." | rule 3, "Why" |
| It shows figures without their basis | "An owner has to see how a figure was built before they can trust it." | rule 9, "Why" |

Owners also "share drawings and bills in confidence, and a leak between clients would end that trust" (rule 13, "Why").

The app's answer is the two promises and the Speed Rule, under which "the owner is the last resort" (guardrails sections 1 and 4; section 5 of this PRD).

### 2.3 The problem for SOVITECH engineers and for SOVITECH

- **Checking must be fast.** Engineers "rely on being able to check every value you produce against its source in seconds" (`prompts/sovitech-ai-system.md`, opening).
- **One invented number spoils the rest.** It "can mis-size a system or a budget, and it undermines every other number next to it" (rule 1, "Why").
- **Units and bases are where estimates go wrong.** "In BMS estimates, unit and basis mistakes are the most common errors and the most expensive: power against energy, footprint against total area, a misread locale." (rule 8, "Why").
- **Design documents are not the installed building.** Design-stage documents "describe what was designed, not what is installed". For existing buildings and BMS modernizations, installed-equipment facts stay provisional until an as-built document, a nameplate photo or a site survey supports them (2.3).
- **The same equipment appears many times.** A unit shows on the plan, the schematic, the schedule and the point list. Counting appearances would multiply it, so equipment is stored as assets, one per tag (2.5; section 9, row "4: keep both").
- **A figure that reads as a price is a commitment.** "A preliminary figure that reads as a price creates a commitment SOVITECH never made." (rule 10, "Why").
- **Life-safety and compliance wording is not marketing.** "These are legal and safety claims, not marketing copy." (rule 11, "Why").
- **The approved screens mix two products.** The dashboards mockups show invented live operations content next to proposal content, and "A design-phase project cannot have live data" (`design/dashboards-spec.md` 1.1). They also show a real hotel's name, which the demo does not use (OD-5).

### 2.4 Romanian specifics that shape the product

Owner documents follow Romanian conventions. Rule 8 and 2.3 turn them into data rules. `docs/build-readiness.md` 2 plans a `ro-building-docs` skill covering the same conventions (area bases, the regim de înălțime grammar, number formats, document stages and title-block fields, diacritics). Every entry in it stays draft until a SOVITECH engineer reviews it, and a skill is never a runtime source of values (build-readiness 2, "Principles").

| Topic | What the app has to handle | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Language | Most documents are Romanian, with English-locale manufacturer tables inside them. Locale is detected per table or per value, not per document. Excerpts stay verbatim in their original language, never translated. The interface language is English; adding Romanian is open (D-26). | rule 8 "Parsing"; 2.4 `Evidence`; `prompts/sovitech-ai-system.md`, opening |
| Number formats | Romanian writes 34.500 for thirty-four thousand five hundred and 1,5 for one and a half. An ambiguous reading such as "1.500" keeps both alternatives at low confidence. "cca.", "aprox.", "~", "circa" and "peste" are stored as approximate and shown as "about". "mp" means m². How the app reads numbers the owner types is open (D-26). | rule 8 "Parsing"; G8-2, G8-3; `prompts/sovitech-ai-system.md`, "Units and numbers" |
| Area bases | Sc/Ac (footprint), Scd/Acd/Ad (gross total), Su/Au (usable), arie utilă încălzită (heated usable), conditioned. Each area records whether it includes below-ground areas and parking. The ratio between bases "varies by building and is never assumed". A value with no stated basis is stored with basis `unknown`. The `ro-building-docs` caveat that urban-planning Scd can leave out parking and technical basements is a draft entry, and build-readiness 6 lists "the Legea 350/2001 Scd exclusions" as "Still unverified". | rule 8 "Qualifiers that must be stated"; G8-1, G8-2, G4-7, G8-11; build-readiness 2 and 6 |
| Floors | The regim de înălțime, from the memoriu or the title block, is the first source, for example "3S+P+Mz+12E+Er". Floors are stored as counts by level type: subsol, demisol, parter, mezanin, etaje, etaj retras or tehnic, mansardă, roof plant. Sheet counts never establish floor counts, and numbering follows the document ("Etaj 1" is the first floor above parter). The demo's floor structure is open (D-18), as is the mockups' floors notation (D-18). | rule 8 "Floors"; G8-9 |
| Document stages and revisions | SF or DALI (feasibility), DTAC (permit), PT (technical design), tender, DDE (execution), shop drawing, as-built or carte tehnică, releveu (site survey). The revision is read as written in the title block (cartuș). Stage matters more than date, and revisions are declared, never guessed. The order used to propose an active candidate between stages waits for the approver (D-53). | 2.3; rule 4; G2-6, G3-5 |
| Abbreviations | Expanded only from the glossary in reference data: CTA/UTA (AHU), VCV (fan coil), CT (boiler room), TA/TAC (automation panel), TG/TGD/TGBT (distribution boards), desfumare (smoke extraction), clapetă antifoc (fire damper). Ambiguous ones name their alternative: PT is proiect tehnic or punct termic; DALI is documentație de avizare or the lighting protocol. The glossary entries still need engineer review ("Still unverified", build-readiness 6). | rule 8 "Abbreviations"; G3-5, G3-8 |
| Energy bills | Each value records its carrier, its metering point as printed (POD, CLC or meter id), its period and its reading type ("index citit", "index estimat", "factură de regularizare", storno). Annual totals are calculated from non-overlapping periods. Corrections replace the periods they correct. A sub-meter is never added to its parent. Gas becomes energy only through the calorific value printed on the bill. | rule 8 "Energy data"; G8-7, G8-8 |
| Currency | EUR and RON. Prices state their VAT basis, price date and price-list version. EUR to RON conversion is a calculation with the BNR reference rate for a stated date, from reference data. The slice-1 display currency is open (D-27). | rule 8 "Currency"; G10-4; build-readiness 4 |
| Location | A country code and a city id, with country first or one place search. SIRUTA would supply Romanian city ids; its licence is "Still unverified" (D-94). | guardrails section 5 row §5-1b (step 1, city before country); build-readiness 4 and 6 |
| Diacritics | Documents use both ş/ș and ţ/ț. The excerpt check normalises diacritics, and the reserved-term check ignores them. | build-readiness 2; rule 1 "Enforced by"; 2.8 |
| Law and standards | A BAC efficiency class (EN ISO 52120-1), the energy certificate class (Mc001) and a legal obligation (the EPBD, Legea 372/2005) are three separate fields. "Whether an obligation applies stays Unknown until the facts behind it are engineer-verified." Standards and thresholds come only from reference data with their edition or date. Which edition of EN ISO 52120-1 to cite is open (D-31). Build-readiness 6 lists the text of Legea 238/2024 and the thresholds of Legea 372/2005 as "Still unverified"; they stay unverified in this PRD. | rule 11 "Compliance"; G11-5, G11-6; build-readiness 5 and 6 |
| Fire safety | The BMS only monitors, displays, logs and alarms on life-safety systems. "Any other arrangement must come from the building's fire-safety scenario ('scenariul de securitate la incendiu') and fire-safety design, approved by ISU, and be confirmed by a SOVITECH engineer. An engineer alone is not enough." | rule 11 "Life-safety systems" |

### 2.5 Why IFC, and its limits

**The direction.** Decided (OD-8, 2026-09-24): the interactive app is to be built "based on data from the onboarding flow, based on IFC files from BIM softwares". IFC models exported from BIM tools (Revit, Archicad, Tekla, Allplan and others) become a primary structured input, next to the onboarding answers and the other documents. The direction approves no guardrail proposal, and it does not by itself revise build-readiness decision 4 (`docs/ifc-input.md`, opening and 6.3; `docs/product/traceability.md` 1.6).

**What a model carries that a PDF does not** (`docs/ifc-input.md` 1.1). Levels (`IfcBuildingStorey`), spaces (`IfcSpace`) with quantity sets, zones, systems, typed equipment, a `GlobalId` and a `Tag` per object, property sets with typed values, declared units, geometry and explicit relationships. The research expects three effects: more values could become `document` values with a machine-checkable locator; area, levels, rooms, systems and equipment could be found without asking the owner; and reading is deterministic code, so less owner content reaches the AI processor (ifc-input 1.1, "What this does to the two promises"). These are research expectations, not requirements.

**Its limits** (ifc-input 1.2). IFC is only as good as the export:
- Export quality depends on the authoring tool and its settings. Equipment can arrive as a proxy with no declared meaning, the engineering tag may sit in `Tag`, in `Name`, in a property or nowhere, and area quantities depend on the exporter.
- A model does not reliably say which design stage it represents, so 2.3 applies unchanged: the stage is declared.
- Spaces may be missing on some storeys, or duplicated between architectural and MEP models.
- An architectural model usually carries little or no MEP. A model without a chiller says nothing about whether the building has one (rule 12).
- Schema versions differ, and some exporters write ratings as untyped text or as numbers with no unit.
- Georeferencing is optional, so orientation is often unknown.
- Step 2 accepts up to 500 MB; whether that applies per file or in total is open (D-22). Server memory for a large file is to be measured in a spike, not assumed (ifc-input 1.2 item 9; `design/onboarding-spec.md` 4).
- `GlobalId` is stable only most of the time, so it is never the only identity.
- All text in a model is untrusted data (rule 14).

**What exports usually lack** (ifc-input 3.5). Controllers, sensors and actuators, point lists, protocols, configurations such as duty and standby, reliable area bases, georeferencing and stage. In the research's words, IFC "mostly settles where things are and how many there are, sometimes what they are, rarely their ratings, and almost never how they are controlled". Points stay Estimated from SOVITECH's templates until a point list exists (G9-4), and IFC does not shorten the critical path: points and costs still need SOVITECH's datasets (ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3; D-92).

**Where v1.5 leaves IFC today.**
- No value read from a model passes rule 1's locator check, because the 2.4 locator has no IFC fields (ifc-input 6.1, "Evidence").
- A model is stored with its `DocumentRecord` and the 2.8 status line for a file stored but not analysed, naming its format as G12-1 names RVT. Showing a stored model as a document does not make it analysed, and no "not found" statement counts it as searched (rule 12; G12-4).
- Storing model values needs the approver to be named (D-05) and to approve proposals ifc-input 6.2.1 (D-38), 6.2.2 (D-39), 6.2.3 (D-40) and 6.2.10 (D-37), with approved mapping tables (D-05; the tables need SOVITECH's asset taxonomy, D-92), and the owner's revision of build-readiness decision 4 (D-01).
- Whether IFC enters slice 1, and in which form, is open (D-04).
- RVT is not parsed: it is stored with "Not analysed: RVT model stored, not analysed" (G12-1). The route for RVT is open (D-01).
- What the model views show when no IFC model is stored is open (D-03).

## 3. Users, personas and jobs

The five personas are the contract's (`docs/dev-prompts/02-prd.md`, "Shared contract"; `docs/product/user-stories.md`, "Personas"). People are named only by role. Screen keys are prompt 1's (`docs/product/traceability.md` 1.1 to 1.3). Who uses the dashboards is open (3.8).

| Persona | Who | Phase | Main screens |
|---|---|---|---|
| Owner | The building owner or manager, not an engineer | Proposal | OB-1 to OB-8; proposal content of DB-01 to DB-13 and DB-15 to DB-22 |
| SOVITECH engineer | Verifies technical facts. The only role that can write `engineer_verified` (rule 10; G10-3) | Proposal | UD-15, UD-48, UD-49, UD-44, UD-40, UD-38 |
| SOVITECH commercial reviewer | Co-signs the quotation record behind a "Formal quotation" (rule 10) | Proposal | UD-38, UD-15, UD-06, DB-18 |
| SOVITECH admin | Accounts, roles, projects, datasets and processors, as prompt 1's stories give them | Proposal | UD-39, UD-40, UD-41, UD-37 |
| Facility manager | Operations only | Operations, later (D-28) | DB-14 and the live (L) parts of other screens |

### 3.1 Owner

**Jobs to be done.**

| Job | Stories | Screens |
|---|---|---|
| Start a project with the four required fields: project name, project type, city and country | US-INTAKE-02, US-INTAKE-03 | OB-1 |
| Hand over what they have, including IFC models, and see each file's status and coverage | US-DOCS-01, US-DOCS-03, US-DOCS-12, US-IFC-01, US-IFC-02 | OB-2, UD-33, DB-15, UD-21 |
| See what the app found, with its source, and correct what is wrong | US-REVIEW-04, US-REVIEW-07, US-REVIEW-08 | OB-3, UD-34, UD-45 |
| Confirm the few facts only they know, and judge conflicts on their own fields | US-REVIEW-05, US-REVIEW-11 | OB-3 to OB-8 |
| Decide what the BMS covers: systems in scope, operations, goals and automation areas | US-SCOPE-02, US-INTAKE-08, US-INTAKE-09, US-INTAKE-10, US-INTAKE-11 | OB-4 to OB-7 |
| Review, then generate a preliminary proposal without being blocked | US-INTAKE-15, US-INTAKE-17, US-INTAKE-18, US-PROPOSAL-01, US-PROPOSAL-02, US-PROPOSAL-04 | OB-8, UD-35, UD-07, UD-47, UD-06 |
| Explore and export the proposal after Generate: scope, zones, equipment, topology, the model view, the Metrics pages, reports | E-SCOPE, E-ZONES, E-ASSETS, E-TOPO, E-MODEL, E-FIN, E-PROPOSAL, E-REPORTS | UD-01, proposal content of DB-01 to DB-13 and DB-15 to DB-22 |
| Keep documents under control: declare a revision, delete a document and see what it changes | US-DOCS-20, US-DOCS-21 | DB-15, UD-22, UD-42, UD-43 |
| Sign in and move between their projects | US-ADMIN-01, US-ADMIN-05, US-ADMIN-06 | UD-36, UD-37, UD-32, UD-16 |

**What the owner may do** (rules 3 and 4; 2.1; details in 3.7):
- enter values and make choices, which become `user` candidates;
- confirm a value that rule 5 puts to them, on a field whose `confirmBy` is `owner` or `either` (`user_confirmed`), within the confirmation budget (D-53);
- accept a visible Suggested choice by pressing Continue (G3-4);
- acknowledge an engineer field with "Looks right", which records `owner_acknowledged` and "never counts as verification" (2.1; G3-3), or send "Something's wrong" to the engineer queue (rule 3);
- correct a value shown with its source, which rejects the shown candidate (G4-5), except an `engineer_verified` value, which goes into conflict for the engineer (G4-19);
- resolve conflicts on owner fields (rule 4);
- declare that a document revises another (2.3), and delete a document, which runs the erasure job (rule 13; G13-3).

The owner never writes `engineer_verified` (G10-3), signs nothing and approves nothing.

**What the app never asks the owner.**
- Technical facts, and `for_quotation` facts that no document can settle in an existing building: installed equipment, the condition and reusability of field devices and wiring, existing controller models, panel space and network topology. These are listed under **SOVITECH will check** as "Site survey needed" (guardrails section 4, item 9).
- Technical questions an owner is unlikely to know, such as the protocol of an existing BMS. They go to the engineer queue (rule 6).
- To confirm an engineer field: equipment types and ratings, protocols, point lists, control strategies (rule 3). There is no owner "Confirm all" on equipment (guardrails section 5 row §5-3b (step 3, "HVAC assets ...")).
- To arbitrate a conflict on an engineer field. The owner reads "Documents disagree on this. A SOVITECH engineer will check it." (rule 4; G4-8).
- A question about anything already in the project data, the documents or reference data. At most, rule 5 shows a confirmation, and only when its three-part test passes. Nothing already asked is asked again, apart from rule 5's two exceptions (rule 5; GS-1).
- A question whose answer changes no output (rule 6; G6-1), or a question the AI wrote (rule 6; G6-3).

### 3.2 SOVITECH engineer

**Jobs to be done.**

| Job | Stories | Screens |
|---|---|---|
| Work one review queue per project: every item only SOVITECH can settle, each opening with its evidence | US-ENGINEER-01, US-ENGINEER-02 | UD-15, UD-48 |
| Verify, or reject with a reason, technical facts after opening the item; see owner acknowledgements as acknowledgements. What one "item" is: D-55 | US-ENGINEER-03, US-ENGINEER-04 | UD-48, DB-17 |
| Resolve the conflicts routed to them | US-ENGINEER-05 | UD-48, DB-10, DB-17 |
| Settle possible duplicates and asset identity: merge, split, remove | US-ENGINEER-06, US-ASSETS-01 | UD-48, DB-05, DB-17 |
| Record site surveys as documents of stage `site_survey`. Desk corrections without a site visit have no defined source yet (D-55) | US-ENGINEER-07, US-ENGINEER-09 | UD-49 |
| Read rule 14 findings, and each model's schema, authoring tool and schema errors, none of it shown to the owner | US-ENGINEER-08, US-IFC-03, US-IFC-04 | UD-44, UD-48 |
| Review SOVITECH datasets and IFC mapping tables for the approver: a review, never an approval. How review and approval records reach the app: D-47 | US-ENGINEER-12, US-ENGINEER-13 | UD-40 |
| Be the reviewing engineer named in a quotation record | US-ENGINEER-15 | UD-38 |

Jobs whose content waits on proposals that are not approved: the tag source of a model (ifc-input 6.2.4; D-41; US-ENGINEER-10), clearing a life-safety flag (proposal 7.2.23, D-52; ifc-input 6.2.12, D-56; US-ENGINEER-11), SOVITECH's proposed design on topology and reports (proposal 7.2.10, D-65; US-TOPO-04, US-REPORTS-10), zone kinds and origin (proposal 7.2.28, D-68; US-ZONES-08), life-safety as an engineer field (proposal 7.2.23, D-52; US-ASSETS-14), and the engineer's side of the model reads in E-IFC (ifc-input 6.2.1, D-38, and the proposals each story names).

**What the engineer may do** (details in 3.7):
- write `engineer_verified`, only as an authenticated user with the `sovitech_engineer` role, only through the engineer review endpoint, only on an item they have opened, and never on demo values (rule 10; G10-3, G3-7);
- resolve conflicts on engineer fields, and any conflict in which a candidate is `engineer_verified` (rule 4; G4-8, G4-14, G4-18);
- reject a candidate with a reason (rule 4), and merge, split or remove assets (2.5);
- record site survey entries, which are `user` candidates citing the survey document (2.1; guardrails section 4, item 9);
- declare that a document revises another (2.3);
- co-sign a quotation record as the reviewing engineer (rule 10);
- take part in a life-safety arrangement beyond monitor, display, log and alarm only as rule 11 allows: it must come from the fire-safety documents approved by ISU, and "An engineer alone is not enough" (rule 11).

**What the app never asks the engineer.**
- To decide the owner's choices: systems in scope, goals, automation areas, and occupancy or schedule where no document states them (rule 3, "Choices belong to the owner"). Conflicts on owner fields go to the owner (rule 4).
- To verify an item they have not opened, including rows ticked in bulk (rule 10; `design/dashboards-spec.md` 7.1.1 row 7.1.1-C10 ("17's bulk checkboxes")).
- To verify demo values (rule 10).
- To approve a dataset, a mapping table or a guardrail change (section 10). That is the approver's (3.6).

### 3.3 SOVITECH commercial reviewer

**Jobs to be done.**

| Job | Stories | Screens |
|---|---|---|
| Keep every investment figure on the stage its stored records give it, so nothing reads as a price before review | US-ENGINEER-14 | OB-8, DB-02, DB-13, UD-06 |
| Co-sign a quotation record with the reviewing engineer, once no `for_quotation` input is Unknown or lacks `engineer_verified` | US-ENGINEER-15 | UD-38, UD-15, DB-18 |
| See a quotation record read "Superseded: inputs changed on <date>" as soon as an input changes | US-ENGINEER-16 | UD-38, UD-06, DB-15 |

Open around this role: where the quotation record is created and co-signed (D-20); whether the two signers must be different people, and whether one account may hold two roles (D-20); what a quotation record shows after its validity period (D-20).

**What the commercial reviewer may do.** Co-sign the quotation record. Rule 10 lists what it holds: "the quotation number"; "the reviewing engineer's and the commercial reviewer's user ids"; "the date and the validity period"; "the currency and the VAT basis"; "inclusions and exclusions"; "a hash of every input candidate". Only this record makes a "Formal quotation" (rule 10, "Stage 3 is derived, not passed"; G10-1). The commercial reviewer never writes `engineer_verified` (rule 10; US-ADMIN-03 AC5).

**What the app never asks the commercial reviewer.** To check technical facts (rule 3), to co-sign while a `for_quotation` input is missing its engineer's check (rule 7: "Only the formal quotation waits. It needs these values verified by an engineer."), or to issue anything on a demo project (rule 10).

### 3.5 Facility manager

Operations phase only. Every facility manager story is "Out of scope: operations phase" (US-OPS-01 to US-OPS-11, US-OPS-14). The jobs they describe are: see whether the BMS is live and when it last synced, live zone and equipment readings, maintenance records, alarms and alarm rules, and measured costs and achieved savings. The screens are DB-14, UD-14, UD-18, UD-30 and the live (L) parts of other dashboard screens. Whether an operations phase comes later is open (D-28), and the facility manager's account also waits for D-16 (US-OPS-14). In the proposal phase the facility manager has no role (US-ADMIN-03, Notes), and confirms, acknowledges, verifies and signs nothing.

### 3.6 Not a persona: the approver

The approver is "the product owner: the person directing this project", named in the table in guardrails section 10. Nobody is named yet (D-05). Approval means "that person's own words in the conversation, about that specific change" (section 10). It is never an app action, an admin power, a service account or a seed (section 10; G1-12; US-ADMIN-03 AC4). How approval records reach the app is open (D-47).

The approver alone approves:
- reference datasets and their versions (rule 1; section 10; G1-12);
- IFC mapping tables, which proposal ifc-input 6.2.10 would make approved datasets (not approved; D-37);
- every guardrail change that tightens or loosens a rule, including a new question, gate or confirmation (section 10). Rule 4 says "Tolerance changes need approval" and "Widening a tolerance is a loosening (section 10)";
- the four values v1.5 leaves to the approver (D-53): the confirmation budget ("The approver sets N", rule 5), the correction threshold ("the threshold set by the approver", rule 3), the first-estimate set ("The approver confirms the set", rule 7) and the document-stage order ("The approver confirms this order", rule 4).

The guardrails do not say who sets a field's tolerance or plausible range in the registry (2.6). Rule 8 ("Area rules") says only that "Converting between bases needs an engineer-approved factor". Who supplies these values is open: section 15 asks it in the SOVITECH engineering row, with the other reference data (D-93).

### 3.8 Who uses the dashboards

Open (D-16). The mockups show named people uploading documents and generating reports on 15 and 18, and a user avatar on 13 and 14. The question is whether part 2 is for the owner only, or also for SOVITECH engineers, which "decides roles, permissions, and whether the engineer review queue lives in this app" (`design/dashboards-spec.md` 8.15).

Until it is decided, prompt 1's stories write the dashboard pages for the owner, keep engineer work on undesigned pages (UD-15, UD-44, UD-48, UD-49), and route engineer items without building an engineer page where the story is blocked: items "are stored with their kind and project and feed the owner's group lines, and no engineer page is built by this story" (US-ENGINEER-02 AC7). A report's "Generated By" names who started the generation and never implies review (`design/dashboards-spec.md` 7.1.1 row 7.1.1-D8 ("18's 'Generated By'")).

### 4.3 Success metrics

**How metrics are used.** "Metrics prompt a review, never an edit. A metric moving the wrong way opens a review. It never by itself justifies widening a tolerance, allowing estimation or raising a budget." (guardrails section 10). No metric below feeds a value, a threshold or a registry setting. On 2026-09-24 no guardrail check is running: `tests/guardrails/` and `evals/guardrails/` do not exist.

**Speed read next to truth.** Guardrails section 4, "Measure it": "Each speed metric is read next to a truth metric." Admins see the pairs on the guardrail events page (US-ADMIN-21 AC2; F-AUDIT-02; UD-41).

| Speed metric | Read next to (truth metric) | Counted from | Target | Label |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Questions per project | The owner correction rate on inferences | Owner questions shown; `owner_corrected_inference` events, with their confidence tier | Target not set (D-22) | Required (guardrails section 4) |
| Confirmations per project | How often engineers later correct accepted items | Owner confirmations shown, which never exceed the budget the approver sets (rule 5 proposes 7; D-53); `engineer_corrected_accepted_item` events | Target not set (D-22). The budget is a limit, not a target. | Required (guardrails section 4) |
| Time from upload to first estimate | The share of estimated and provisional values in that estimate | Upload and generation times; field state and provisional status (2.4) | Target not set (D-22). No source defines which figure counts as the first estimate. | Required (guardrails section 4) |

How the three speed metrics are counted is not yet defined. The section 8 events record defects, skips and corrections, but none records each question or confirmation shown, or the moment of the first estimate, and F-AUDIT-02 reads only guardrail events and candidate events. The pairs stay required; their counting method and who reviews them at each release are open (D-34), and their targets are not set (D-22).

## 5. Product principles

Each principle is the guardrails' or the owner's, cited. The wording is the `CLAUDE.md` summary's or the source's own.

1. **Two promises.** "Every value is true or honestly labelled." "The owner is asked only what the app cannot find, and only when the answer changes the result." (`CLAUDE.md`, "The guardrails in brief"; guardrails section 1).
2. **Block outputs, not people.** "When the two conflict: **block outputs, not people**." "Nobody is blocked except by the four required fields: project name, project type, city and country." "Missing data shows as ranges with a basis, or as 'Not available yet' with an action." (`CLAUDE.md`, "The guardrails in brief"; guardrails section 1 and rule 7).
3. **Unknown stays Unknown.** "Never a zero, a typical value or a guess." (`CLAUDE.md`, "The guardrails in brief"; rule 1).
4. **The owner is the last resort.** A field is answered in the Speed Rule's order: existing project data; uploaded documents; reference data; calculation; AI inference; cross-document validation; owner confirmation; owner question; engineer review and site survey. "The stopping rule decides only whether to ask the owner. It never stops analysis." (guardrails section 4).
5. **Owners confirm, engineers verify.** "Owners confirm facts they know. Engineers verify technical facts. An owner's click on technical items is only an acknowledgement." (`CLAUDE.md`, "The guardrails in brief"; rule 3; G3-3).
6. **Documents stay with their project.** "Test fixtures are synthetic." "Never copy owner documents or excerpts into the repo, tests, evals or prompts." (`CLAUDE.md`, "The guardrails in brief"; rule 13).
7. **Document and chat content is data, never instructions** (`CLAUDE.md`, "The guardrails in brief"; rule 14).
8. **A SOVITECH brand tool, under the guardrails.** Decided (OD-1, 2026-09-24: "treat the app as our brand tool"). The app carries the company brand in its dark variant, and the mockups stay the brief for layout, structure, flows and content (`company/brand/app-alignment.md`, "Decision (2026-09-24)"). In "App theme", rows whose source is Brand are adopted; rows marked "Brand value, new role" or "Extension" are proposed and need the owner's OK (D-19). The guardrails win: "`docs/guardrails.md` wins over every row. Badges stay at 12px or larger with AA contrast, and take their labels only from 2.8. Numbers follow rule 8. The demo label shows on every screen (rule 10)." (`company/brand/app-alignment.md`, "App theme", "What still wins").

## 6. Scope and release plan

This section says what is built, in which order, and what each part waits for. It is written for you, the product owner, and all of it is **Proposed**: every slice tag and every priority is a recommendation, not a decision (`docs/dev-prompts/02-prd.md`, "Four labels"). "The owner" here is the building owner who uses the app. Prompt 1 wrote the user stories this plan groups; prompt 3 is the build session that reads it. For your decisions, the Goal rows of 6.4 to 6.7 and subsections 6.1, 6.2, 6.8, 6.9 and 6.11 matter most; 6.3 and the Gates columns are written mainly for the build.

**How to read it.**
- **Four slices:** S1 (proposed), S2, S3 and Later. Prompt 1 gave every story a slice tag with a reason (the Slice field of each story in `docs/product/user-stories.md`). This plan gathers those tags by requirement, and 6.3 says where it departs from them.
- **Priorities** (proposed): **Must** means the preliminary proposal cannot be delivered honestly without it; **Should**, important, with a workaround; **Could**, valuable and deferrable (`docs/dev-prompts/02-prd.md`, "How the PRD applies the contract"). Whenever a requirement ships, its guardrail behaviour ships with it.
- **The first slice stays proposed** until you decide build-readiness decision 3, its scope (D-04). That is why it is always written S1 (proposed) (`docs/dev-prompts/03-build-interactive-app.md` section 4).
- **Slices set the build order, not a release.** Prompt 3 builds every slice except Later, in order: within each of its build phases, S1 (proposed) first, then S2, then S3. It never calls anything released or "slice 1 done", and it does not build Later. If you limit the build to S1 (proposed), it stops there and lists the rest as not built (`docs/dev-prompts/03-build-interactive-app.md` section 4). Because prompt 3 orders its work by phase first, the S1 (proposed) goal, a stored preliminary proposal, is reached only in its phase 5, after phase 4 has built the S2 and S3 workspace pages (its section 10). To review S1 (proposed) as a checkpoint before any later work, limit the first run to it.
- **A gate does not move a requirement out of its slice.** A gated requirement is built in its slice with only its "Until decided" behaviour (section 7) until the decision, approval or dataset on its "Gated by" line lands. A gate is a decision, approval or dataset that must land first. It is written "Blocked by open question <source id> (D-NN)" or "Depends on proposal <proposal> (not approved; D-NN)", where D-NN is its row in section 15.
- **Every requirement appears in exactly one slice table** (6.4 to 6.7): 48 in S1 (proposed), 50 in S2, 48 in S3 and 21 in Later, 167 in all. This was checked by script against the Slice line of every requirement in sections 7 and 11.
- The operations phase is in no slice (6.8). The quotation record is in 6.9. Stories that have no requirement of their own are in 6.10, and what the plan means for the first real owner document is in 6.11.

### 6.1 Where the plan comes from, and where the sources disagree

The PRD follows prompt 1's slice tags, except where 6.3 says otherwise. `docs/build-readiness.md` describes the first slice differently. Its "Method" line and section 3 describe it as "part 1 intake, extraction, the value model, and a proposal estimate made of points and a CAPEX range" (section 3 "Now" item 8; section 5 decision 3). Prompt 1 tags the points and CAPEX figures S2, because they need SOVITECH's datasets and an approver to approve them (build-readiness decisions 6 and 1; new Q32; `docs/product/traceability.md` 10.2 conflict 4).

| Item | `docs/build-readiness.md`, first slice | Prompt 1's tag, and where the PRD puts it | What the PRD follows, and why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Points by type from SOVITECH's point templates | In the first slice (3 "Now" item 8; decision 3) | Structure and missing case: S1 (proposed), R-112 (US-PROPOSAL-06). The estimate: S2, R-114 (US-PROPOSAL-07) | Prompt 1. A dataset feeds a value only with an approval record (guardrails 2.1, section 10; G1-12), and no approval record can exist before the approver is named (build-readiness decision 1; D-05). How approval records then reach the app is a separate question for the approver (new Q32; D-47). The templates themselves are D-92. |
| CAPEX range at stage 1 or 2 | In the first slice (3 "Now" item 8; decision 3) | Stage labels, price component and missing cases: S1 (proposed), R-112 and R-127 (US-PROPOSAL-08, US-ENGINEER-14). The range: S2, R-114 (US-PROPOSAL-09) | Prompt 1, for the same reason: SOVITECH's cost ranges need an approval record (D-92, D-05, D-47). R-114 covers stage 2 ("Preliminary investment estimate") only. Stage 1 ("Indicative range") is "Benchmarks only" (rule 10) and needs an approved benchmark dataset, which the dataset request in build-readiness 4 does not name (benchmarks appear only in the question of D-93); a benchmark per m² would also need a currency-ratio unit (proposal 7.2.22, D-44). Until one exists, a missing first-estimate field gives "Not available yet" (R-112) in every slice. |
| Asset types, and step 3's equipment count by type | In the first slice (3 "Now" items 3 and 8) | The register and its Calculated counts: S1 (proposed), R-065. Types from the SOVITECH taxonomy: S2, R-067 (US-ASSETS-02) | Prompt 1: the taxonomy is a dataset with the same approval need (D-92, D-05). Until then each type reads Unknown under SOVITECH will check (R-067, "Until decided"). |
| Operating cost, payback, NPV and IRR read "Not available yet" | In the first slice (3 "Now" item 8) | S1 (proposed), R-087 and R-111 | Both agree. |
| Step 3 as a value list with Edit and no 3D | In the first slice (3 "Now" item 10) | S1 (proposed), R-045. The model view: S2, R-078 | Both agree. |
| IFC, RVT and other unread formats stored as "Not analysed" | In the first slice (3 "Now" item 5) | S1 (proposed), R-014 and R-022 | Both agree. |

**Why this stays proposed.** The build-readiness description predates your IFC direction of 2026-09-24, and it is itself a proposal: decision 3 is open (D-04). The PRD's S1 (proposed) is not a decision either. If SOVITECH's point templates, cost ranges and asset taxonomy arrive with approval records in time, you may move R-114 into S1 (proposed) (US-PROPOSAL-07 and US-PROPOSAL-09, Slice), together with R-067: points are estimated per asset type and configuration (build-readiness 4; guardrails 2.5), and asset types come only from the approved taxonomy (R-067), so R-114 alone would have no typed asset to estimate. One effect to know when you decide: S1 (proposed) computes no points, investment or operating-cost figure, so the answers on steps 5 to 7 change no figure the owner sees in it; occupancy and schedule mainly change operating cost (traceability 10.2 conflict 3; G7-1). Rule 6 keeps a question only when its answer changes a declared output (its sensitivity test), so a strict reading could drop some of those questions (R-002). Prompt 3 runs that test with test datasets and formulas instead, keeps the approved questions, and logs the cost to Speed for the approver (`docs/dev-prompts/03-build-interactive-app.md` section 10, phase 1).

**Datasets and approval.** Every requirement gated by SOVITECH's datasets (D-92) also waits for the approver (D-05) and for the route by which approval records reach the app (D-47), even where its Gated by line names only the datasets: under G1-12 a dataset with no approval record feeds no value.

### 6.2 IFC across the slices

**The direction.** Decided (OD-8, 2026-09-24): the app is built "based on data from the onboarding flow, based on IFC files from BIM softwares". IFC models become a primary input next to the onboarding answers and the other documents. The direction approves no guardrail proposal, and revising build-readiness decision 4 is still your call (`docs/ifc-input.md` 6.3; D-01).

**When IFC enters the build: three options** (`docs/ifc-input.md` 6.3.1 item 1). ifc-input recommends none of them. The choice is yours, under build-readiness decisions 3 and 4 (D-04, D-01).

| Option | What S1 (proposed) would add | Requirements that would move into S1 (proposed) | What still waits, whichever you choose |
|---|---|---|---|
| "IFC data in slice 1", without geometry or a viewer | ifc-input 6.3.1 item 1 defines it as IFC data (spatial tree, spaces, quantity sets, assets, systems) in slice 1. Under guardrails v1.5 none of that can be stored, so what S1 (proposed) would add live is code reading each stored model on the server for the engineer: its header, its schema errors, and its text checked under rule 14. That record shows only on the engineer's per-document view (UD-44), which exists only where the engineer queue lives (dashboards 8.15, D-16), so nobody sees it until that is decided. The value path is written behind closed gates in any case (below). | R-023, R-024 (US-IFC-03, US-IFC-04, Slice) | Every value read from a model (below). Under guardrails v1.5 the owner would still see no value from a model. |
| "IFC data and the viewer in slice 1" | The above, plus conversion and the stored model shown as a document | R-023, R-024, R-025, R-078, R-079 (US-IFC-03, US-IFC-04, US-IFC-08, US-MODEL-04 to US-MODEL-06, Slice), and with them R-080 and R-162, whose criteria hold from the first page that draws a model view. R-025, R-078 and R-079 stay blocked by onboarding Q3 and dashboards 8.5 (D-03), and R-079 also by dashboards 8.3 (D-02), until those are decided. R-054 moves only with the System Scope page it sits on (R-052, S2; US-SCOPE-12) | The same, plus pins, scale bars and orientation on the views (proposal 7.2.8, D-45; ifc-input 6.2.15, D-46) |
| "IFC after slice 1" | Nothing beyond storing models as "Not analysed" | none | The same |

**What prompt 1's tags imply: "IFC after slice 1".** In S1 (proposed), IFC and RVT files are accepted, stored with their document record and listed as "Not analysed: IFC model stored, not analysed" or "Not analysed: RVT model stored, not analysed" (R-022, R-014). Reading a model for the engineer (R-023, R-024) and the model view (R-025, R-054, R-078, R-079) are S2 at the earliest, because build-readiness's first slice reads only native-text PDF and XLSX (3 "Now" item 5; decision 4, D-01) and has no 3D on step 3 (3 "Now" item 10). Values read from models are S3 (R-027 to R-040, R-131, R-132) and Later (R-041, R-042 and the model joins in 6.7). This reading is Proposed (`docs/product/user-stories.md` US-IFC-01, US-IFC-03 and US-IFC-08, Slice).

**Value extraction from IFC waits, in every slice,** for all of these:
- the approver, named in guardrails section 10 (build-readiness decision 1; D-05). Every "Depends on proposal" gate already waits for the approver, so the requirements do not list this gate again;
- Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.1 (not approved; D-38), the IFC evidence locator (how a value points to the place in the model it was read from);
- Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.2 (not approved; D-39), document records for models;
- Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.3 (not approved; D-40), coverage and "not found" for models (what the app records about what a model contains and what it could not read, so that a "not found" statement names each model and never claims more than was read);
- Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.10 (not approved; D-37), mapping tables as approved datasets (the tables that turn model content into the app's fields and types, approved like other datasets);
- the approved mapping tables themselves (ifc-input 6.3.1 items 2 and 3). They need the SOVITECH asset taxonomy with its life-safety flags (Blocked by open question ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3 (D-92)) and an approval record, which only the approver gives (D-05) and whose route into the app is still open (D-47);
- your revision of build-readiness decision 4 (Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 4 (D-01)).

Some values need more: identity across models (ifc-input 6.2.4, D-41), IFC area bases (6.2.6, D-49), quantities computed from shapes (6.2.7, D-50), storey counts (6.2.8, D-43), inferences made by code (6.2.9, D-42), the units IFC files declare (6.2.11, D-63), life-safety signals (6.2.12, D-56) and hidden content (6.2.13, D-59). Pins, scale bars and orientation on views wait for proposal 7.2.8 (D-45) and ifc-input 6.2.15 (D-46). ifc-input 6.3.1 item 2 names the minimum set to take first and what each of the others is needed for, without ordering them (D-05).

**Until then (guardrails v1.5).** A model is stored as a document of its project (its `DocumentRecord`, keyed by project id and content hash, so no other project can reach it) and reads "Not analysed: IFC model stored, not analysed". No value, badge or field state comes from it, and no "Not found in the analysed documents" statement counts it as searched (rule 12; G12-1, G12-4). IFC does not shorten the critical path: points and costs still need SOVITECH's datasets (ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3; D-92).

**Prompt 3 and the gated IFC path.** Prompt 3 also writes the IFC value path in its phase 2, and the view marks in its section 8, behind gates that stay closed until the approvals above land, with their tests outside the guardrail index (`docs/dev-prompts/03-build-interactive-app.md` sections 5.4, 8 and 10). The slice tags here set the order of that gated work. Where it reaches Later requirements (areas and metering points read from a model, R-041 and R-042; pins, scale and orientation marks, R-082), prompt 3's "do not build Later" and its phase 2 and section 8 scope disagree. This is reported for you to settle; this plan does not settle it. Prompt 3's default for the parsing scope (its section 5.2: IFC parsed, values behind the `ifc-values` gate) also differs from the "Until decided" lines of R-023 and R-024 (no model is read). Where the two differ, prompt 3 follows the stricter and logs it (its section 4): no stored model is read live, even for the engineer, until those rows are decided (D-01, and D-04 for R-023), while the gated path is still written and tested on fixtures.

### 6.8 The operations phase: in no slice

Live operations content has its own status, "Out of scope: operations phase". Not building it in the proposal phase is itself required (`design/dashboards-spec.md` 7.1 row 7.1-r27 ("All (L) values"), 7.1.1 rows 7.1.1-E2 ("'BMS LIVE' chip; …") and 7.1.1-D12 ("14, the whole page"); rules 1 and 12). Whether an operations phase comes later is open: it waits for dashboards 8.1 (D-28).

If you decide to have one, it would contain the E-OPS stories, all tagged Later by prompt 1: whether the BMS is live and when it last synced (US-OPS-01); scrubbing the building through time (US-OPS-02); live zone conditions and occupancy (US-OPS-03); live equipment status and readings (US-OPS-04); maintenance records per asset (US-OPS-05); opening the live BMS from the plan (US-OPS-06); the Alarms page, its bulk actions, its rules, and the alarm counts, tabs and OPERATIONS group (US-OPS-07 to US-OPS-10); measured operating costs and achieved savings (US-OPS-11); programme progress on the phasing plan (US-OPS-12); a project phase that gates operations content (US-OPS-13); and the facility manager's account (US-OPS-14).

Beyond dashboards 8.1, those stories also wait for the approver on proposals 7.2.1 (live telemetry, D-76), 7.2.2 (status and alarm vocabulary, D-80), 7.2.3 (time scrubbing, D-81), 7.2.6 (occupancy and personal data, D-60), 7.2.11 (project phase, D-75), 7.2.16 (read-only dashboards, D-79), 7.2.24 (programme progress, D-84), 7.2.32 (time series, D-72) and 7.2.33 (alarms, D-85), and on dashboards 8.9 (D-30) and 8.15 (D-16) (section 7, E-OPS). Prompt 3 builds none of it unless the PRD records your decision on dashboards 8.1 and `docs/guardrails.md` carries the operations proposals (`docs/dev-prompts/03-build-interactive-app.md` section 10, "Not built in any phase").

The absences are built from the first screens: no live element in the shell (R-139), no facility manager role (R-134) and no operations entry in the menu (R-144), all S1 (proposed), and none in the workspace navigation (R-146, S2).

### 6.9 The quotation record

A "Formal quotation" comes only from a stored quotation record naming the reviewing engineer and the commercial reviewer (rule 10, "Stage 3 is derived, not passed"; G10-1). The E-ENGINEER requirements scope it as follows.
- **S1 (proposed):** every investment figure takes its stage only from stored records, as "Indicative range" or "Preliminary investment estimate" (R-127). The event trail keeps whatever a record needs once records exist (R-167). A commercial reviewer co-signs only where issuing a quotation record exists (R-134).
- **S3:** creating the stored quotation record, and its "Superseded: inputs changed on <date>" line when an input changes, are in scope as R-129. The tag is proposed. Blocked by open question new Q35 (D-20) · Blocked by open question dashboards 8.15 (D-16). Where the record is created and co-signed, in this app or in a commercial system it is imported from, is open (new Q35, D-20), as is whether the two signers must be different people (D-20).
- **Until then:** no screen issues a quotation record, and no screen or export shows the "Formal quotation" stage (R-129, "Until decided").

### 6.10 Stories with no requirement of their own

These stories are on no requirement's Stories line. Prompt 3 does not build their content. Where they have a v1.5 behaviour, the requirement named in their epic's "Waiting on approval" list carries it (section 7).
- **Waiting on approval** (prompt 1's tag in brackets): US-DOCS-05 and US-DOCS-19 (S3); US-IFC-05 (S3); US-IFC-06, US-IFC-07 and US-IFC-21 (Later); US-ZONES-08 (Later); US-ASSETS-14 (Later); US-FIN-11, US-FIN-15, US-FIN-28, US-FIN-29 and US-FIN-30 (Later); US-REPORTS-10 and US-REPORTS-12 (Later).
- **Out of scope: operations phase:** US-OPS-01 to US-OPS-14 (Later; 6.8).

### 6.11 Real owner documents

S1 (proposed) holds synthetic data only (R-143). R-159 (S3) lets an environment store a real owner document only once four things hold: the audited erasure job, no document text in any log, every processor recorded in rule 13, and no development login in that environment. Its gates are Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 2 (D-09), the AI processor route · Blocked by open question new Q38 (D-13), the production sign-in · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 1 (D-05), the approver, because a processor is recorded in rule 13 only by an approved edit to the guardrails. The erasure job comes with the Documents page (R-016, S2). Malware scanning of uploads, which `docs/build-readiness.md` 3 "Later" also names before the first real upload, has no source in the guardrails, the approved design or an owner decision, so it is not a condition of R-159. It is Proposed (PRD) in section 11 and waits for your decision on the non-functional baselines (D-35); until it is adopted, the four conditions alone do not make an environment ready for real owner documents (R-159, Sources). The same decision covers how long backups keep a document and how an erasure reaches them, which no source settles. Counsel reviews the GDPR obligations for owner documents before the first real one (D-94). The sign-in that replaces the development login is R-153, tagged S3, which is why R-159 is S3 too. So, as tagged, the first real owner document can arrive only in S3, once R-153 is built. If you want real documents sooner, R-159 and R-153 would move together (reported for your slice decision, D-04).

## 7. Functional requirements

Grouped by epic in the contract order. Each requirement cites prompt 1's stories and functions; its acceptance criteria are prompt 1's, by id. Cross-cutting behaviour stays in the epics where prompt 1 put it: the one value component, display precision and the demo line in E-REVIEW, and the proposal-phase shell in E-ADMIN. Whenever a requirement ships, its "Guardrail behaviour" line ships with it.

### E-INTAKE: Intake wizard

The eight-step wizard as a flow, from project creation to the hand-off to generation (`docs/product/user-stories.md` E-INTAKE). It covers the wizard frame and stepper in the brand's dark variant, step 1's four required fields, what steps 5 to 7 ask and when they do not ask, "Skip for now", the step 8 review with its inline asks and the "Generate Proposal" hand-off, late findings before and after Generate, and the paths that wait for open questions: branching by project type, suggestions, notes, follow-up inputs, a clickable stepper, resume, and the way back to the intake after Generate. Screens: OB-1 to OB-8, UD-35 (step 8 states) and UD-16 (only its "back to intake" entry). Step 2's file handling is E-DOCS, step 3's values and the open-item lists are E-REVIEW, step 4's scope is E-SCOPE, and the generating state and the landing after Generate are E-PROPOSAL.

#### R-004 Late findings never interrupt, before and after Generate

- **Epic:** E-INTAKE · **Stories:** US-INTAKE-19, US-REVIEW-16 · **Functions:** F-INGEST-04, F-VALUE-03, F-QUESTION-07, F-QUESTION-09, F-RENDER-09 · **Screens:** OB-2, OB-3, OB-4, OB-5, OB-6, OB-7, OB-8

You'll see them on the review step.", for findings that arrive together (rule 7); a late value that rule 5 did not flag is labelled and is not an open item (rule 7); candidates and events stay append-only (2.4).

The story's gates, proposal 7.2.27 (D-69) and new Q17 (D-14), apply to the rest of it (AC3 and AC4, the home for open items on UD-01, UD-02 and DB-15), which waits in E-REVIEW "Waiting on approval"; AC2 builds nothing on those screens. Which screen "the review step" is stays new Q17. While the way back to the intake is gated, step 8's list after Generate is reached only through a "Not available yet" action's step 8 inline ask (R-012, US-INTAKE-22 AC6); that is the scenario proposal 7.2.27 describes (US-REVIEW-16 Notes).

- **Until decided:** project type stays one single choice, not split into building status and scope, and steps 2 to 8 show the same questions for every type (US-INTAKE-04 AC1, AC2).
- **Acceptance:** US-INTAKE-04 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4
- **Sources:** `docs/product/user-stories.md` US-INTAKE-04 (Slice: "any question a project type adds is a new owner question, which needs the approver"); `docs/guardrails.md` rule 6, section 10 ("a new question"), section 5 row §5-1c (step 1, project type is single-select); `design/onboarding-spec.md` 3 (Step 1, "Behaviour") and 7 Q5. The build-readiness decision 1 gate is added here from the story's Slice and Open questions fields; its Status does not carry it.

### E-DOCS: Documents

How files reach a project and what the owner sees about each one: upload on step 2 (OB-2) and after the intake (UD-21), the step 2 file list and its states (UD-33), the Documents page (DB-15) with its menus (UD-22), the delete confirmation (UD-42) and the revision declaration (UD-43). It covers each file's `DocumentRecord` (kind, stage, revision as written, supersedes), its analysis status and coverage in guardrails 2.8 wording, native-text PDF and XLSX reading with evidence checked by code, formats stored as "Not analysed", revisions, delete and the erasure job, re-reading, and rules 12 to 14 as the owner sees them (also on OB-3, DB-05 and the engineer queue UD-15). IFC and RVT models are E-IFC. How values render (the value component, badges, confirmations, open items) is E-REVIEW, and the app shell around the Documents page is E-ADMIN.

#### R-013 Upload on step 2, with each file's status

- **Epic:** E-DOCS · **Stories:** US-DOCS-01, US-DOCS-03, US-DOCS-23 · **Functions:** F-INGEST-01, F-INGEST-02, F-INGEST-03, F-INGEST-04, F-INGEST-05, F-INGEST-08, F-INGEST-09, F-EXTRACT-07, F-VALUE-10, F-AUTH-04, F-EXPORT-01, F-RENDER-01, F-RENDER-03, F-RENDER-05, F-RENDER-06, F-RENDER-09 · **Screens:** OB-2, UD-33, DB-15
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (rule 7, rule 10, rule 12, rule 13, rule 14, 2.3, 2.8; §5-2, §5-All, 7.1.1-D6, 7.1.1-E1) · Owner decision 2026-09-24 (OD-5: "no") · From approved design
- **Gated by:** none
- **Priority:** Must (proposed) · **Slice:** S1 (proposed)
- **Requirement:** The app lets the owner drop or browse several files at once on step 2, refuses only a file whose format is not on the accepted-format line or that is larger than the per-file size limit shown there, with an inline error on that file's row, and never blocks Continue. Each listed file shows its analysis status and coverage as code recorded them, in 2.8 wording, its detected stage with its one badge, and its revision as written. On the demo project the listed files are synthetic fixtures committed in the repo, and demo values cite them.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** Only 2.8 status lines: "Partly analysed (<read> of <total> pages)", "Not analysed: <file type> stored, not analysed", "Analysis failed"; a queued or analysing file shows a progress state with no text of its own. A stage nothing states reads Unknown; an analysed title block with no revision reads "none stated". No Edit on kind or stage (proposal 7.2.26 not approved, D-51), no file size (proposal 7.2.30 not approved, D-54), any file count is a bound value, and no remove action until the erasure job ships (R-016). The size-limit line is on the render test's reviewed allowlist. The five "Common document types (optional)" tiles are hints with no selected, checked or counted state. File content addressing the app is data. On the demo project the demo line "Demo data, not an assessment of the real building" shows on step 2 and on every page of its exports, demo values never carry `engineer_verified`, and the demo never uses the real hotel's name. Tests: G2-1, G12-1, G12-3, GS-1.
- **Acceptance:** US-DOCS-01 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9; US-DOCS-03 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9, AC10, AC11; US-DOCS-23 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6
- **Sources:** onboarding-spec 3 (Step 2); guardrails section 5 rows §5-2 (step 2, "No per-file status") and §5-All (all steps, "The demo project (fictional hotel)"); guardrails 2.3, 2.8, rule 2 ("Render test" allowlist), rule 7, rule 10 ("Demo data"), rule 12, rule 14; dashboards-spec 7.1.1 rows 7.1.1-D6 ("The demo registers on 15 and 18") and 7.1.1-E1 ("All of …"); build-readiness 3 "Now" items 5 and 10 and 2 "synthetic-fixtures" (Proposed). OD-5 is the owner's answer "no" when asked whether the demo should keep the real hotel's name. The live tile checklist is Proposed (onboarding-spec 3, Step 2) and is not part of this requirement; what the tiles are is open (D-24), and US-DOCS-01 AC7 keeps them hints with no state meanwhile. Whether the size limit also applies to all files together is R-021. The look of the undesigned file list, progress, error and drag-over states is open (dashboards 8.10, D-06). File names that contain digits against the render test: traceability 10.2 item 5 and 10.3 near miss 7 (synthetic fixture names can avoid digits meanwhile). Not reusing the real hotel's published facts is recommended, not decided (OD-5).

#### R-014 Formats the app does not read are stored and marked "Not analysed"

- **Epic:** E-DOCS · **Stories:** US-DOCS-04 · **Functions:** F-INGEST-02, F-INGEST-03, F-INGEST-05, F-INGEST-08, F-RENDER-03 · **Screens:** OB-2, UD-33, DB-15, UD-21

#### R-015 Read PDF and XLSX in the background, with evidence checked by code

- **Epic:** E-DOCS · **Stories:** US-DOCS-06, US-DOCS-07, US-DOCS-08, US-DOCS-09, US-DOCS-10, US-DOCS-11 · **Functions:** F-INGEST-02, F-INGEST-04, F-INGEST-05, F-INGEST-08, F-EXTRACT-01, F-EXTRACT-02, F-EXTRACT-03, F-EXTRACT-04, F-EXTRACT-05, F-EXTRACT-06, F-EXTRACT-07, F-EXTRACT-10, F-VALUE-01, F-VALUE-02, F-VALUE-10, F-REGISTRY-04, F-QUESTION-09, F-REVIEW-01, F-AUTH-02, F-AUTH-03, F-AUTH-06, F-AUDIT-01, F-RENDER-01, F-RENDER-03 · **Screens:** OB-2, OB-3, UD-33, UD-21, UD-15, DB-05, DB-15

- **Gated by:** none
- **Priority:** Must (proposed) · **Slice:** S1 (proposed)
- **Requirement:** The app reads each native-text PDF and XLSX file in the background for every registered field, records by code which pages, sheets and cells it read, and never makes the owner wait for it. Documents reach the AI only inside delimited data blocks built from one project, and code runs rule 1's five checks on every proposed candidate before storing it, so each stored value cites its file and location and each gap reads "Not found in the analysed documents" with what was searched. The app records each document's kind, stage and revision from its title block (cartuș), with the revision as written and the stage unknown when nothing states it.

Installed-equipment facts from design-stage documents stay provisional, and installation dates and warranties never come from model knowledge ("Not provided yet"). Embedded instructions and hidden text become findings for the engineer and change no state. Late results add a dot, join the review list and give one quiet notice. Logs and error reports hold no document text. Until build-readiness decision 2 is taken, only synthetic documents reach the AI (D-09). - **Epic:** E-DOCS · **Stories:** US-DOCS-22 · **Functions:** F-INGEST-04, F-EXTRACT-03, F-VALUE-01, F-VALUE-03, F-VALUE-04, F-QUESTION-09 · **Screens:** DB-15, OB-3
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (2.4, rule 4, section 4)
- **Gated by:** Blocked by open question new Q12 (D-61)
- **Priority:** Should (proposed) · **Slice:** S3
- **Requirement:** Once new Q12 is answered, when SOVITECH releases a new extractor, prompt or model version, or registers a new field, the app reads the project's documents again, appends new candidates and changes no stored candidate. A re-read value that disagrees with a `user_confirmed` or `engineer_verified` candidate puts the field in conflict, routed by rule 4, and never replaces the checked value; a re-read value equal to one the owner corrected away follows the answer to new Q12.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** Late results never interrupt: a dot on the step, the review list and one quiet notice, and no answer the owner gave changes. A skipped field that gains an eligible candidate becomes known and leaves the open items. A change to `prompts/`, the model id or the output schema runs the guardrail evals first, each sampled 5 times (CLAUDE.md, definition of done item 2). Tests: G4-1, G4-18, G7-4.
- **Until decided:** Not built: documents are not read again when the extractor, prompt or model version changes or a field is registered, and a field registered after a document was read counts that document in no "Not found in the analysed documents" line (rule 12).
- **Acceptance:** US-DOCS-22 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4
- **Sources:** guardrails 2.4, rule 4, rule 7 ("Late findings never interrupt"), section 4 ("The stopping rule … never stops analysis"); onboarding-spec 7 Q14 (settled by guardrails 2.3 and rule 4); CLAUDE.md "Definition of done". The new Q12 gate is added from the story's Open questions field; its Status does not carry it. Open: what happens when a re-read candidate equals a value the owner corrected away (new Q12, D-61; traceability 10.3 near miss 3); no criterion covers that case, and AC2 is not read as settling it.

### E-IFC: IFC models

IFC models exported from BIM tools are a primary input by the owner's direction of 2026-09-24 (OD-8: "based on data from the onboarding flow, based on IFC files from BIM softwares"). The direction approves no guardrail proposal and does not revise build-readiness decision 4. Under guardrails v1.5 a model is stored with its `DocumentRecord` and reads "Not analysed: IFC model stored, not analysed"; code may record what it contains for the engineer; and, once a viewer is decided, a stored model may be shown as a document under the four conditions of prompt 2 "Model views". No value read from a model passes rule 1's locator check until the approver accepts ifc-input 6.2.1, 6.2.2, 6.2.3 and 6.2.10, so every requirement below that stores a model value carries those four gates, build-readiness decision 4 and the approved mapping tables (ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3; D-92, written as one gate with build-readiness decision 6 where a story also names it), plus the gates of its own stories, and states the v1.5 behaviour meanwhile. The locator is described in full in R-027. Screens: OB-1 to OB-5, UD-21, UD-33, DB-15, UD-15, UD-44, UD-40, UD-41, UD-22, UD-43, DB-01, DB-04, DB-05, DB-10, DB-16, DB-17 and DB-20. The model views themselves are E-MODEL; the engineer's tag-source, life-safety and table-review actions are E-ENGINEER; dataset approval status is E-ADMIN.

#### R-022 IFC and RVT models are stored as documents marked "Not analysed"

- **Epic:** E-IFC · **Stories:** US-IFC-01, US-IFC-02 · **Functions:** F-INGEST-01, F-INGEST-02, F-INGEST-03, F-INGEST-05, F-INGEST-06, F-INGEST-07, F-INGEST-08, F-AUTH-03, F-AUTH-06, F-RENDER-03, F-RENDER-05 · **Screens:** OB-2, UD-33, DB-15, UD-21
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (rule 12, rule 13, 2.3, 2.8; §5-2) · Owner decision 2026-09-24 (OD-8: "based on data from the onboarding flow, based on IFC files from BIM softwares") · From approved design
- **Gated by:** none
- **Priority:** Must (proposed) · **Slice:** S1 (proposed)
- **Requirement:** The app accepts IFC files of any schema (IFC2X3, IFC4, IFC4X3_ADD2) and RVT files on step 2 and through "Upload Document", stores each under its project id and content hash with a `DocumentRecord`, and lists it with the other documents. Each model shows the 2.8 status line for a file stored but not analysed, naming its format as G12-1 names RVT ("Not analysed: IFC model stored, not analysed"; "Not analysed: RVT model stored, not analysed"), for as long as no value from it can be stored, including while model reading runs for the engineer. No value, badge, field state or "not found" coverage comes from a stored model, and its stage and revision read Unknown.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** Stage and revision read Unknown, never "none stated", and code sets neither from the file name or the model's contents. Once the revision declaration exists (R-016, S2), the owner or an engineer may declare a model a revision of an earlier one (2.3); code proposes no revision link from a model's contents. Once Delete exists (R-016, S2), it runs the erasure job, which also removes every converted viewing file made from the model. An RVT file is never sent to a conversion service that is not on the processor list. No owner screen shows a model-check line, schema line, count or task, and no app copy about a model contains a reserved term outside the places 2.8 allows (the general form of ifc-input 5.4 IFC-14, proposed, not indexed: its setup needs no stored model value, and its own situation, an IDS report shown in the UI, waits for the IDS check, new Q15, D-36). Continue and Generate never wait for a model. No link, banner or other element on step 2, the upload surface or Documents offers an IFC export guide (US-IFC-07 AC1; new Q16, D-36). Demo line on demo projects. Tests: G12-1, G12-4, G13-4.
- **Acceptance:** US-IFC-01 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9; US-IFC-02 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4
- **Sources:** guardrails 2.3, 2.8 ("File stored but not analysed"), rule 12, rule 13 ("Isolation", "Erasure"), G12-1; guardrails section 5 row §5-2 (step 2, "No per-file status"); ifc-input 1.2 items 6 and 13, 5.1 (`*.ifc` kept out of the repo except fixtures), 6.1 ("Coverage", "Isolation"), 6.3.1 items 2 and 7; build-readiness 3 "Now" item 5 and decision 4 (D-01); prompt 2 "A proposal is never a requirement". This holds under every option of ifc-input 6.3.1 item 1 (D-04). For RVT, an IFC export from the owner's designer is the recommended route, Proposed (ifc-input 2.2); Autodesk APS would be a processor under rule 13 and is not proposed (ifc-input 6.3.1 item 7; new Q16, D-36). Removing converted files with the model is stricter than rule 13's wording and adds no question, gate or owner-facing wording (ifc-input 6.2.16 would make it a rule). Owner-facing model coverage lines are Waiting on approval (US-IFC-10). The step 3 banner that must not name BIM files is E-REVIEW (traceability 10.2 item 1). US-IFC-01 AC1 (its Documents and "Upload Document" part), AC7 and AC8, and US-IFC-02 AC4 apply once R-016 ships (S2); in S1 (proposed) the model is listed on step 2 with no remove action (R-013).

- **Epic:** E-IFC · **Stories:** US-IFC-03 · **Functions:** F-IFC-01, F-INGEST-03, F-REVIEW-01, F-AUTH-02, F-RENDER-05 · **Screens:** UD-15, UD-44, DB-15

Where the engineer queue lives is open (dashboards 8.15, D-16).
