#### R-025 A stored model is converted for viewing and shown only as a document

- **Epic:** E-IFC · **Stories:** US-IFC-08 · **Functions:** F-IFC-10, F-AUTH-03, F-INGEST-07, F-VIEWER-01, F-VIEWER-02, F-RENDER-06 · **Screens:** OB-3, DB-01, DB-10, DB-16
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (rule 2, rule 13, 2.3) · Owner decision 2026-09-24 (OD-8: "based on data from the onboarding flow, based on IFC files from BIM softwares")
- **Gated by:** Blocked by open question onboarding Q3 and dashboards 8.5 (D-03) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 3 (D-04) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 4 (D-01)
- **Priority:** Should (proposed) · **Slice:** S2
- **Requirement:** When the viewer is built, the app converts a stored IFC model once into viewing files (3D geometry and plan images) and shows the model only as a document, under four conditions: the viewing files are keyed by project id plus content hash and served only after the project access check; the erasure job removes them with their document; nothing is drawn as text in the 3D scene, in textures or in plan images, and every label, count or area shown with the view is a bound value, none of them read from the model; and the view names its document with the stage and revision as recorded. The conversion record is not a value, a selection in the view shows no data from the model, and no model reads as analysed because it is shown.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** No conversion option that prints areas or names into a plan image is used, and an SVG plan with printed areas fails the render test (ifc-input 5.4 IFC-12, proposed, not indexed; its setup needs no stored model value, so it waits only for onboarding Q3, dashboards 8.5 and build-readiness decisions 3 and 4). The v1.5 render test cannot see text inside a raster plan image, a texture or a 3D scene; a test that fails on it is proposal ifc-input 6.2.15 (D-46), so until then keeping text out of them rests on the conversion options alone. Two projects that upload the same model each get their own conversion, and neither can load the other's. The model is never sent to a service that is not on the processor list. Removing converted files with their document is stricter than rule 13's wording and adds no question, gate or owner-facing wording. Pins, scale bars, north arrows, "From a superseded revision" on a view and "Illustrative model, not to scale" wait for proposal 7.2.8 and ifc-input 6.2.15 (D-45; D-46; E-MODEL). Tests: G2-1, G13-4.
- **Until decided:** Not built: no conversion runs and no view shows a stored model; the model views show their no-model state (E-MODEL, UD-46). The tooling (That Open Fragments on three.js, or IfcConvert GLB and SVG without printed areas) is Proposed (ifc-input 2.2), to be settled in a spike.
- **Acceptance:** US-IFC-08 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8
- **Sources:** prompt 2 "Model views"; ifc-input 2.2 ("Browser viewing"), 2.3 (licences: xeokit excluded, counsel before the first release), 4.2 ("Geometry for the 3D and 2D views"), 6.1 near miss 2 (project id plus content hash, not the hash alone), 6.3.2; guardrails rule 2 ("Render test"), rule 13 ("Isolation", "Erasure"), 2.3, G13-4; build-readiness 3 "Now" item 10 (no 3D in slice 1, Proposed) and "Later" (viewer libraries after onboarding Q3, dashboards 8.1 and 8.5 (build-readiness writes "dashboards Q1 and Q5") and proposal 7.2.8: build order, not a guardrail). The viewer is not gated on ifc-input 6.2.16. Converting on the server, so that the browser never parses the owner's file, is Proposed (ifc-input 2.2; section 13), for prompt 3's ADR. US-IFC-08 AC4's render-test clause holds for SVG plans only; for raster images it needs ifc-input 6.2.15 (D-46). F-IFC-10's own status line also names ifc-input 6.2.1; under functions.md's status rule that gate belongs to the parts only gated E-MODEL stories need (the join by GlobalId), not to this requirement. Which storey a plan image shows cannot be labelled from the model under v1.5 (traceability 10.3 near miss 28). Several models together or one at a time is open (ifc-input 6.3.2 item 4, D-03); so is the viewer library (ifc-input 6.3.2 item 6, D-03).

#### R-027 Model values carry an IFC locator checked by code

- **Epic:** E-IFC · **Stories:** US-IFC-27 · **Functions:** F-EXTRACT-04, F-IFC-04, F-VALUE-01, F-AUDIT-01 · **Screens:** UD-15, UD-41
- **Status:** Owner decision 2026-09-24 (OD-8: "based on data from the onboarding flow, based on IFC files from BIM softwares") · Required by guardrails (rule 1, rule 13, 2.1, 2.4)
- **Gated by:** Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.1 (not approved; D-38) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.2 (not approved; D-39) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.3 (not approved; D-40) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.10 (not approved; D-37) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 4 (D-01) · Blocked by open question ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3 (D-92)
- **Priority:** Should (proposed) · **Slice:** S3
- **Requirement:** Once model values can be stored, the app reads each stored model on the server with deterministic, table-first code and calls the AI only for what no approved mapping table maps (R-030), in delimited data blocks. Every model value it stores is a candidate whose evidence names the file by `Evidence.contentHash`, the model's declared schema as document metadata (`model.schema`, ifc-input 6.2.2), the element's GlobalId, STEP instance ids and attribute, property-set or quantity-set path, including through the type object (the proposed `Evidence.locator.ifc`, ifc-input 6.2.1), and the verbatim STEP text as its excerpt, and code runs rule 1's checks on it before it is stored. Values written in the file are `document`; sums, counts from the asset register and "exact unit conversions" (guardrails 2.1) over stored candidates are `calculated` by the engine; interpretations are `ai_inference`, capped by rule 3, and an asset type from an IFC class is always an inference, never `document`.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** A candidate that fails a check (another project's file, a changed content hash, a locator that does not resolve, an excerpt not found, a value that does not parse from its excerpt) is rejected and logged, and the field stays Unknown; so is a quantity the AI derived rather than read. Quantities computed from a model's shapes (areas, containment, port tracing) wait for ifc-input 6.2.7 (D-50); any inference made by code rather than the AI (a class lookup, a level type from a storey name, a space category) waits for ifc-input 6.2.9 (D-42). A model never creates a `reference` candidate. A table-only path makes no AI call. Tests: G1-4, G1-10, G13-1. Proposed cases, not indexed: ifc-input 5.4 IFC-1 (waits for ifc-input 6.2.1) and IFC-11 (the IFC2X3 file gives the same register as the IFC4 file; waits for ifc-input 6.2.1, 6.2.2, 6.2.3 and 6.2.10).
- **Until decided:** v1.5 behaviour: the app stores the IFC file with its `DocumentRecord` and shows "Not analysed: IFC model stored, not analysed" (R-022). Any candidate that code or the AI proposes from a model fails rule 1's locator check, is rejected and logged, and the field stays Unknown; no mapping table is consulted. Code may record what the model contains for the engineer's view only (R-023 records its header and schema errors). No "not found" statement counts a model whose values cannot be kept (rule 12, G12-4).
- **Acceptance:** US-IFC-27 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4
- **Sources:** prompt 2 "Shared contract" ("IFC") and "How the PRD applies the contract" (the locator is itself a proposal; the four fields mapped as above); ifc-input 4.1 items 1 to 7, 4.3, 6.1 ("Sources", "Evidence", "Candidates and events"), 6.2.1, 6.3.1 items 2 and 4; guardrails rule 1 ("Evidence is verified by code, not trusted"), 2.1, 2.4, rule 3, rule 13, rule 14; traceability 10.3 near miss 9 (a v1.5 constraint belongs to the first requirement that builds the feature). US-IFC-27 AC1 needs no code of its own: the evidence verifier built with document extraction (R-015) rejects any candidate without a valid locator. The approved mapping tables (ifc-input 6.3.1 items 2 and 3) are R-030. Build-readiness decision 1 is not listed: every "Depends on proposal" already waits for the approver. The model-view join by GlobalId is E-MODEL. The ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3 gate is the PRD's: prompt 2 gates every stored IFC value on the approved mapping tables (ifc-input 6.3.1 items 2 and 3), which need the SOVITECH asset taxonomy with its life-safety flags; item 2, the approver, is implied by the proposal gates.

#### R-028 A model's stage and revision, and revision links between models

- **Epic:** E-IFC · **Stories:** US-IFC-09, US-IFC-12 · **Functions:** F-INGEST-02, F-INGEST-06, F-IFC-01, F-EXTRACT-07, F-VALUE-07 · **Screens:** OB-2, UD-33, DB-15, UD-22, UD-43
- **Status:** Owner decision 2026-09-24 (OD-8: "based on data from the onboarding flow, based on IFC files from BIM softwares") · Required by guardrails (2.3, rule 4)
- **Gated by:** Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.1 (not approved; D-38) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.2 (not approved; D-39) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.3 (not approved; D-40) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.10 (not approved; D-37) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 4 (D-01) · Blocked by open question ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3 (D-92)
- **Priority:** Should (proposed) · **Slice:** S3
- **Requirement:** Once model records and model values can be stored, a model's stage and revision follow guardrails 2.3: upload order and issue date alone never make one model a revision of another; a revision link that code proposes changes nothing until the owner or an engineer confirms it; and a declared revision supersedes the older model's unverified values with no conflict and one notice listing the changed values, while a changed `engineer_verified` value puts the field in conflict for the engineer. Values from a model cite the IFC locator of R-027. Those from a model whose stage is unknown say so on their source lines, and for an existing building or a BMS modernization a design-stage model gives From design drawings only where no earlier 2.8 badge applies, with the stage named on the source line, and its installed-equipment facts stay provisional until an as-built document, a nameplate photo or a site survey supports them.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** One badge per value, the first match in the 2.8 order. The change notice reads, for example, "<revision> changed <n> values". The conflict goes to the engineer queue, never to the owner (rule 4). Tests: G2-6, G4-13, G4-14. Proposed case, not indexed: ifc-input 5.4 IFC-13 (Rev B with unchanged GlobalIds; waits for ifc-input 6.2.1, 6.2.2, 6.2.3 and 6.2.10).
- **Until decided:** v1.5 behaviour: a stored model's stage and revision read Unknown whatever its file name or IfcProject phase says, code proposes no revision link between models, and only the owner's or an engineer's declaration links two models as revisions (R-022). No value comes from a model, so a declared model revision supersedes no value. The model stays stored with its `DocumentRecord` and reads "Not analysed: IFC model stored, not analysed" (R-022).
- **Acceptance:** US-IFC-09 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4; US-IFC-12 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4
- **Sources:** ifc-input 6.1 ("Documents and stage"), 6.2.2; guardrails 2.3 ("Stage matters more than date", "Revisions and removal"), rule 4, G2-6, G4-13, G4-14. How a model's format, schema, authoring tool, stage and revision are recorded and set, and code proposing a revision link from matching GlobalIds, are proposal ifc-input 6.2.2's content and are Waiting on approval (US-IFC-09 and US-IFC-12, parts). ifc-input 6.2.2's "Edit" on the file row is not carried (traceability 10.2 item 10). How a model's stage and kind readings would combine with proposal 7.2.26 (D-51) is in ifc-input 6.2.2 (D-39). Where the change notice goes after Generate is open (new Q17, D-14). The ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3 gate is the PRD's: prompt 2 gates every stored IFC value on the approved mapping tables (ifc-input 6.3.1 items 2 and 3), which need the SOVITECH asset taxonomy with its life-safety flags; item 2, the approver, is implied by the proposal gates.

#### R-029 A model counts in "not found" only for what code processed

- **Epic:** E-IFC · **Stories:** US-IFC-10 · **Functions:** F-INGEST-05, F-INGEST-03, F-IFC-01, F-RENDER-03 · **Screens:** OB-2, UD-33, DB-15, OB-4
- **Status:** Owner decision 2026-09-24 (OD-8: "based on data from the onboarding flow, based on IFC files from BIM softwares") · Required by guardrails (rule 12, 2.8)
- **Gated by:** Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.1 (not approved; D-38) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.2 (not approved; D-39) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.3 (not approved; D-40) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.10 (not approved; D-37) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 4 (D-01) · Blocked by open question ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3 (D-92)
- **Priority:** Should (proposed) · **Slice:** S3
- **Requirement:** Once a model's values can be stored, a "Not found in the analysed documents (<coverage>)" statement counts the model as searched only for the parts code processed: no "not found" statement covers a part of a model that could not be processed, and finding nothing of a kind in a model never sets a field not applicable or a count to zero.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** "Not found in the analysed documents" is never "does not exist" (rule 12). Tests: G12-2, G12-4. Proposed case, not indexed: ifc-input 5.4 IFC-5 (a model counts as searched only once its values can be kept, so it waits for this requirement's gates; its model-naming half needs ifc-input 6.2.3, whose wording is Waiting on approval).
- **Until decided:** v1.5 behaviour: a model's row keeps "Not analysed: IFC model stored, not analysed" and shows no "Model contents" line, and no "Not found in the analysed documents (<coverage>)" line counts any model as searched (rule 12, G12-4). Code may record what the model contains for the engineer's view only (R-023 records its header and schema errors).
- **Acceptance:** US-IFC-10 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4
- **Sources:** ifc-input 6.1 ("Coverage"), 6.2.3; guardrails rule 12, 2.8, G12-2, G12-4; prompt 2 "A proposal is never a requirement" (no "not found" statement may count a model whose values cannot be kept). US-IFC-10's own gates are ifc-input 6.2.2, 6.2.3 and build-readiness decision 4; this requirement adds ifc-input 6.2.1 and 6.2.10, because its criteria AC3 and AC4 let a model count as searched, which rule 12 and G12-4 allow only once the model's values can be kept. The owner-facing "Model contents" line, "Partly analysed" for models and "not found" lines naming each model and its kind are proposal ifc-input 6.2.3's content and are Waiting on approval (US-IFC-10, part). The digits in a model-contents line are record-bound (proposal 7.2.30, D-54); register headers that state coverage are proposal 7.2.31 (D-83). The ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3 gate is the PRD's: prompt 2 gates every stored IFC value on the approved mapping tables (ifc-input 6.3.1 items 2 and 3), which need the SOVITECH asset taxonomy with its life-safety flags; item 2, the approver, is implied by the proposal gates.

#### R-030 IFC mapping tables: approval read from stored records, no online dictionary

- **Epic:** E-IFC · **Stories:** US-IFC-11 · **Functions:** F-REGISTRY-06, F-REVIEW-08, F-IFC-03, F-IFC-04, F-IFC-05 · **Screens:** UD-40, UD-15
- **Status:** Owner decision 2026-09-24 (OD-8: "based on data from the onboarding flow, based on IFC files from BIM softwares") · Required by guardrails (rule 1, 2.1, section 10)
- **Gated by:** Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.1 (not approved; D-38) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.2 (not approved; D-39) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.3 (not approved; D-40) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.10 (not approved; D-37) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 4 (D-01) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 6 (D-92) · Blocked by open question new Q32 (D-47)
- **Priority:** Should (proposed) · **Slice:** S3
- **Requirement:** Once model values can be stored, wherever the approval status of a table that maps IFC content to fields, asset types or systems is shown, it is read from stored approval records (US-IFC-11 AC5). A table version with no approval record, attached to a field as reference data, fails the loosening check and creates no `reference` candidate; an engineer's review of a table version changes no approval status; no action in the app creates or changes an approval record; and no online dictionary is consulted at runtime.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** A model never creates a `reference` candidate. Approval status appears read-only (E-ADMIN, UD-40). Property-set names that ifc-input 3.2 marks as not checked stay marked. Tests: G1-12.
- **Until decided:** v1.5 behaviour: no IFC mapping table is consulted and no candidate is shaped by one, and no value comes from a model (R-022). No action in the app creates or changes an approval record.
- **Acceptance:** US-IFC-11 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5
- **Sources:** ifc-input 2.2 (bSDD may inform a table's content and is never consulted at runtime), 3.2, 4.1, 6.2.10, 6.3.1 items 2 and 3; guardrails rule 1, 2.1, section 10, G1-12; build-readiness decision 6 (the asset taxonomy with life-safety flags that the class tables need); new Q32 (how approval records reach the app). Build-readiness decision 1, which US-IFC-11's status also names, is not listed: every "Depends on proposal" already waits for the approver. New Q32 stays as a gate in its own right (how approval records reach the app, which no app role may create), and its D row (D-47) is kept apart from the approver row (D-05), so this gate does not carry build-readiness decision 1. Tables as versioned datasets whose approval records gate every candidate they shape, each candidate recording its table version, and "Mapping not approved" on the engineer's view are proposal ifc-input 6.2.10's content and are Waiting on approval (US-IFC-11, part). The engineer's review action is E-ENGINEER.

#### R-032 Building properties from a model

- **Epic:** E-IFC · **Stories:** US-IFC-13 · **Functions:** F-IFC-03, F-IFC-04, F-VALUE-03, F-QUESTION-02, F-QUESTION-06, F-REGISTRY-07, F-VALUE-10, F-RENDER-03 · **Screens:** OB-1, OB-3, OB-5
- **Status:** Owner decision 2026-09-24 (OD-8: "based on data from the onboarding flow, based on IFC files from BIM softwares") · Required by guardrails (rule 1, rule 2, rule 3, rule 4, rule 8, rule 11)
- **Gated by:** Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.1 (not approved; D-38) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.2 (not approved; D-39) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.3 (not approved; D-40) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.10 (not approved; D-37) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.9 (not approved; D-42) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 4 (D-01) · Blocked by open question ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3 (D-92)
- **Priority:** Should (proposed) · **Slice:** S3
- **Requirement:** Once model values can be stored, the app reads a model's building property-set values (storey count, planned areas, occupancy type, sprinkler protection) as candidates that cite the IFC locator of R-027. A storey count with no qualifier is compared with every qualified floor candidate, giving one confirmation that names the matching reading, or a conflict; a planned area with no basis is stored with basis unknown and its original, and any confirmation names the basis; an occupancy type that names the building type gives building type as Likely with that evidence. It never overwrites the step 1 answers, never uses the project name as evidence for a value, and never preselects Fire Safety because a model indicates sprinkler protection.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** A building value from the model shows one 2.8 badge with a source line naming the model, and a field the model does not state reads Unknown. Confirmations appear only when rule 5's test passes and count against the budget the approver sets (approver setting 1, D-53). Inclusion of Fire Safety stays the owner's decision (rule 11). Tests: G1-11, G4-11, G8-2.
- **Until decided:** v1.5 behaviour: no candidate comes from a model's building properties; the storey count, planned areas, occupancy type and sprinkler protection keep their sources from documents and the owner, and the step 1 answers are untouched. The model stays stored with its `DocumentRecord` and reads "Not analysed: IFC model stored, not analysed" (R-022), and no "not found" statement counts it (rule 12, G12-4).
- **Acceptance:** US-IFC-13 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7
- **Sources:** ifc-input 4.2 ("Project, building, document"), 4.5, 6.1 ("Conflicts", "Owner flow"), 6.2.9; guardrails rule 1, rule 3, rule 4, rule 5, rule 8, rule 11. The first-estimate set is approver setting 3. A georeference serves the viewer only; a north arrow from it waits for proposal 7.2.8 and ifc-input 6.2.15 (E-MODEL). The ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3 gate is the PRD's: prompt 2 gates every stored IFC value on the approved mapping tables (ifc-input 6.3.1 items 2 and 3), which need the SOVITECH asset taxonomy with its life-safety flags; item 2, the approver, is implied by the proposal gates.

#### R-037 Equipment assets from a model

- **Epic:** E-IFC · **Stories:** US-IFC-19 · **Functions:** F-IFC-05, F-VALUE-08, F-EXTRACT-05, F-REGISTRY-04, F-CALC-04, F-CALC-08, F-REVIEW-03, F-VALUE-13, F-IFC-02, F-EXTRACT-10, F-VALUE-10, F-RENDER-01, F-RENDER-03 · **Screens:** OB-3, DB-17, DB-05
- **Status:** Owner decision 2026-09-24 (OD-8: "based on data from the onboarding flow, based on IFC files from BIM softwares") · Required by guardrails (2.5, rule 1, rule 2, rule 3, rule 4, rule 11, rule 14; 7.1.1-L2)
- **Gated by:** Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.1 (not approved; D-38) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.2 (not approved; D-39) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.3 (not approved; D-40) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.10 (not approved; D-37) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.4 (not approved; D-41) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.9 (not approved; D-42) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 4 (D-01) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 6 and ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3 (D-92)
- **Priority:** Should (proposed) · **Slice:** S3
- **Requirement:** Once model values can be stored, the app adds a model's equipment to the asset register, citing the IFC locator of R-027, with one asset per normalised tag across all documents, its type always an `ai_inference` whose confidence code caps (a tag prefix the glossary defines supports Likely), and its location only from explicit containment. Untagged objects are listed for the engineer as possible duplicates and never counted or merged, and points are never read from a model: they stay Estimated from SOVITECH templates. Every model asset whose type is on rule 11's list, that belongs to a rule 11 system or that is dual-use is flagged `lifeSafety`, offers only view, log and documents, and gets only status and alarm points, and nothing the model states and no action in the app clears the flag.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** Unverified values on engineer fields read SOVITECH will check, with a source line naming the model and the element; a location or system no relation states reads Unknown and is listed for the engineer. One tag with two types is one asset with Two values on its type, in the engineer queue, counted once. "Looks right" records only `owner_acknowledged` and leaves badges and Provisional unchanged. A property saying a unit is BMS ready leaves its interface Unknown under SOVITECH will check and makes no integration points. Hidden content in a model is reported to the engineer and gives no values. With AHUs in scope and fire detection present, the fire-alarm input and fire-mode status per AHU panel stay in the point list, and dual-use car-park fans state their hardwired fire-mode priority (rule 11). Tests: G1-6, G3-1, G3-3, G3-8, G4-3, G4-16, G4-17, G9-4, G11-3, G11-4. Proposed case, not indexed: the "Today" version of ifc-input 5.4 IFC-10 (untagged fan coils listed as possible duplicates, count "Not available yet"; waits for ifc-input 6.2.1, 6.2.2, 6.2.3 and 6.2.10).
- **Until decided:** v1.5 behaviour: no asset, tag, type or location is read from a model; the asset register is built from schedules, datasheets and other documents. The model stays stored with its `DocumentRecord` and reads "Not analysed: IFC model stored, not analysed" (R-022), and no "not found" statement counts it (rule 12, G12-4). A table-only path makes no AI call (ifc-input 6.3.1 item 4).
- **Acceptance:** US-IFC-19 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9, AC10, AC11, AC12

#### R-039 Ratings and properties from a model, with their units

- **Epic:** E-IFC · **Stories:** US-IFC-22 · **Functions:** F-IFC-04, F-REGISTRY-02, F-REGISTRY-03, F-CALC-06, F-VALUE-09, F-EXTRACT-02, F-EXTRACT-03, F-VALUE-10, F-RENDER-01, F-RENDER-03, F-IFC-02, F-EXTRACT-10 · **Screens:** DB-17, DB-05
- **Status:** Owner decision 2026-09-24 (OD-8: "based on data from the onboarding flow, based on IFC files from BIM softwares") · Required by guardrails (rule 1, rule 2, rule 8, rule 14, 2.7)
- **Gated by:** Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.1 (not approved; D-38) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.2 (not approved; D-39) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.3 (not approved; D-40) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.10 (not approved; D-37) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.11 (not approved; D-63) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 4 (D-01) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 2 (D-09) · Blocked by open question ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3 (D-92)
- **Priority:** Should (proposed) · **Slice:** S3
- **Requirement:** Once model values can be stored, the app reads a model asset's ratings, citing the IFC locator of R-027, with their units resolved from the file and mapped to a registry unit of the field's dimension, or refused. A chiller's cooling capacity and electrical input are two fields; a rating written as text goes through the rule 8 parser, keeping both readings of an ambiguous number at low confidence and keeping approximate wording; a value with no unit gives no quantity candidate for a field that has a dimension; an implausible value is Please check and stays out of totals; a rating the model does not state reads Unknown, never zero. Model text reaches the AI only inside delimited data blocks, and code checks any value from the answer before it is stored.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** A rating shows one 2.8 badge, the first match in the 2.8 order (SOVITECH will check while the engineer field is unverified), with a source line naming the model, the element and, for a design-stage model of an existing building, its stage. Any "not found" line counts only what was analysed. Hidden content in a model is reported to the engineer and gives no values. Tests: G1-1, G8-3, G8-4, G8-5, G8-10. Proposed cases, not indexed: ifc-input 5.4 IFC-7 and IFC-9 (wait for ifc-input 6.2.1, 6.2.2, 6.2.3 and 6.2.10), IFC-8 (waits for those and ifc-input 6.2.11).
- **Until decided:** v1.5 behaviour: no rating candidate is made from a model; ratings come from schedules, datasheets and other documents. The model stays stored with its `DocumentRecord` and reads "Not analysed: IFC model stored, not analysed" (R-022), and no "not found" statement counts it (rule 12, G12-4). A table-only path makes no AI call (ifc-input 6.3.1 item 4).
- **Acceptance:** US-IFC-22 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9, AC10
- **Sources:** ifc-input 3.2, 3.5, 4.1 (the AI maps only user-defined property names a table cannot map), 4.2 ("Assets"), 6.1 ("Units"), 6.2.11, 6.3.1 item 4; guardrails 2.7, rule 1, rule 2, rule 8 ("Power", "Parsing"), rule 14; build-readiness decision 2 (the AI's residual mapping of user-defined property names). Whether ratings in registry units could ship without ifc-input 6.2.11 and build-readiness decision 2 was reported with the first draft; prompt 1's gates are kept. A plant's make and model as a vendor field is proposal 7.2.7 (D-71), not built. Property-set names that ifc-input 3.2 marks as not checked stay marked. The ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3 gate is the PRD's: prompt 2 gates every stored IFC value on the approved mapping tables (ifc-input 6.3.1 items 2 and 3), which need the SOVITECH asset taxonomy with its life-safety flags; item 2, the approver, is implied by the proposal gates.

### E-REVIEW: Review of found values

How found values reach the owner (`docs/product/user-stories.md` E-REVIEW). It holds the cross-cutting pieces every screen and export shares: the one value component with its badge, source line and status lines, display precision, and the demo line. It also holds step 3's building facts with Edit, confirmations within the rule 5 budget, "View all extracted data" and step 3's undesigned states; conflicts the owner can judge and the "For you" and "SOVITECH will check" lists on the review step; the notice after a declared revision; the project card on the dashboards; and the Property page. Screens: every OB and DB screen and most UD pages through the shared component and the demo line (US-REVIEW-01, US-REVIEW-03); OB-3, OB-5, OB-8, UD-34 and UD-45 for step 3 and the review step; DB-02, DB-06 to DB-08 and DB-10 to DB-22 for the project card; UD-02 for Property. The home for open items after the intake waits for proposal 7.2.27; its behaviour meanwhile is in R-004. The engineer's queue is E-ENGINEER, the HVAC assets row and "Looks right" are E-ASSETS, file status lines on step 2 and the Documents page are E-DOCS, and exports are E-REPORTS.

#### R-043 One value component and display precision

- **Epic:** E-REVIEW · **Stories:** US-REVIEW-01, US-REVIEW-02 · **Functions:** F-VALUE-02, F-VALUE-10, F-CALC-01, F-CALC-02, F-RENDER-01, F-RENDER-02, F-RENDER-03, F-RENDER-04, F-RENDER-06, F-AUDIT-05 · **Screens:** OB-2, OB-3, OB-4, OB-5, OB-6, OB-7, OB-8, DB-01, DB-02, DB-03, DB-04, DB-05, DB-06, DB-07, DB-08, DB-09, DB-10, DB-11, DB-12, DB-13, DB-14, DB-15, DB-16, DB-17, DB-18, DB-19, DB-20, DB-21, DB-22, UD-01, UD-02, UD-03, UD-05, UD-06, UD-08, UD-09, UD-10, UD-11, UD-13, UD-17, UD-20, UD-25, UD-26, UD-27, UD-28, UD-29, UD-33, UD-34, UD-35, UD-38, UD-45

- **Priority:** Must (proposed) · **Slice:** S1 (proposed)
- **Requirement:** The app renders every engineering value on every screen and export through one value component that receives only a resolved field object and shows one 2.8 badge on the same line as the figure, the source line below it, any 2.8 status line, and a missing value as "Unknown", "Not provided yet" or "Not available yet" with its action, never as a zero, a blank or a dash. - **Epic:** E-REVIEW · **Stories:** US-REVIEW-04, US-REVIEW-05, US-REVIEW-06, US-REVIEW-07, US-REVIEW-08, US-REVIEW-09 · **Functions:** F-INGEST-04, F-INGEST-05, F-INGEST-08, F-EXTRACT-06, F-VALUE-02, F-VALUE-03, F-VALUE-04, F-VALUE-05, F-VALUE-06, F-VALUE-10, F-VALUE-11, F-VALUE-14, F-REGISTRY-02, F-REGISTRY-03, F-QUESTION-01, F-QUESTION-02, F-QUESTION-07, F-CALC-02, F-CALC-04, F-CALC-05, F-RENDER-01, F-RENDER-03, F-RENDER-05, F-REVIEW-01, F-AUDIT-01, F-AUDIT-03 · **Screens:** OB-3, OB-5, OB-8, UD-34, UD-45

#### R-046 Conflicts and the open-item lists on the review step

- **Epic:** E-REVIEW · **Stories:** US-REVIEW-11, US-REVIEW-12 · **Functions:** F-VALUE-03, F-VALUE-04, F-QUESTION-01, F-QUESTION-07, F-RENDER-01, F-REVIEW-01, F-REVIEW-04 · **Screens:** OB-3, OB-8

"For you" lists only what the owner can resolve, ordered by its effect on the estimate (the top three, then "and <n> more"), each with what it concerns and its action, and "SOVITECH will check" shows engineer items as one line per group; every count on the step counts only what the owner can act on.

You entered <b>. Which is right?" with each source (rule 4); a `conflict_resolved` event records the chosen candidate, who, when and why (rule 4); "Documents disagree on this. A SOVITECH engineer will check it." (G4-8, G4-18); "Not available yet: two values for <field>" (G4-12) or "Provisional: two values for <field>" with a range (rule 4); the proposed value follows the document-stage order the approver confirms, never issue date alone (rule 4); "<n> things for you to check" and "SOVITECH will check <n> equipment classifications" (G7-5); "Source document removed" under "For you" for owner fields (G4-15), and, until new Q13 is answered, under "SOVITECH will check" for engineer fields, not counted in "<n> things for you to check" (Proposed (PRD interim, reversible); D-61); "Site survey needed" under SOVITECH will check (G1-7); a labelled value rule 5 did not flag is not an open item (rule 7); nothing blocks "Generate Proposal" (rule 7).

Grouped: the two stories share OB-3 and OB-8 and the review step's conflicts and lists, no gate and S1 (proposed); split from step 3 (R-045), whose unconfirmed items these lists receive (US-REVIEW-06 AC1, AC2). The approved step 8 draws neither list; guardrails section 5 adds both. Open, not gating: which screen "the review step" is (D-14); where an engineer field whose only source document was deleted is listed (D-61); where a "For you" item's action leads, and whether the owner returns to the review after it (partly D-10; R-008); the document-stage order and the tolerances (D-53, D-93). ### E-SCOPE: Systems in scope

Which building systems the BMS proposal covers, and how that choice reaches every screen and estimate. It covers step 4's detection badges and the owner's choice (OB-4), Fire Safety as monitoring only, excluded systems in every estimate (DB-12, DB-13, DB-22), the System Scope page drawn twice (DB-16 and DB-06, with DB-13's SELECT SYSTEMS panel and UD-31 for its 3D and 2D behaviour) with its points and its canvas, scope options beyond step 4's eight systems, the per-floor Systems View drawn twice (DB-03, DB-09), system risers and pins on the canvas, SOVITECH's proposed design on these pages, and a per-system automation level on CAPEX (DB-13). Scope decisions also render on OB-8, DB-19, DB-20 and DB-22. Each requirement holds stories that share one gate set and one slice. Zones drawn on a stored model's plan (US-ZONES-06), the per-level equipment chart (US-ASSETS-12) and equipment pins (US-ASSETS-13) have requirements in their own epics.

#### R-052 System Scope page: decisions, edits and detail panel

- **Epic:** E-SCOPE · **Stories:** US-SCOPE-05, US-SCOPE-06, US-SCOPE-07 · **Functions:** F-VALUE-01, F-VALUE-06, F-VALUE-10, F-VALUE-11, F-VALUE-12, F-VALUE-14, F-REGISTRY-08, F-QUESTION-06, F-CALC-02, F-CALC-04, F-PRICE-05, F-PROPOSAL-02, F-RENDER-01, F-RENDER-03, F-RENDER-05, F-RENDER-06, F-RENDER-09, F-VIEWER-03, F-AUTH-02, F-AUDIT-03 · **Screens:** OB-4, OB-8, DB-06, DB-13, DB-16, DB-19, DB-20, DB-22
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (rules 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 2.4, 2.5, 2.6, 2.8; 7.1-r20, 7.1-r27, 7.1.1-C1, 7.1.1-C4, 7.1.1-C7, 7.1.1-C8, 7.1.1-E1, 7.1.1-E2, 7.1.1-E4, 7.1.1-E5) · From approved design
- **Gated by:** Blocked by open question dashboards 8.3 (D-02)
- **Priority:** Should (proposed) · **Slice:** S2
- **Requirement:** The app shows the systems in scope on a System Scope page (DB-16 and DB-06, with DB-13's SELECT SYSTEMS panel where it is built): each catalogue system shows one In Scope state drawn from its recorded decision, identical on every surface that shows it, and a detail panel shows the system's description, decision, levels, equipment and zones as register queries. The owner can change a system's scope there with no question, confirmation or required field added: the change appends a new decision candidate, and every dependent output reads "Out of date, recalculating" until the engine appends the new result.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** Each decision shows Provided by you, Suggested (until "Save and Continue" writes a visible suggestion as the owner's answer, as G3-4 tests for automation areas) or Not provided yet, never drawn as off or excluded; no "Planned" state, no Coverage percentage, bar or dash; the ⓘ never holds the only copy of a label, range, source, basis or open-items count (2.8). Counts are Calculated register queries by asset type with the filter named and "Provisional: depends on <n> equipment items not yet checked"; level labels come from the level register, one per level; one value renders identically everywhere (G2-7) with no count-up animation (G2-8). Where a stored quotation record used a decision that the owner changes, its figures read "Superseded: inputs changed on <date>" and return to their "Preliminary investment estimate" labels (G10-2), and a generated proposal keeps its snapshot. No BMS LIVE chip, live footer, live status or "Current Load"; no Controllers or Network tab while proposal 7.2.10 is not approved (D-65). Demo line on the page (GS-1).
- **Until decided:** The page's content is built once and reached from the project sidebar (R-146) and from "← Back to System Scope" on Equipment and Zones; its "Save and Continue →" opens Zones, and its "← Back to Topology" link is shown only once Topology is built (its Logical view, R-071, S3), because no link leads to a page that is not built (R-146). Which tab or sidebar item holds it, whether DB-06 stays a second page and whether DB-13's panel edits stay open. Proposed (dashboards-spec 2.5; PRD interim, reversible): DB-16's layout as the base, with DB-06's pills and DB-13's panel, where built, showing the same decisions read-only.
- **Acceptance:** US-SCOPE-05 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9, AC10, AC11, AC12; US-SCOPE-06 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9, AC10, AC11; US-SCOPE-07 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9
- **Sources:** docs/product/user-stories.md E-SCOPE (US-SCOPE-05 to US-SCOPE-07); guardrails 2.4, 2.5, 2.6, 2.8, rules 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 10; design/dashboards-spec.md 4 (06; 16 "Behaviour" and "Links"), 1.2 (06 and 16 drawn twice), 7.1 rows 7.1-r20 ("06 scope pills"), 7.1-r27 ("All (L) values"); 7.1.1 rows 7.1.1-C1 ("16's "From Topology" counts, 17's ..."), 7.1.1-C4 ("16's "Coverage ..."), 7.1.1-C7 ("Scope shown on 13, 16, 19, 20 and 22, against step 4"), 7.1.1-C8 ("Edits: 13's checkboxes, sliders and ..."), 7.1.1-E1, 7.1.1-E2 (""BMS LIVE" chip; "BMS Live · Last sync" footer"), 7.1.1-E4 ("Level labels: 11's callouts, the stacks on 13, 16 and 17 ..."), 7.1.1-E5 ("Every value"); traceability.md 10.2 conflicts 24 and 25. "Planned" is new Q22 (D-64); one registered editor per decision is proposal 7.2.17 and the post-Generate home for notices is proposal 7.2.27, neither written here. #### R-053 Estimated points per system on System Scope

- **Epic:** E-SCOPE · **Stories:** US-SCOPE-08 · **Functions:** F-VALUE-12, F-REGISTRY-06, F-QUESTION-07, F-CALC-03, F-CALC-08, F-RENDER-01, F-RENDER-04, F-RENDER-05, F-RENDER-07 · **Screens:** DB-06, DB-16
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (rules 1, 8, 9, 10, 2.1; 7.1-r10, 7.1-r11, 7.1.1-C2) · From approved design
- **Gated by:** Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 6 (D-92) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 1 (D-05) · Blocked by open question dashboards 8.3 (D-02)
- **Priority:** Should (proposed) · **Slice:** S2
- **Requirement:** On System Scope the app shows the points of each system whose recorded decision is include as an Estimated range from SOVITECH point templates, with its basis in the inputs' own labels and its method and version, broken down into hardware I/O by type, integration by protocol and variant, and virtual, never as one priced total. Demo line on the page (GS-1).
- **Until decided:** For build-readiness decisions 6 and 1: every points figure reads "Not available yet", naming the missing point templates, with the item under SOVITECH will check (US-SCOPE-08 AC6). Benchmarks shown to the owner are proposal 7.2.5 (D-91) and are not written here. The proposal's points estimate is E-PROPOSAL (US-PROPOSAL-07), blocked by the same decisions; points per asset are R-067; whether room automation is its own catalogue system is dashboards 8.7 (R-055).

#### R-054 A stored model on System Scope's canvas

- **Epic:** E-SCOPE · **Stories:** US-SCOPE-12 · **Functions:** F-INGEST-07, F-IFC-10, F-RENDER-05, F-RENDER-06, F-VIEWER-01, F-VIEWER-02, F-VIEWER-03, F-AUTH-03 · **Screens:** DB-06, DB-16, UD-31
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (rules 1, 2, 7, 8, 12, 13, 2.2, 2.3; 7.1.1-E4) · From approved design · Owner decision 2026-09-24 (OD-8: "based on data from the onboarding flow, based on IFC files from BIM softwares")
- **Gated by:** Blocked by open question onboarding Q3 and dashboards 8.5 (D-03) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 3 (D-04) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 4 (D-01) · Blocked by open question dashboards 8.3 (D-02)
- **Priority:** Should (proposed) · **Slice:** S2
- **Requirement:** System Scope's canvas shows a stored model only as a view of that document, naming the document with its stage and revision as recorded, and reads "Not available yet", naming the missing model with the action to upload one, when no model is stored. A click on a model object shows no object selection and no data from the model, and the levels listed beside the canvas come from the level register, with nothing attached to the model's geometry.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** The canvas follows prompt 2's four conditions for model views: viewing files keyed by project id plus content hash and served only after the project access check (G13-4); removed with their document by the erasure job, a stricter build choice that ifc-input 6.2.16 would make a rule (D-89); nothing drawn as text in the scene, textures or plan images, and every label, count or area shown with it bound to a value id, none read from the model (G2-1 sees page elements only; text inside a canvas has no check yet, ifc-input 6.2.15); the view names its document with stage and revision as recorded. Showing a model never makes it analysed: its file keeps "Not analysed: IFC model stored, not analysed" while its values cannot be kept, and no model-check line is shown to the owner (the general form of ifc-input 5.4 IFC-14, proposed, not indexed, needs no stored model value; its own situation, an IDS report, waits for new Q15 (D-36), and an owner-facing model-check line for ifc-input 6.2.14 (D-73)). No 2D mode is offered (US-MODEL-10), and no system riser, pin, link between systems, key-plan inset, section-direction caption, scale bar or north mark is drawn while proposal 7.2.8 and ifc-input 6.2.15 are not approved (R-057). Demo line on the page (GS-1); a demo model comes from a synthetic fixture in the repo.
- **Until decided:** For onboarding Q3, dashboards 8.5 and build-readiness decisions 3 and 4: no viewer is built, so the canvas and its 3D / 2D / Section control are not built, and no illustrative model is shown. For dashboards 8.3: whether the 3D and 2D controls swap this canvas or open Topology 07 and 10 (UD-31) stays open.
- **Acceptance:** US-SCOPE-12 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8
- **Sources:** docs/product/user-stories.md E-SCOPE (US-SCOPE-12); guardrails 2.2, 2.3, rules 1, 2, 7, 8, 12 and 13 ("Isolation", "Erasure"); design/dashboards-spec.md 4 (06, 16), 1.2 (06 and 16 drawn twice); 7.1.1 row 7.1.1-E4 ("Level labels: 11's callouts, the stacks on 13, 16 and 17 ..."); docs/ifc-input.md 2.2 (viewer tooling, recommended), 6.1 near miss 2, 6.3.2 items 1, 3 and 5; docs/dev-prompts/02-prd.md "Model views". An illustrative model would need proposal 7.2.8 (D-45; docs/ifc-input.md 6.3.2 item 1 asks what the views show with no IFC). The viewer, the canvas's conversion states (UD-46) and the storey-to-level join are E-MODEL (US-MODEL-05, US-MODEL-07, US-MODEL-10). G2-1 cannot see text drawn inside a canvas and G13-4 does not test erasure, so those halves of US-SCOPE-12 AC3 and AC4 have no automated check yet (ifc-input 6.2.15 and 6.2.16); the criteria stay, because prompt 2's "Model views" conditions require the behaviour. OD-8 is added to the Status because this capability shows or reads the owner's IFC models (the IFC direction of 2026-09-24); US-SCOPE-12 does not carry it.

#### R-057 System risers and pins on System Scope's canvas

- **Epic:** E-SCOPE · **Stories:** US-SCOPE-13 · **Functions:** F-VIEWER-04, F-VIEWER-05 · **Screens:** DB-06, DB-16
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (rules 1, 2, 11; 7.1.1-L4) · From approved design · Owner decision 2026-09-24 (OD-8: "based on data from the onboarding flow, based on IFC files from BIM softwares")
- **Gated by:** Depends on proposal 7.2.8 (not approved; D-45) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.15 (not approved; D-46) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.1 (not approved; D-38) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.2 (not approved; D-39) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.3 (not approved; D-40) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.10 (not approved; D-37) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.4 (not approved; D-41) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.8 (not approved; D-43) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.9 (not approved; D-42) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 3 (D-04) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 4 (D-01) · Blocked by open question onboarding Q3 and dashboards 8.5 (D-03) · Blocked by open question ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3 (D-92)
- **Priority:** Could (proposed) · **Slice:** Later
- **Requirement:** On a stored model's view on System Scope's canvas the app draws system risers and pins only where a document places them. The fire system is drawn as a separate system with a one-way monitoring link, never joined to another system's riser, and labelled "monitoring only (read-only); fire logic and fire-mode interlocks remain in the fire system". Every label or count shown with the view is a page element bound to a value id, never text inside the scene.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** Bound labels (G2-1; text inside a canvas is invisible to it, ifc-input 6.2.15). Level labels come from the level register, one label per level everywhere (rule 8; 2.2). Values read from a model, once they can be stored, carry the contract's locator: the file hash as `Evidence.contentHash`; the IFC schema as document metadata (`model.schema`, ifc-input 6.2.2); the GlobalId, the STEP instance ids and the attribute, property-set or quantity-set path, including through the type object, as the proposed `Evidence.locator.ifc` (ifc-input 6.2.1); and the verbatim STEP text as the excerpt. Placements and containment written in the file are `document`; a type or level type inferred by code waits for ifc-input 6.2.9, and an asset type from an IFC class is always an inference. Pins join model objects to register assets by tag, which needs ifc-input 6.2.4. Model views keep prompt 2's four conditions (as in R-054). Demo line on the page (GS-1); any model shown comes from a synthetic fixture in the repo.
- **Until decided:** The v1.5 behaviour: nothing is drawn on System Scope's canvas: no system risers, pins, links between systems, key-plan inset, section-direction caption or north mark (US-SCOPE-13 AC1). An IFC model is stored with its DocumentRecord and shows "Not analysed: IFC model stored, not analysed"; code may record what the model contains as coverage for the engineer; no "not found" statement counts a model whose values cannot be kept (rule 12, G12-4).
- **Acceptance:** US-SCOPE-13 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4
- **Sources:** docs/product/user-stories.md E-SCOPE (US-SCOPE-13); guardrails 2.2, rules 1, 2, 8, 11 and 12; design/dashboards-spec.md 4 (06, 16), 7.2 item 8 and "Batch 2 sharpens" row 8; 7.1.1 row 7.1.1-L4 ("16's fire riser drawn joining Water"); docs/ifc-input.md 4.1, 4.2, 6.2.1 to 6.2.4, 6.2.8 to 6.2.10, 6.2.15, 6.3.1 item 2, 6.3.2; docs/dev-prompts/02-prd.md "Model views" and "How the PRD applies the contract". Risers and pins placed by level need the storey-to-level join (US-MODEL-07, E-MODEL), after the viewer of R-054. G2-1 cannot see text inside a canvas, so that half of US-SCOPE-13 AC3 has no automated check yet (ifc-input 6.2.15). The ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3 gate is the PRD's: prompt 2 gates every stored IFC value on the approved mapping tables (ifc-input 6.3.1 items 2 and 3), which need the SOVITECH asset taxonomy with its life-safety flags; item 2, the approver, is implied by the proposal gates. ### E-ZONES: Zones

The building's zones as one register: zone subjects with what each zone counts, their level and their area with basis (OB-3's Zones row, DB-20, DB-04, DB-06's ZONES tab); the Zones page drawn twice (DB-20 and DB-04) with its List mode (UD-27), zone details and the zone editor (UD-09) for corrections and owner-added zones; area roll-ups by category; the Matrix mode (UD-27); and zones drawn on a stored model's floor plan (US-ZONES-06, R-064).

#### R-060 Zone register

- **Epic:** E-ZONES · **Stories:** US-ZONES-01 · **Functions:** F-INGEST-09, F-EXTRACT-04, F-EXTRACT-06, F-VALUE-03, F-VALUE-10, F-VALUE-11, F-CALC-04, F-CALC-05, F-RENDER-01, F-RENDER-05 · **Screens:** OB-3, DB-04, DB-06, DB-20
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (2.2, rules 1, 3, 4, 8, 12; 7.1.1-C1, 7.1.1-C6) · From approved design
- **Gated by:** none
- **Priority:** Should (proposed) · **Slice:** S1 (proposed)
- **Requirement:** The app keeps the zones that analysed documents list as one register of zone subjects, each with its id and name as written, its level, what it counts (HVAC control zone, lighting zone or fire compartment, or Unknown) and its area with basis, and each value a candidate with its source and evidence that code has checked. Every zone count, including step 3's Zones row, is a Calculated count over this register that names what it counts, never counts zones of different kinds together, and feeds no per-zone estimate while its qualifier is unknown.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** A zone area goes through the value component with its basis named, or with basis unknown and its original text kept; area candidates on one basis that differ beyond the registered tolerance show Two values with both sources, routed by `confirmBy`. A zone with a drawn outline and no written area reads Unknown, and neither the AI nor code produces an area from the outline. An inferred zone type shows Likely or Possible. Once any document is analysed, a missing zone count reads "Not found in the analysed documents (<coverage>)", never zero and never covering unread pages or stored-only files (G12-4); before any analysis it reads Unknown. Equipment and system counts per zone are register queries naming the zone. Under v1.5 no zone is read from an IFC model (IfcSpace, IfcZone and IfcSpatialZone as zones are E-IFC's and gated), and a stored model never counts as searched. Demo zones cite synthetic fixture documents in the repo, and the demo line shows (GS-1).
- **Acceptance:** US-ZONES-01 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9, AC10, AC11
- **Sources:** docs/product/user-stories.md E-ZONES (US-ZONES-01); guardrails 2.2, rules 1, 3, 4, 8 ("Counts state what they count") and 12; design/dashboards-spec.md 7.1.1 rows 7.1.1-C1 ("16's "From Topology" counts, 17's ..."), 7.1.1-C6 ("20's zone areas, count, type and description"); design/onboarding-spec.md 3 (Step 3); docs/build-readiness.md 3 "Now" items 5 and 10; docs/ifc-input.md 6.1 ("Conflicts": no identity rule for zones, so same-id zones on different levels are not merged); traceability.md 10.2 conflicts 27 and 29, 10.3 near misses 16 and 27. Step 3's Zones row itself is E-REVIEW (US-REVIEW-04 AC9). Zone kinds, origin and containment wait for proposal 7.2.28 (US-ZONES-08). Plausible ranges and tolerances are approver setting 5 (D-93); the demo floor structure is dashboards 8.4 (D-18) and build-readiness decision 7 (D-18).

### E-ASSETS: Asset register

Equipment as assets, never as bare counts: one asset per tag with every appearance as evidence, counts by type calculated from the register, and the owner's acknowledgement on equipment (OB-3, DB-17, DB-05); types shown as Likely or Possible, points per asset and view-only life-safety assets; the Equipment list drawn twice (DB-17 and DB-05, and DB-06's EQUIPMENT tab) with its inspector, Documents tab, filters and export (UD-26); the asset detail page (UD-08) with ratings; the per-level equipment chart on DB-05 (US-ASSETS-12, R-069); and pins on a stored model's plan and 3D view (US-ASSETS-13, R-070).

#### R-065 Asset register, counts by type and the owner's acknowledgement

- **Epic:** E-ASSETS · **Stories:** US-ASSETS-01, US-ASSETS-03, US-ASSETS-04 · **Functions:** F-INGEST-09, F-EXTRACT-04, F-EXTRACT-08, F-VALUE-01, F-VALUE-03, F-VALUE-04, F-VALUE-08, F-VALUE-10, F-VALUE-14, F-QUESTION-07, F-CALC-04, F-RENDER-01, F-RENDER-03, F-RENDER-05, F-RENDER-06, F-REVIEW-01, F-REVIEW-03, F-AUTH-02, F-AUTH-04 · **Screens:** OB-3, DB-03, DB-05, DB-09, DB-16, DB-17, DB-20
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (2.5, rules 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 14; §5-3b, 7.1-r9, 7.1-r17, 7.1.1-C1, 7.1.1-C10) · From approved design
- **Gated by:** none
- **Priority:** Must (proposed) · **Slice:** S1 (proposed)
- **Requirement:** The app keeps equipment as an asset register with one asset per normalised tag, system prefix included, and every appearance as evidence; it lists untagged appearances as possible duplicates for the engineer without merging or counting them, keeps each configuration with its motors or drives, and lets only engineer accounts merge, split or remove assets, each as an event with a reason. Every equipment count, from step 3's HVAC assets row to each page's list total, is a Calculated count over the register with its filter in the label, broken down by asset type and excluding removed and merged assets. On equipment the owner can say only "Looks right" or "Something's wrong", alone or for a selection, which records owner_acknowledged or sends a note to the engineer queue and changes no badge, value or estimate.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** Counts carry "Provisional: depends on <n> equipment items not yet checked" while any input is unchecked. Step 3's row is badged Calculated, its items appear once under SOVITECH will check as one line per group ("<n> equipment classifications"), and the owner's count holds only items they can act on; no "Confirm all" and no Edit on the equipment count. Assets whose type is unknown or in conflict are shown apart and counted once. A type seen only untagged reads "Not available yet", naming the items listed for SOVITECH (ifc-input 5.4 IFC-10, proposed, not indexed; waits for the minimum set, ifc-input 6.2.1, 6.2.2, 6.2.3 and 6.2.10, and its counted version also for ifc-input 6.2.5). Once any document is analysed, a type with no asset reads "Not found in the analysed documents (<coverage>)", never zero unless a document, the owner or an engineer says there are none; before any analysis it reads Unknown (G12-2). Tags show as written, and an AI total is rejected. Cases: same-tag evidence (G4-3), type conflicts to the engineer (G4-16), untagged symbols listed (G4-17), duty/standby and twin-head configurations (G4-4), document-stage precedence proposed and a person decides (G4-6), design-stage-only assets From design drawings with the stage named (G2-6), one count identical across screens (G2-7) with no count-up (G2-8), owner_acknowledged never clears Provisional (G3-3), a non-engineer call to the verification endpoint is rejected (G10-3). An owner's note that reads like an instruction changes no state (rule 14). Demo assets cite synthetic fixture documents and never carry engineer_verified, and the demo line shows (GS-1). Under v1.5 no asset is read from an IFC model (E-IFC holds the gated read), and a stored model never counts as searched.
- **Acceptance:** US-ASSETS-01 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9, AC10; US-ASSETS-03 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9, AC10; US-ASSETS-04 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9
- **Sources:** docs/product/user-stories.md E-ASSETS (US-ASSETS-01, US-ASSETS-03, US-ASSETS-04); guardrails 2.5, rules 3, 4, 7 and 14; guardrails section 5 row §5-3b (step 3, HVAC assets ...); design/dashboards-spec.md 7.1 rows 7.1-r9 ("All counts (01, 03, 05, 07, 08, 09)"), 7.1-r17 ("05, 10 asset tags"); 7.1.1 rows 7.1.1-C1 ("16's "From Topology" counts, 17's ..."), 7.1.1-C10 ("17's bulk checkboxes"); docs/build-readiness.md 3 "Now" items 3, 5, 8 and 10; traceability.md 10.2 conflicts 4 and 42, 10.3 near misses 26 and 29. The document-stage order used to propose an active candidate is approver setting 4 (D-53); whether the engineer review queue lives in this app is dashboards 8.15 (D-16). Types from the taxonomy are R-067. Coverage on register headers (proposal 7.2.31) and parts summing to their total (proposal 7.2.14) are not written here.

#### R-067 Asset types, points per asset and view-only life-safety assets

- **Epic:** E-ASSETS · **Stories:** US-ASSETS-02, US-ASSETS-09, US-ASSETS-10 · **Functions:** F-EXTRACT-05, F-VALUE-10, F-VALUE-13, F-REGISTRY-04, F-REGISTRY-06, F-QUESTION-07, F-CALC-08, F-RENDER-01, F-RENDER-03, F-RENDER-04, F-RENDER-05, F-REVIEW-02, F-REVIEW-03, F-REVIEW-07, F-AUDIT-05 · **Screens:** OB-3, DB-05, DB-09, DB-10, DB-16, DB-17, DB-20, UD-08, UD-26

- **Priority:** Must (proposed) · **Slice:** S2
- **Requirement:** The app stores each asset's type as an `ai_inference` whose confidence code caps against the evidence, shown as Likely, Possible or SOVITECH will check and worded as a possibility, and shows each asset's points as an Estimated range from SOVITECH point templates per motor or drive and configuration, broken down by point type and identical wherever the asset appears. It sets `lifeSafety` on an asset whose type the approved taxonomy marks, that belongs to a system rule 11 lists, or that is dual-use equipment; a flagged asset offers only view, log and documents, alone or in bulk, and its points are status and alarm inputs only.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** Likely from a schedule row (G3-1) or a tag prefix the reference glossary defines (G3-8), at most Possible from a symbol (G3-2), SOVITECH will check when partly legible or ambiguous; after an engineer's verification the badge reads Verified by SOVITECH with the line "AI inference, verified by SOVITECH" (G3-7); a tier's wording drops one step when corrections exceed the threshold the approver sets (G3-6; approver setting 2, D-53); one badge per value on the same line, at 2.8's prominence. Points: basis line naming the point-template version, method and version, "Provisional: depends on <n> equipment items not yet checked", ranges rounded outward (G9-1), breakdown into hardware I/O by type, integration by protocol and variant, and virtual (G9-3), source `estimated` (G9-4), both motors of a duty/standby pair (G4-4); integration points Estimated with the method named when no register map, EDE file, PICS or point list exists, and none for an interface that is unknown or written only as "compatibil BMS" (G1-6); the fire-alarm input and fire-mode status for each AHU panel (G11-3); an excluded system's assets add no points except those (G10-7); the same value on Equipment, Zones and Topology (G2-7). Dual-use car-park fans state the hardwired fire-mode priority, and the BMS is read-only in fire mode (G11-4); "Something's wrong" on a flagged asset sends a note and changes no flag; no action clears a flag under v1.5. Demo line (GS-1). Life-safety signals read from IFC models (ifc-input 4.4) are E-IFC's, gated by ifc-input 6.2.12 (D-56).
- **Until decided:** No type candidate is created while no approved taxonomy version exists: each asset's type reads Unknown under SOVITECH will check (US-ASSETS-02 AC9). Points read "Not available yet", naming the missing point template, with the item under SOVITECH will check (US-ASSETS-09 AC8). `lifeSafety` is still set from membership of a system rule 11 lists and from dual use a document shows (US-ASSETS-10 AC2, AC9); flags by type wait for the approved taxonomy.
- **Acceptance:** US-ASSETS-02 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9, AC10; US-ASSETS-09 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9, AC10, AC11, AC12; US-ASSETS-10 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9
- **Sources:** docs/product/user-stories.md E-ASSETS (US-ASSETS-02, US-ASSETS-09, US-ASSETS-10); guardrails 2.5, 2.8, rules 1, 3, 9 and 11; design/dashboards-spec.md 7.1 rows 7.1-r16 ("05 asset types and plant on floor ..."), 7.1-r19 ("06, 05, 08, 10 life-safety scope"); 7.1.1 rows 7.1.1-C3 ("17's "Points ..."), 7.1.1-L2 ("Life-safety parts inside other systems ..."); docs/build-readiness.md 4 (point templates, asset taxonomy with lifeSafety flags, glossary review) and 5 (decisions 1 and 6); traceability.md 10.2 conflict 4, 10.3 near misses 8 and 33. ### E-TOPO: System topology

System topology shows how the building's documented systems and their equipment relate (`docs/product/user-stories.md` E-TOPO). It covers Topology's Logical view (DB-08), the system panels of the 3D topology (DB-07), the 2D floor plan with system layers (DB-10, on the per-level plans of UD-04), the system drawings and supplier lines on System Scope (DB-16, with DB-06 folded in as proposed), Topology's view modes and System Scope's view-mode control (UD-31). Under guardrails v1.5 it shows the systems the owner put in scope and the assets the registers hold for them, protocols only where a document names them, fire as a separate monitored system, and one supplier label per line. The system overlays on the model and the system layers on the plan (US-TOPO-02, US-TOPO-09) wait for values read from a model and for the geometry proposals (R-075); what Topology leaves out meanwhile holds from its first build (R-071). SOVITECH's proposed design and vendor names wait for proposals and are listed under "Waiting on approval". Asset rows and asset detail are E-ASSETS, zones E-ZONES, scope decisions and System Scope's list and detail panel E-SCOPE, the level register, the model view and the per-level plans E-MODEL, and every live element E-OPS.

#### R-071 Logical view and system details from the registers

- **Epic:** E-TOPO · **Stories:** US-TOPO-01, US-TOPO-03, US-TOPO-06, US-TOPO-04, US-TOPO-02, US-TOPO-09 · **Functions:** F-VIEWER-05, F-VALUE-10, F-VALUE-12, F-VALUE-14, F-CALC-04, F-CALC-08, F-REGISTRY-08, F-EXTRACT-06, F-PROPOSAL-06, F-RENDER-01, F-RENDER-03, F-RENDER-05, F-RENDER-09 · **Screens:** DB-08, DB-07, DB-10
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (rule 2, 2.5; 7.1-r2 ("All values")) · Required by guardrails (rule 2, 2.5, 4, 8; 7.1-r9 ("All counts …")) · Required by guardrails (rule 1, 8, 11; 7.1-r12 ("03, 07, 08 protocols")) · Required by guardrails (rule 1, 12; 7.1-r27 ("All (L) values")) · Required by guardrails (rule 8, 4; 7.1-r8 ("Floor lists, stacks, cost groups")) · Required by guardrails (rule 10; 7.1-r1 ("All screens")) · Owner decision 2026-09-24 (OD-3: "treat the app as our brand tool") · From approved design
- **Gated by:** none
- **Priority:** Should (proposed) · **Slice:** S3
- **Requirement:** The app shows Topology's Logical view as one group per system whose recorded scope decision is include, each listing that system's documented assets from the asset register as Calculated counts by asset type, with the page's system and level filters applied as register queries. A system chosen in SYSTEM DETAILS shows its field devices, its zones and its FIELD DEVICES list through the same register queries that System Scope and Equipment use, and an asset's interface shows a protocol only where a document names it. Nothing of SOVITECH's proposed design (controllers, automation stations, management-level servers, clients and applications, networks, buses, integration lists, data flow), nothing drawn on a model or a plan, and no live element is built on DB-07, DB-08 or DB-10.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** Counts are badged Calculated, broken down by asset type, with "Provisional: depends on <n> equipment items not yet checked" while any input is provisional (2.8). A system in scope with no asset found reads "Not found in the analysed documents (<coverage>)", never zero, "none" or an empty group (rule 12). Each group shows its scope decision with the same badge (Provided by you) and source line as System Scope (G2-7); a Suggested preselection not yet accepted adds no group. Each asset type shows one 2.8 badge: Two values, Unknown, Likely, Possible or SOVITECH will check, and Verified by SOVITECH once an engineer verifies it. A protocol named without its variant shows the variant as Unknown; "compatibil BMS" or "BMS ready" is kept as written, with the protocol Unknown under SOVITECH will check and no integration points (G1-6); a volt-free contact shows as hardwired I/O; nothing reads "Other"; a protocol count counts only distinct documented protocols from the registered list and never a transport such as HTTPS. No status word outside the 2.8 lists appears ("Planned", "In Progress" and "Under Review" are not used). With no include decision recorded, the view reads "Not available yet", naming the systems in scope, with the action to choose them (rule 7). No STATISTICS panel, "SYSTEM VIEW ● Live" bar, transport controls or "BMS LIVE" chip is built (7.1-r27). While the overlays and the level join wait (R-075, R-081), Topology draws no system riser, device icon, pin or system colour on any model, offers no 3D or plan mode, builds no SYSTEM LAYERS panel on any plan, opens no pin, routing line, popover or ELEMENT DETAILS from a plan, and builds no model thumbnail, floor caption or "Isolate System" button; the systems in scope and their documented equipment stay available in the Logical view. #### R-072 Fire as a separate monitored system, and one supplier label per line

- **Epic:** E-TOPO · **Stories:** US-TOPO-05, US-TOPO-07, US-TOPO-08 · **Functions:** F-VIEWER-05, F-VALUE-10, F-VALUE-12, F-VALUE-13, F-VALUE-14, F-CALC-08, F-REGISTRY-08, F-PRICE-02, F-QUESTION-07, F-RENDER-01, F-RENDER-05 · **Screens:** DB-06, DB-07, DB-08, DB-10, DB-16
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (rule 11; 7.1-r18 ("07, 08 fire topology")) · Required by guardrails (rule 11; 7.1.1-L4 ("16's fire riser drawn joining Water")) · Required by guardrails (rule 10; 7.1-r22 ("06, 08 supply split")) · Required by guardrails (rule 1, 10; 7.1-r21 ("06, 07 vendor names …")) · Required by guardrails (rule 10; 7.1-r1 ("All screens")) · From approved design
- **Gated by:** none
- **Priority:** Must (proposed) · **Slice:** S2
- **Requirement:** Wherever System Scope or a topology view groups devices by system or draws systems, the app draws Fire Safety as its own system with a one-way monitoring link to the BMS, places fire dampers, smoke detectors and fire alarm panels in the fire system's group, and shows the fire-alarm input and the fire-mode status among each affected panel's points, also when Fire Safety's recorded decision is exclude. Every line or system group that names who supplies it shows its supply-split field's value through the value component, the same on every page, or Unknown with an open item. No vendor, maker or brand name is shown beside an integration, a third-party system or a scope line, and no vendor slot is built.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** The fire system carries "monitoring only (read-only); fire logic and fire-mode interlocks remain in the fire system" (7.1-r18). A link that touches a life-safety asset or the fire system runs only in the monitoring direction and is never labelled or styled as a control command; a selected life-safety asset or the fire system shows only view, log and documents, never command, reset, inhibit, delay or override (rule 11). The fire riser never joins Water, HVAC or any other system's riser or icon (7.1.1-L4). A car-park fan that a PDF or XLSX document shows serving both car-park ventilation and smoke extraction is drawn as life-safety equipment, with the hardwired fire-mode priority stated and the BMS read-only in fire mode (G11-4). The fire points stay in whatever the scope decision (G11-3, G10-7). Room control with an unknown supplier names no supplier and shows the room points as a range over the SOVITECH-supplied and GRMS-integrated options, with an open item; room controllers are never counted from rooms (G10-6). Nothing is labelled "Third Party", "Utility", "SAUTER" or "SOVITECH" by assumption (rule 10). A changed supply split shows the new label on every page, and dependent estimates read "Out of date, recalculating" until they are recalculated (2.4; G2-7). The demo project shows "Demo data, not an assessment of the real building" (GS-1). Test ids: G11-3, G11-4, G10-6, G10-7, G2-7, GS-1.

- **Sources:** `docs/product/user-stories.md` US-TOPO-05, US-TOPO-07, US-TOPO-08 (its gates-closed criterion AC1 only; the vendor field is under "Waiting on approval"). US-TOPO-08 is a Later story placed here for AC1 only, as an S2 part; its gate (proposal 7.2.7) applies to the vendor field, not to this absence. `design/dashboards-spec.md` 7.1 rows 7.1-r18 ("07, 08 fire topology"), 7.1-r19 ("06, 05, 08, 10 life-safety scope"), 7.1-r21 ("06, 07 vendor names …"), 7.1-r22 ("06, 08 supply split"), 7.1.1 row 7.1.1-L4 ("16's fire riser drawn joining Water"); `docs/guardrails.md` rule 10 (stage 2 "also states who supplies what"), rule 11, 2.4; `docs/product/functions.md` F-VIEWER-05, F-VALUE-13, F-CALC-08, F-PRICE-02. #### R-075 System overlays on the model and system layers on per-level plans

- **Gated by:** Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.1 (not approved; D-38) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.2 (not approved; D-39) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.3 (not approved; D-40) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.10 (not approved; D-37) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.4 (not approved; D-41) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.8 (not approved; D-43) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.9 (not approved; D-42) · Depends on proposal 7.2.8 (not approved; D-45) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.15 (not approved; D-46) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 4 (D-01) · Blocked by open question onboarding Q3 and dashboards 8.5 (D-03) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 3 (D-04) · Blocked by open question ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3 (D-92)
- **Priority:** Could (proposed) · **Slice:** Later
- **Requirement:** Once values read from a stored IFC model can be stored and joined to the registers, the app draws the systems in scope on Topology's model view (DB-07) as risers by level with device icons at register assets' locations, and on each level's plan on DB-10 (UD-04) as system layers with pins; on DB-10 a SYSTEM LAYERS panel toggles what is drawn (DB-07's SYSTEM LAYERS panel, whose Management, Automation and Third-Party layers are SOVITECH's proposed design, also waits for proposal 7.2.10, D-65), and a pin's popover opens the asset's detail (UD-08). The system membership, containment and placements written in the file are read on the server by a deterministic, table-first extractor through approved mapping tables (ifc-input 6.2.10; 6.3.1 items 2 and 3), with the AI used only for what a table cannot map (ifc-input 4.1, 6.3.1 item 4), and stored as `document` candidates with the IFC locator: the file hash as `Evidence.contentHash`, the IFC schema as document metadata (`model.schema`, ifc-input 6.2.2), the entity GlobalId, the STEP instance ids and the attribute, property-set or quantity-set path (including through the type object) as the proposed `Evidence.locator.ifc` (ifc-input 6.2.1), and the verbatim STEP text as the excerpt (ifc-input 4.1 item 3). Every name, label or count shown with a view is a page element bound to a register value, and nothing is drawn as text in a 3D scene, a texture or a plan image.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** Values written in the file are `document`; counts from the asset register are `calculated` by the engine. Routing lines traced through port networks would be computed from the model's shapes and wait for proposal ifc-input 6.2.7 (not approved; D-50); they are not part of this requirement. An asset type from an IFC class is always an inference, never `document` (ifc-input 4.1, 4.3; as G3-1 treats a schedule row), capped by rule 3, and a class lookup made by code follows proposal ifc-input 6.2.9, a gate of this requirement, because 2.1 defines `ai_inference` as derived by the AI. The fire system is drawn as its own riser and layer with a one-way monitoring link and never joins Water, HVAC or any other system's riser or icon; fire assets on the plan are drawn as monitored only and allow only view, log and documents (rule 11; 7.1-r18; 7.1.1-L4). Under proposal ifc-input 6.2.12 (not approved; D-56) any life-safety signal in the model (ifc-input 4.4) would set the flag and only an engineer would clear it; meanwhile nothing clears a flag. Level labels on the canvas are the register's generated labels, as page elements bound to the level (G2-1); a count or device total shown with a view is a register query bound to a value id, nothing is counted from the view, and untagged model objects are never counted (rule 2; 2.5). No direction word, compass or north mark appears without a stored value that gives the orientation (rule 1). ELEMENT DETAILS shows the tag as written, the type with its single 2.8 badge (Two values while the type is in conflict, Unknown while no type is stored; otherwise Likely, Possible or SOVITECH will check until an engineer verifies it, then Verified by SOVITECH), the location with the level's register label and its room or zone from the register, and the points broken down by type as an Estimated range (G9-3); no Status, Last Update, Alarms tab, "Open in BMS →" or "BMS Live · Last sync" footer is built (7.1-r27). Toggling a layer and "View Details →" write no decision, candidate or event (rule 3), and the SYSTEM LAYERS ⓘ never holds the only copy of a label, range, basis, source or open-items count (2.8). The demo project shows "Demo data, not an assessment of the real building" (GS-1). Test ids: G2-1, G9-3, GS-1.
- **Until decided:** The v1.5 behaviour: the app stores the IFC file with its `DocumentRecord` and shows "Not analysed: IFC model stored, not analysed", the 2.8 status line naming the format as G12-1 names RVT. No value read from a model is stored, so no system riser, device icon, pin or system colour is drawn on any model, Topology offers no 3D or plan mode, no SYSTEM LAYERS panel is built on any plan, and no pin, routing line, popover or ELEMENT DETAILS panel opens from a plan; the systems in scope and their documented equipment stay available in the Logical view, which carries these absences from its first build (R-071). Code may record what the model contains as coverage for the engineer's view only (E-IFC), and no "not found" statement counts a model whose values cannot be kept (rule 12; G12-4).
- **Acceptance:** US-TOPO-02 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8; US-TOPO-09 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9

### E-MODEL: Building model and levels

The building model and its levels (`docs/product/user-stories.md` E-MODEL): the level register behind every floor list, filter, stack and level label; per-floor figures and their honest gaps; the view of a stored IFC model on step 3 (OB-3), on DB-01, on DB-02's canvas, in DB-13's building panel and on System Scope's canvas (DB-16), with its no-model state (UD-46) and its view modes; what model areas, views and plan pages leave out while no value read from a model can be stored; the parts that need those values or the geometry proposals (floor isolation joined to the register, pins and orientation, object selection, and the per-level plans of DB-10, DB-17 and DB-20 on UD-04); DB-01's floor inspector; DB-13's panel modes; and the signage around the model. Under guardrails v1.5 a model view is a view of a document, and a stored IFC model is never read for values. Storing, reading and converting models are E-IFC and E-DOCS, step 3's value rows E-REVIEW, zones E-ZONES, asset rows and detail E-ASSETS, DB-13's figures E-FIN, the system overlays and layers on models and plans E-TOPO (R-075), and live content E-OPS.
