#### R-078 A view of the stored IFC model, and its no-model state

- **Epic:** E-MODEL · **Stories:** US-MODEL-04, US-MODEL-05 · **Functions:** F-VIEWER-01, F-IFC-10, F-AUTH-03, F-INGEST-02, F-INGEST-03, F-INGEST-07, F-INGEST-08, F-QUESTION-09, F-RENDER-05, F-RENDER-06 · **Screens:** OB-3, DB-01, DB-02, DB-13, DB-16, UD-46
- **Status:** Owner decision 2026-09-24 (OD-8: "based on data from the onboarding flow, based on IFC files from BIM softwares") · Owner decision 2026-09-24 (OD-5: "no") · Required by guardrails (rule 2, 13, 2.3) · Required by guardrails (rule 7) · Required by guardrails (rule 10; 7.1-r1 ("All screens")) · From approved design
- **Gated by:** Blocked by open question onboarding Q3 and dashboards 8.5 (D-03) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 3 (D-04) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 4 (D-01)
- **Priority:** Should (proposed) · **Slice:** S2
- **Requirement:** When the project has a stored IFC model with converted viewing files, the app shows it in 3D on step 3 and in the model areas of the workspace pages, naming the model document it shows with that document's stage and revision as recorded, and showing only models that no declared revision supersedes and that are neither withdrawn nor erased. The view is a view of a document: it is never a source of values, nothing in it can be selected or highlighted, and nothing is drawn as text in its scene or textures. With no viewable model, the model area reads "Not available yet", naming what is missing (no IFC model, a model still being prepared, or a model that could not be converted), with the action to upload a model, or another export when the conversion failed.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** The four conditions under which v1.5 allows a stored model to be shown as a document (`docs/dev-prompts/02-prd.md`, "Model views") hold: the viewing files are keyed by project id plus content hash and served only after the project access check (rule 13, "Isolation"; G13-4); the erasure job removes them with their document, a stricter build choice than rule 13's list that adds no question, gate or owner-facing wording (proposal ifc-input 6.2.16, not approved, would make it a rule; D-89); nothing is drawn as text in the scene, in textures or in plan images, and every label, count or area beside the view is a bound value, under v1.5 none read from the model (rule 2; G2-1); the view names its document with its stage and revision as recorded, and a stage never recorded reads unknown (2.3). No model reads as analysed because it is shown: the stored file keeps its `DocumentRecord` and the 2.8 status line "Not analysed: IFC model stored, not analysed", in the form G12-1 uses for RVT (E-IFC). No owner screen shows a model-contents line, a model-check result, a count or a task about the model, and no copy about a model contains a reserved term outside the places 2.8 allows (the general form of ifc-input 5.4 IFC-14, proposed, not indexed, needs no stored model value; its own situation, an IDS report, waits for new Q15 (D-36), and an owner-facing model-check line for ifc-input 6.2.14 (D-73)); the count wording of `docs/ifc-input.md` 4.5 is proposal ifc-input 6.2.14 and is not used. With only RVT or DWG files, the area shows the no-model state and each file keeps its 2.8 status line (G12-1). No illustrative, generic or mockup model is drawn in place of a missing model, and no signage, brand name or logo text is drawn on any building (R-080; rule 2). What only values read from a model supply is left out, as R-080 states: no single storey isolated, no floor selector beside the view on OB-3, no level label on the geometry, no pin, highlight, zone fill, scale bar, compass or "From a superseded revision" label, no selection and no plan mode. A view still loading, or files missing, never blocks Continue, Generate or any other control, and a model that becomes viewable later opens no dialog and changes nothing the owner entered (rule 7). On the demo project the view shows the synthetic fixture model from the repo with "Demo data, not an assessment of the real building", and the real hotel's name appears nowhere on the page (OD-5; GS-1). Test ids: G2-1, G13-4, G12-1, GS-1.
- **Until decided:** No model view is built: whether and when a viewer is built is open (onboarding Q3, dashboards 8.5, build-readiness decisions 3 and 4), and `docs/build-readiness.md` 3 ("Now" item 10) recommends no 3D on step 3 in the first slice. The pages that draw a model area render without it, and never draw an illustrative, generic or mockup model in its place (US-MODEL-05 AC2; R-080). A stored IFC model keeps its `DocumentRecord` and its "Not analysed: IFC model stored, not analysed" line (E-IFC).
- **Acceptance:** US-MODEL-04 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9, AC10, AC11; US-MODEL-05 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7
- **Sources:** `docs/product/user-stories.md` US-MODEL-04, US-MODEL-05; `docs/dev-prompts/02-prd.md` "Model views"; `docs/ifc-input.md` 2.2 (tooling, recommended, not decided; a spike settles it), 2.3 (licences, counsel before release), 5.2 and 5.3 (the synthetic fixture), 6.1 ("Isolation", "Display"), 6.2.15, 6.2.16, 6.3.2; `docs/guardrails.md` rules 2, 7, 12 and 13, 2.3, 2.8; `design/onboarding-spec.md` 3 (Step 3), 7 (Q3); `design/dashboards-spec.md` 7.1 row 7.1-r1 ("All screens"). Converting, keying and erasing the viewing files belong to E-IFC (US-IFC-08, F-IFC-10). What to show with no IFC model is open (D-03); under v1.5 only "Not available yet" is allowed, because an illustrative model needs proposal 7.2.8. Several models together or one at a time is D-03; the demo model is the synthetic fixture and will not look like the mockups' tower (D-18). The export guide for the owner's designer is D-36. The view modes wait also for the navigation question and are R-079; that gate (D-02) is not in the Status of US-MODEL-04 or US-MODEL-05. The gates-closed criteria of US-MODEL-07 to US-MODEL-10 and the absences of US-MODEL-13 are in R-080, because those stories do not share this requirement's gates. US-MODEL-04 AC6 tags "(rule 13)" on a behaviour stricter than rule 13's list; it is kept because the "Model views" conditions require the behaviour.

#### R-081 Floor isolation and level labels joined to the model

- **Epic:** E-MODEL · **Stories:** US-MODEL-07 · **Functions:** F-VIEWER-01, F-VIEWER-02, F-VIEWER-03, F-IFC-03, F-IFC-06, F-VALUE-11, F-RENDER-06 · **Screens:** OB-3, DB-01, DB-07, DB-10, DB-13, DB-16, DB-17, UD-04
- **Status:** Owner decision 2026-09-24 (OD-8: "based on data from the onboarding flow, based on IFC files from BIM softwares") · Required by guardrails (rule 8, 2.2; 7.1.1-E4 ("Level labels …")) · From approved design
- **Gated by:** Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.1 (not approved; D-38) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.2 (not approved; D-39) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.3 (not approved; D-40) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.10 (not approved; D-37) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.4 (not approved; D-41) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.8 (not approved; D-43) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.9 (not approved; D-42) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 4 (D-01) · Blocked by open question onboarding Q3 and dashboards 8.5 (D-03) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 3 (D-04) · Blocked by open question ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3 (D-92)
- **Priority:** Could (proposed) · **Slice:** Later
- **Requirement:** Once values read from a stored IFC model can be stored, the app joins the model's storeys to the level register: a level chosen from the register isolates its storey on the model views (step 3's floor selector, DB-01, DB-07, DB-13 and DB-16, and the building drawing beside DB-17's floor stack select), with the register's generated labels shown as page elements bound to the level. The storey names and elevations and the containment written in the file are read on the server by a deterministic, table-first extractor through approved mapping tables (ifc-input 6.2.10; 6.3.1 items 2 and 3), with the AI used only for what a table cannot map (ifc-input 4.1, 6.3.1 item 4), and stored as `document` candidates with the IFC locator: the file hash as `Evidence.contentHash`, the IFC schema as document metadata (`model.schema`, ifc-input 6.2.2), the entity GlobalId, the STEP instance ids and the attribute, property-set or quantity-set path (including through the type object) as the proposed `Evidence.locator.ifc` (ifc-input 6.2.1), and the verbatim STEP text as the excerpt (ifc-input 4.1 item 3). A storey adds level evidence to the register (ifc-input 4.2 "Levels"); it never establishes a level or a floor count by itself.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** Values written in the file are `document`; sums, counts from the register and 2.1's "exact unit conversions" over stored candidates (an elevation converted to metres, for example) are `calculated` by the engine. Quantities computed from the model's shapes (containment found by geometry, for example) wait for proposal ifc-input 6.2.7 (not approved; D-50) and are not part of this requirement. Interpretations are `ai_inference`, capped by rule 3, and a level type inferred by code from a storey name follows proposal ifc-input 6.2.9, a gate of this requirement, because 2.1 defines `ai_inference` as derived by the AI. A storey count never establishes a floor count: floor counts stay the register's counts by level type, with the regim de înălțime first (rule 8; ifc-input 5.4 IFC-4, proposed, not indexed, waits for ifc-input 6.2.8 with the minimum set (ifc-input 6.2.1, 6.2.2, 6.2.3 and 6.2.10), and for ifc-input 6.2.9 where code types the level). Storeys of different models are matched only as proposal ifc-input 6.2.4 defines. Level labels with a model view are the register's generated labels, as page elements bound to the level (G2-1), and nothing is drawn as text in a 3D scene or a texture. Model text is never shown as a value, and model text that addresses the reader changes no state (rule 14). A register level with no storey in the model reads "Not available yet", naming the level missing from the model, with an action to upload a model that covers it (rule 7). The demo project shows "Demo data, not an assessment of the real building" (GS-1). Test ids: G2-1, GS-1.
- **Until decided:** The v1.5 behaviour: the app stores the IFC file with its `DocumentRecord` and shows "Not analysed: IFC model stored, not analysed", the 2.8 status line naming the format as G12-1 names RVT. No value read from a model is stored, so no storey is isolated, lifted or labelled on its own, no floor selector is built beside the view on OB-3, no level label, function or number is attached to the geometry, and the register takes no level, level name or floor count from the model's storeys; levels stay available through the register lists (R-077), and these absences hold from S2 (R-080). Code may record what the model contains as coverage for the engineer's view only (E-IFC), and no "not found" statement counts a model whose values cannot be kept (rule 12; G12-4).
- **Acceptance:** US-MODEL-07 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8
- **Sources:** `docs/product/user-stories.md` US-MODEL-07; `docs/ifc-input.md` 4.1, 4.2 ("Levels"), 5.4, 6.1, 6.2.1 to 6.2.4, 6.2.7 to 6.2.10, 6.3.1 items 2 to 4, 6.3.2 ("What the direction settles", which under v1.5 waits for these proposals: traceability 10.2 item 18, 10.3 near miss 28); `docs/dev-prompts/02-prd.md` "How the PRD applies the contract" (the locator), "For E-IFC and E-MODEL"; `design/dashboards-spec.md` 7.1.1 row 7.1.1-E4 ("Level labels …"); `docs/product/functions.md` F-IFC-03, F-IFC-06, F-VIEWER-03. The gates-closed criteria (AC1 to AC4) also stand in R-080, which holds them from S2. The per-level plans on DB-10, DB-17 and DB-20 that this join enables are R-084. The demo floor structure is open (D-18). The ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3 gate is the PRD's: prompt 2 gates every stored IFC value on the approved mapping tables (ifc-input 6.3.1 items 2 and 3), which need the SOVITECH asset taxonomy with its life-safety flags; item 2, the approver, is implied by the proposal gates. OD-8 is added to the Status because this capability shows or reads the owner's IFC models (the IFC direction of 2026-09-24); US-MODEL-07 does not carry it.

Zone fills and zone polygons also wait for proposal 7.2.28 (not approved; D-68) and are not part of this requirement. No signage, brand name or logo text is drawn on a model (7.1-note). The demo project shows "Demo data, not an assessment of the real building" (GS-1). Test ids: G2-1, GS-1.

These absences hold from S2 (R-080). Code may record what the model contains as coverage for the engineer's view only (E-IFC), and no "not found" statement counts a model whose values cannot be kept (rule 12; G12-4).

### E-FIN: Metrics

The Metrics pages as the owner sees them in the proposal phase: Financial Overview (DB-02), CAPEX (DB-13), OPEX & Savings (DB-12), Payback Analysis (DB-21) and Lifecycle Analysis (DB-22), with the Metrics navigation and its undesigned landing (UD-03) and the controls whose targets are undefined (UD-23, UD-24, UD-25). Under guardrails v1.5 the unit registry has no unit for durations, currency ratios or CO₂ (dashboards-spec 7.1.1 "Missing units come first"), so the pages built first show the investment through the price component, the building's operating cost from its bills, counts from the register and "Not available yet" lines that name what is missing. Savings, return indicators, the cash-flow charts, the key assumptions, CO₂, lifecycle cost, the savings opportunities, the cost callouts on the model and the automation levels are gated requirements, each with its own gates. Phasing (DB-11), Scenarios (DB-19), packages, the scenario bar and the monthly series wait for approval. How the estimate is computed is E-PROPOSAL; exports are E-REPORTS; the quotation record is E-ENGINEER; live content is E-OPS.

ANNUAL SAVINGS and the savings rows, the BMS operating cost row and the ANNUAL CASH FLOW panel each read "Not available yet", naming what is missing; no ROI caption is shown while no ROI formula is registered, and no VALUE DRIVERS panel while no savings estimate exists. The scenario bar and time scale, the "By Phase" tab, the CAPEX / OPEX toggle, the cost callouts on the model and every live value are not built.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** No "BMS LIVE" chip, live status or other live value (7.1-r27). "Not available yet" names what is missing and is never an empty card, a dash or a zero (rule 7); "add energy bills" is offered only where the project can have bills and bills are among the missing inputs, and no "<n>% vs. baseline" caption is shown (7.1-r4). The row the mockup calls "Annual OPEX (BMS)" is labelled "BMS operating cost", never "OPEX" alone (7.1.1-S8). Every value goes through the value or price component, with its badge on the same line and its source line below it (7.1.1-E5). No chart is drawn without a payback (7.1-r5). The demo line "Demo data, not an assessment of the real building" on the page of the demo project (7.1.1-E1; GS-1).
- **Acceptance:** US-FIN-01 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9, AC10

#### R-090 Investment figures and priced lines on Metrics pages

- **Epic:** E-FIN · **Stories:** US-FIN-03, US-FIN-07 · **Functions:** F-CALC-03, F-PRICE-01, F-PRICE-02, F-PRICE-05, F-PRICE-06, F-QUESTION-07, F-REGISTRY-06, F-RENDER-02, F-RENDER-04 · **Screens:** DB-02, DB-11, DB-13, DB-19, DB-21, DB-22
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (rules 1, 7, 8, 9, 10, 2.8; 7.1-r2, 7.1-r3, 7.1.1-P1, 7.1.1-P2, 7.1.1-P6, 7.1.1-P7) · From approved design
- **Gated by:** none
- **Priority:** Should (proposed) · **Slice:** S2
- **Requirement:** On every Metrics page, each investment figure goes through the price component: a range labelled with its stage read from stored records ("Preliminary investment estimate", or "Indicative range" where the registry allows one and an approved dataset version for it exists), rounded outward, with its VAT basis, price date and price-list version, its basis, provisional inputs, exclusions and open items; where no figure can be computed it reads "Not available yet", naming the missing item, with an Add action where the item is an owner input. Every priced line names the supplier of each item rule 10 lists, with a range over both supply options and an open item while a split is unknown; third-party plant that SOVITECH does not supply is not priced as BMS scope; a price comes only from the versioned price list or an approved dataset, never from a figure typed on a screen; and a SAUTER product is named only as a catalogue token from an approved catalogue version.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** No "Formal quotation" and no reserved pricing term (quote, quotation, offer, ofertă, deviz) without a stored quotation record (G10-1); "Superseded: inputs changed on <date>" when a quotation record's inputs changed, with the figures back to the "Preliminary investment estimate" label (G10-2); the BNR rate and its date on RON figures, and no rate from the AI (G10-4). The same option with the same filter shows the identical figure, badge, range and rounding from one snapshot on every page (G2-7). "Incomplete: excludes <item names>" with the same prominence as the figure (rule 1). Open items counted as rule 7 requires ("<n> things for you to check", with SOVITECH will check as one line per group; G7-5). Ranges round outward and never narrow (rule 9); no count-up (G2-8). No product named from a dataset without an approval record, such as the product list in company/products/ (G1-12). Never an empty card, a dash or a zero (rule 7).
- **Acceptance:** US-FIN-03 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9, AC10, AC11; US-FIN-07 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6

#### R-091 Breakdowns, shares and excluded systems on Metrics pages

- **Epic:** E-FIN · **Stories:** US-FIN-05, US-FIN-08 · **Functions:** F-CALC-03, F-CALC-08, F-CALC-09, F-CALC-10, F-CALC-11, F-PRICE-02, F-PRICE-03, F-RENDER-01, F-RENDER-07, F-VALUE-12 · **Screens:** DB-02, DB-11, DB-12, DB-13, DB-21, DB-22

- **Priority:** Should (proposed) · **Slice:** S2
- **Requirement:** Every cost breakdown on the Metrics pages comes from the same snapshot as the total beside it. Each share names what it is a share of, is a range or is left out when the amounts are ranges, and is never computed from an unknown part or an "Incomplete" total; an unknown part is a labelled gap, and a cost line with no known system is named as such, so no group is made smaller silently. A system whose recorded scope decision is exclude contributes no cost, savings, operating-cost or lifecycle line on any Metrics page and is listed among the estimate's exclusions, while the fire interface points stay in the point list; every page renders the same recorded decision per system with its badge.

The scope renders identically on every page (7.1.1-C7; G2-7). That the parts of a breakdown must sum to their total is proposal 7.2.14 (D-82), not a v1.5 rule, and is not part of this requirement. Shares from ranges have no section 7 case yet (traceability 10.3 item 36).

#### R-095 OPEX & Savings: the building's operating cost

- **Epic:** E-FIN · **Stories:** US-FIN-12, US-FIN-13, US-FIN-14 · **Functions:** F-CALC-03, F-CALC-06, F-CALC-07, F-CALC-09, F-EXTRACT-09, F-INGEST-05, F-PRICE-06, F-QUESTION-01, F-REGISTRY-01, F-REGISTRY-06, F-RENDER-01, F-RENDER-05, F-RENDER-09, F-VALUE-14 · **Screens:** DB-12
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (rules 1, 6, 7, 8, 12; 7.1-r4, 7.1-r27, 7.1.1-D13, 7.1.1-E1, 7.1.1-E2, 7.1.1-E3, 7.1.1-P3, 7.1.1-P4, 7.1.1-S5, 7.1.1-S6, 7.1.1-S7, 7.1.1-S8) · From approved design
- **Gated by:** Blocked by open question new Q27 and build-readiness decision 10 (D-27)
- **Priority:** Should (proposed) · **Slice:** S3
- **Requirement:** The app builds OPEX & Savings (DB-12) with the building's operating cost before any BMS. Energy cost comes only from uploaded bills, per carrier, metering point, period and reading type, with annual totals calculated from non-overlapping billing periods of one metering point; maintenance, staff and other costs are Unknown unless a document states them, and the owner is asked nothing new about them; a system's current cost is shown only where a document attributes metered or billed energy to it, and a building total is never split across systems by a typical ratio. The total, OPEX INTENSITY and the breakdown shares are computed only from a complete total, and the intensity reads "Not available yet", naming the missing unit, while no unit for cost per m² per year exists. MONTHLY OPEX TREND, the ENERGY COST BREAKDOWN chart, the "Last <n> Months" selector, TOP SAVINGS OPPORTUNITIES and its "View" buttons, the ⓘ on OPEX BREAKDOWN, the scenario bar, any achieved saving or delta against a baseline or a previous year, any benchmark comparison, every live value and any project status are not built; every total states the billing periods it covers.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** "Building operating cost" and "BMS operating cost" are two labels, and "OPEX" never stands alone as the label of either value; the page name "OPEX & Savings" stays (7.1.1-S8). Bills: a regularisation replaces the periods it corrects (G8-7); a sub-meter is never added to its parent (G8-8); a total with supplier-estimated readings reads as provisional; gas becomes energy only through the calorific value printed on the bill; a RON bill shown in EUR shows the BNR rate and its date (prompt 1's reading of rule 8, traceability 10.3 item 52), and while no approved BNR dataset version exists, the bill's RON amount is kept as written and not converted, and its EUR figure reads "Not available yet", naming the missing exchange rate (rules 1, 7, 8; G1-12). An existing building with no bills reads "Not available yet", naming the missing bills, with the upload action; new construction reads "Not available yet", naming what an estimate lacks, with no bill upload (7.1-r4). A carrier with no bill among the analysed documents reads "Not found in the analysed documents" with their coverage, never a zero (rule 12). Unknown or "Not provided yet" for costs no document states, never a typical value or a zero (rule 1); "Incomplete: excludes <item names>" with the same prominence as the figure, and no intensity or share from an incomplete total; shares name their base and come from the same snapshot as their amounts (G9-8). No "Market Benchmark" marker or "vs. similar buildings" comparison without an approved benchmark dataset (7.1.1-S7). No "BMS LIVE" chip, live footer, achieved saving or "Operational" status, and the page never calls its figures real-time (7.1.1-E2, 7.1.1-E3, 7.1.1-D13). The demo line on the page of the demo project (GS-1).
- **Until decided:** While new Q27 and build-readiness decision 10 are open (D-27, "Until decided"), no amount in EUR or RON per year is stored or computed: energy cost shows per billing period as the bills state it, with its carrier, metering point, period and reading type (US-FIN-13 AC1); every amount per year, the total, OPEX INTENSITY and the shares read "Not available yet", naming the open question on annual amounts, as R-087 treats a value with no registered unit; EUR is the only display currency, so a bill in RON is stored as written, is neither shown in RON nor converted, and its EUR figure reads "Not available yet", naming the missing exchange rate. The labels, the Unknown costs and the parts not built apply as written. Proposed (PRD interim, reversible).
- **Acceptance:** US-FIN-12 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9, AC10, AC11, AC12; US-FIN-13 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9, AC10; US-FIN-14 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6
- **Sources:** docs/product/user-stories.md US-FIN-12, US-FIN-13, US-FIN-14 (US-OPS-01, US-OPS-11 and US-OPS-13 are cited for the live chip and footer, the achieved savings and the project status not built here; they keep "Out of scope: operations phase" and slice Later, D-28); docs/guardrails.md rule 1, rule 6, rule 7, rule 8 ("Energy data", "Currency"), rule 12, 2.7; design/dashboards-spec.md 4 (screen 12), 5 ("Energy bills and building operating costs"), 7.1 rows 7.1-r4 ("02 savings"), 7.1-r27 ("All (L) values"), 7.1.1 rows 7.1.1-S5 ("12's energy cost and monthly series"), 7.1.1-S6 ("12's maintenance, staff and other costs; total OPEX; intensity"), 7.1.1-S7 ("12's \"Market Benchmark …"), 7.1.1-S8 ("\"OPEX\" meaning the building's …"), 7.1.1-P3 ("€/m² (13) and €/m²/year (12)"), 7.1.1-P4 ("Shares on 11, 12, 13, 21 and 22"), 7.1.1-D13 ("12's \"real-time\" framing and achieved savings"), 7.1.1-E2 ("\"BMS LIVE\" chip …"), 7.1.1-E3; docs/product/traceability.md 10.3 item 52. The parts not built wait under their own stories: the monthly series (US-FIN-15) and the scenario bar (US-FIN-11) under "Waiting on approval", with months as proposal 7.2.32 (D-72); the savings opportunities under R-106; the ⓘ under R-098. The gates are the PRD's: US-FIN-13 names storing annual amounts (new Q27) and the display currency (build-readiness decision 10) among its open questions, and their D row's interim keeps annual amounts in EUR or RON and RON display out (D-27, "Until decided"; traceability 10.2 conflict 34 names US-FIN-13). The stories' other open questions do not stop this requirement: asking for other operating costs (new Q31, D-07) and staff cost as personal data (proposal 7.2.6, D-60). The E-OPS stories behind the absences here are cited, not built: US-OPS-01, US-OPS-11, US-OPS-13 (they keep "Out of scope: operations phase" and slice Later).

#### R-099 Estimated energy savings in kWh/a

- **Epic:** E-FIN · **Stories:** US-FIN-32 · **Functions:** F-CALC-03, F-CALC-10, F-REGISTRY-06, F-RENDER-01 · **Screens:** DB-02, DB-13, DB-21, UD-06

- **Gated by:** Blocked by open question new Q29 (D-93) · Blocked by open question dashboards 8.6 (D-07) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 1 (D-05)
- **Priority:** Should (proposed) · **Slice:** Later
- **Requirement:** Once an approved savings-factor dataset version and a method exist, the app shows the energy the BMS could save, in kWh per year, as an Estimated range with its method, operating hours and a named baseline (its years, weather normalisation and occupancy), on the Metrics pages and in the proposal. A building with no operating history reads "Not available yet", naming the missing baseline, and no euro value is derived while no energy-price unit is registered.

A savings-factor version with no approval record feeds no candidate (section 10; near miss 33 in traceability 10.3). Excluded systems contribute no savings line (G10-7).
- **Until decided:** Every energy saving reads "Not available yet", naming the missing savings factors, and no savings candidate is created (US-FIN-32 AC1, AC2).

Buildings with no operating history get a baseline only through proposal 7.2.19 (D-62); until then they read "Not available yet", so 7.2.19 does not stop this requirement. Climate data for weather normalisation is new Q28 (D-93), among the story's open questions.

### E-PROPOSAL: Preliminary proposal

The preliminary proposal from "Generate Proposal" on step 8 (OB-8): the generating and failed states (UD-07, UD-47), the stored proposal with its snapshot and versions, and what the proposal shows (UD-06): its stage, points by type, the investment estimate, open items and the life-safety and compliance sentences generated from stored state. Under v1.5 the output is always a preliminary proposal. No screen or export shows the "Formal quotation" stage until a stored quotation record exists (G10-1); creating that record is E-ENGINEER's. The figures wait for SOVITECH's point templates and cost ranges with approval records, so S1 (proposed) builds the structure, the stage labels and the missing cases. AI-drafted prose waits for the AI processor route. The Overview page (UD-01) and CAPEX's stepper with its Review step (UD-05, UD-17) wait for open questions; SOVITECH's proposed design waits for approval.

#### R-109 Generate, the generating state and the failed state

- **Epic:** E-PROPOSAL · **Stories:** US-PROPOSAL-01, US-PROPOSAL-02 · **Functions:** F-PRICE-01, F-PROPOSAL-01, F-PROPOSAL-02, F-QUESTION-08, F-QUESTION-09, F-RENDER-05, F-RENDER-06 · **Screens:** OB-8, UD-07, UD-47
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (rules 2, 3, 7, 10; §5-8, §5-All) · From approved design
- **Gated by:** none
- **Priority:** Must (proposed) · **Slice:** S1 (proposed)
- **Requirement:** The app lets the owner press "Generate Proposal" on step 8 whenever they reach it, and shows a generating state that says the preliminary proposal is being prepared and shows no figure. When generation finishes, the owner is shown the result with its stage, its headline investment range or "Not available yet", and its open items; if generation fails, a failed state (UD-47) says the proposal could not be generated, keeps every answer and upload unchanged, and lets the owner return to step 8 and generate again. Generation writes no owner answer and accepts no suggestion from any step.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** Generate is never blocked by missing data or running analysis, and a late analysis result during generation opens no dialog and changes no answer (rule 7). A missing first-estimate input gives the "Indicative range" fallback where the registry allows one and an approved dataset version exists (G7-2a), otherwise "Not available yet" with the missing field and an Add action (G7-2b). "Preliminary investment estimate" as a range, and no reserved pricing term without a stored quotation record (G10-1). The generating state shows no figure, partial total or animated count (G2-8). The demo line on step 8 and on the generating state (§5-All; GS-1).
- **Acceptance:** US-PROPOSAL-01 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5; US-PROPOSAL-02 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5
- **Sources:** docs/product/user-stories.md US-PROPOSAL-01, US-PROPOSAL-02; docs/guardrails.md rule 3 ("A suggestion left in place counts as the owner's answer"), rule 7 ("Late findings never interrupt"), rule 10, 2.8, section 5 row §5-8 (step 8, "Generate Proposal", "Ready to generate") and row §5-All (all steps, the demo project); design/onboarding-spec.md 3 (step 8), 7 Q12; docs/product/traceability.md 1.3 (UD-47). The result is the stored proposal of R-111 (US-PROPOSAL-02 AC3); where the owner lands after generation is open (onboarding Q12, D-14; dashboards 8.3, D-02) and waits under R-116. The generating state's look follows the part 1 style until dashboards 8.10 (D-06) is answered. The first-estimate set is approver setting 3 (D-53). Step 8's summary cards, inline asks, Generate state, "Still reading" line and Proposal card are E-INTAKE (US-INTAKE-15 to US-INTAKE-17); its "For you" and "SOVITECH will check" lists are E-REVIEW.

#### R-110 The stored proposal: snapshot, changed inputs and new versions

- **Epic:** E-PROPOSAL · **Stories:** US-PROPOSAL-03, US-PROPOSAL-10, US-PROPOSAL-11 · **Functions:** F-CALC-02, F-CALC-03, F-INGEST-04, F-PRICE-05, F-PROPOSAL-01, F-PROPOSAL-02, F-RENDER-03, F-VALUE-01 · **Screens:** OB-8, UD-06
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (rules 4, 7, 9, 10, 2.4, 2.8) · From approved design
- **Gated by:** none
- **Priority:** Must (proposed) · **Slice:** S1 (proposed)
- **Requirement:** The app stores each generated proposal with the snapshot of candidate ids and formula versions it used and an inputs hash, and never mixes newer values into it. When an active candidate among its inputs changes, the stored proposal records that it is based on changed inputs (shown to the owner only through 2.8's lines on the affected figures, because a status line for a whole output is proposal 7.2.25, D-67), and each figure whose inputs changed reads "Out of date, recalculating" and is never shown as current. A new version, with its own snapshot and inputs hash and with the earlier version kept readable as generated, is stored only when the owner presses "Generate Proposal" again (from the step 8 inline ask that a "Not available yet" action opens) or when analysis that was still running at Generate finishes.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** Breakdown and total come from the snapshot id (G9-8); the same value shows identically on every surface (G2-7). "Out of date, recalculating" for a figure whose inputs changed (2.4, 2.8; proposal 7.2.25 would add another wording, D-67). "Superseded: inputs changed on <date>" when a quotation record rests on changed inputs, with the figures back to the "Preliminary investment estimate" label (G10-2). Changed inputs open no dialog and block nothing; generating again changes no answer the owner gave; the version stored when running analysis finishes keeps the notice "Still reading <n> files. Your estimate will update when they finish." true (rule 7). Earlier versions keep their snapshots (rule 4, 2.4).
- **Acceptance:** US-PROPOSAL-03 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4; US-PROPOSAL-10 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5; US-PROPOSAL-11 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6
- **Sources:** docs/product/user-stories.md US-PROPOSAL-03, US-PROPOSAL-10, US-PROPOSAL-11; docs/guardrails.md rule 4, rule 7 ("Late findings never interrupt"), rule 9, rule 10 ("A quotation goes stale when its inputs change"), 2.4 ("Recalculation"), 2.8; docs/product/traceability.md 10.2 item 38, 10.3 item 35. Whether the app regenerates by itself beyond the case rule 7 promises is open (onboarding Q12, D-14); other ways back to "Generate Proposal" are new Q6 (D-14); while those and dashboards 8.3 (D-02) are open, no back-to-intake entry is built after Generate (US-INTAKE-22). These are prompt 1's interims inside ungated stories (US-PROPOSAL-11 AC1, AC5), and the owner's answers replace them. A regenerate action beside the stored output is part of proposal 7.2.25; snapshot ids printed on exports are proposal 7.2.18 (D-87).

- **Requirement:** The proposal's life-safety and compliance sentences are generated from stored state, never by the AI. Fire Safety, when included, reads "monitoring only (read-only); fire logic and fire-mode interlocks remain in the fire system"; the fire-alarm input and fire-mode status per AHU panel stay in the points when Fire Safety is unchecked and AHUs are in scope with fire detection present; dual-use car-park fans state the hardwired fire-mode priority and that the BMS is read-only in fire mode; and what the BMS does with any life-safety system is described only as monitor, display, log and alarm. A BAC class reads "aims to support BAC class <x> (<standard and edition from reference data>)" before engineer verification, and the sentence "designed to provide the functions of BAC class <x>, verified by SOVITECH" is built only from an engineer verification record on a non-demo project. Whether a legal obligation applies "stays Unknown until the facts behind it are engineer-verified" (rule 11).
- **Guardrail behaviour:** Fire Safety as monitoring only (G11-1); interface points kept (G11-3); fire-mode priority stated (G11-4); "aims to support" before verification, and never a compliance claim (G11-6). Reserved terms appear only in the sentences the app builds from stored state, as 2.8 allows. Demo values never carry `engineer_verified`, so the sentence built from a verification record never appears on the demo project (rule 10). Standards and editions come from reference data, and a superseded standard is never cited as current (rule 11).
- **Acceptance:** US-PROPOSAL-13 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7
- **Sources:** docs/product/user-stories.md US-PROPOSAL-13; docs/guardrails.md rule 10 ("Demo data"), rule 11 ("Life-safety systems", "Compliance"), 2.8 (reserved terms); docs/build-readiness.md 5 decisions 6 (the function set, D-92) and 9 (the standard's edition, D-31), which are among the story's open questions and do not stop it.

#### R-114 Points and investment estimated from SOVITECH datasets

- **Epic:** E-PROPOSAL · **Stories:** US-PROPOSAL-07, US-PROPOSAL-09 · **Functions:** F-CALC-01, F-CALC-08, F-PRICE-02, F-PRICE-03, F-REGISTRY-06, F-REVIEW-01, F-REVIEW-03, F-VALUE-08, F-VALUE-13 · **Screens:** UD-06
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (rule 1, rule 9, rule 10, rule 11, 2.5; §5-8)
- **Gated by:** Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 6 (D-92) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 1 (D-05) · Blocked by open question new Q32 (D-47)
- **Priority:** Must (proposed) · **Slice:** S2
- **Requirement:** Once SOVITECH's point templates and cost ranges exist with approval records, the app estimates points per asset, by type and configuration, and CAPEX from points by type and the cost ranges, both as Estimated ranges with their basis, method, price date, VAT basis, currency, price-list version, supply split, exclusions and open items. A dataset version with no approval record feeds no estimate.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** Points from templates are `estimated`, never `calculated` (G9-4); a duty and standby group counts every pump, with points for every motor (G4-4); room points are a range over the SOVITECH-supplied and GRMS-integrated options with an open item (G10-6); fire-alarm input and fire-mode status per AHU panel stay in (G11-3); life-safety assets get status and alarm inputs only (rule 11); integration points without a register map, EDE file, PICS or point list are Estimated with the method named (rule 1); one physical point is counted once (2.5). CAPEX is always a range while any input is provisional; "Incomplete: excludes <item names>" with no headline, payback or ROI (G1-2); reuse and replacement as a range, with "Site survey needed" under SOVITECH will check (G1-7); a range over both supply options while a split is unknown (rule 10); excluded systems priced nowhere (G10-7); "Looks right" leaves the estimate provisional (G3-3); no reference candidate from an unapproved dataset (G1-12).
- **Until decided:** No point or CAPEX candidate is created, and the proposal shows the missing cases of R-112 (US-PROPOSAL-07 AC1; US-PROPOSAL-09 AC1). Proposed (PRD interim, reversible): the formulas may be built and tested on synthetic fixture templates and cost ranges in tests only, and no SOVITECH price table is committed to the repository (D-92).
- **Acceptance:** US-PROPOSAL-07 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9; US-PROPOSAL-09 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9
- **Sources:** docs/product/user-stories.md US-PROPOSAL-07, US-PROPOSAL-09; docs/guardrails.md 2.1, 2.5 ("Counting"), rule 1 ("Interfaces", "Reuse"), rule 9, rule 10 ("Stage 2 also states who supplies what"), rule 11, section 10; docs/build-readiness.md 3 "Now" item 8, 4 ("SOVITECH engineering datasets"), 5 decisions 1, 3 and 6; docs/product/traceability.md 10.2 item 4, 10.3 item 33, 10.4 new Q32. - **Epic:** E-PROPOSAL · **Stories:** US-PROPOSAL-12 · **Functions:** F-AUDIT-01, F-PROPOSAL-03, F-PROPOSAL-04, F-REGISTRY-05, F-RENDER-01 · **Screens:** UD-06

Anthropic API code starts from the `claude-api` skill (CLAUDE.md).
- **Until decided:** Drafting is built and evaluated on synthetic fixtures only (build-readiness 3 "Now" item 6), and for a project with real owner documents no document text is sent to an AI service (US-PROPOSAL-12 AC1). Proposed (PRD interim, reversible): on such a project the proposal carries no AI-drafted prose, only the sentences built from stored state.

### E-REPORTS: Reports and exports

Everything that leaves the app as a file, and the Reports page (DB-18): one export frame with the demo line; the preliminary proposal as a PDF from its snapshot with its appendix of sources and open items (UD-06, and "Download Proposal" on DB-13); the register of generated outputs; compliance-related report content; "Export Report" on Payback and Lifecycle Analysis (DB-21, DB-22); Export Scope (DB-06); and the undesigned generator, templates library and viewer (UD-12, UD-19, UD-20), with the bill of quantities. Where an export lands is undesigned (dashboards-spec 2.4.5; D-06). The appendix is required for exported proposals (2.8 "Prominence", G10-5); extending it to every export, and a lifecycle for generated outputs, is proposal 7.2.25. No export shows the "Formal quotation" stage until a stored quotation record exists (G10-1).

### E-ENGINEER: Engineer and commercial review

The work of the SOVITECH engineer and the SOVITECH commercial reviewer. Everything only SOVITECH can settle reaches one engineer queue per project and never the owner. The engineer acts on it there: verification through the one guarded writer, conflicts only an engineer can judge, asset identity, site surveys and rule 14 findings. An owner's acknowledgement stays an acknowledgement. Every investment figure takes its stage from stored records, and "Formal quotation" comes only from a quotation record that names the reviewing engineer and the commercial reviewer (rule 10). Screens: UD-15, UD-48, UD-49, UD-38 and UD-40, with the owner's group lines on OB-3 and OB-8, the price stage on OB-8, DB-02, DB-13 and UD-06, and the engineer's actions on DB-05, DB-10, DB-16 and DB-17. What holds before the queue page exists is R-125; the page itself waits for dashboards 8.15 (R-128). Reviews of reference datasets (US-ENGINEER-12) share the datasets page with US-ADMIN-19 and are covered by R-150. IFC tag sources, flag clearing and mapping tables as datasets wait for approval (below); their v1.5 behaviour is R-131, R-126 and R-132.

#### R-125 Everything only SOVITECH can settle reaches the engineer queue, never the owner

- **Epic:** E-ENGINEER · **Stories:** US-ENGINEER-01, US-ENGINEER-03, US-ENGINEER-04, US-ENGINEER-05, US-ENGINEER-06, US-ENGINEER-07, US-ENGINEER-08 · **Functions:** F-REVIEW-01, F-REVIEW-03, F-REVIEW-04, F-VALUE-02, F-VALUE-03, F-VALUE-04, F-VALUE-08, F-CALC-02, F-CALC-04, F-QUESTION-02, F-QUESTION-07, F-EXTRACT-10, F-PRICE-01, F-RENDER-02, F-RENDER-03, F-AUTH-02, F-AUTH-03, F-AUTH-04, F-AUDIT-01 · **Screens:** UD-15, UD-48, OB-3, OB-8, DB-10, DB-17
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (rules 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 13, 14, 2.4, 2.5, 2.8, section 4; §5-3b, 7.1.1-C5)
- **Gated by:** none
- **Priority:** Must (proposed) · **Slice:** S1 (proposed)
- **Requirement:** The app routes every item that only SOVITECH can settle to the project's engineer queue and never asks the owner about it: engineer-field inferences; conflicts on engineer fields or with an `engineer_verified` candidate, including a declared revision, a later document or an owner edit that disagrees with one, and a type or location disagreement on one tag, which stays one asset; untagged appearances, listed as possible duplicates; document values the owner corrected on engineer or `for_quotation` fields; confirmations beyond the budget the approver sets; technical questions; facts only a site visit can settle; rule 14 findings, which change no state; and "Something's wrong" notes. The owner sees these only as one line per group under "SOVITECH will check", and until an engineer resolves an engineer-routed conflict its dependent outputs read "Provisional: two values for <field>" or "Not available yet: two values for <field>". An owner's "Looks right", single or in bulk, writes only `owner_acknowledged`, which ranks below `user_confirmed` and never clears Provisional; a change in a tier's wording never changes verification; no user without the engineer role verifies a value, closes an engineer-routed conflict or writes an asset event; and verification of a demo project's value is refused for everyone.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** An engineer-field inference shows Likely or Possible as rule 3 caps it, or SOVITECH will check at low confidence, with its source line. "Site survey needed" sits under SOVITECH will check, and reuse of existing devices, wiring or controllers is never assumed: on a BMS modernization with no site survey and an approved cost basis for both options, the CAPEX range covers reuse and replacement, with the badge Estimated and its stage label read from stored records, and without one it reads "Not available yet", naming the missing cost basis. The owner reads a routed conflict as "Documents disagree on this. A SOVITECH engineer will check it." and sees no "Which is right?" question. "<n> things for you to check" counts only owner items (rule 7), and a finding is never listed under For you. A finding's guardrail event holds the document id and the location and no document text (rule 13). The budget value is approver setting 1 (D-53); which action "Not available yet" offers when the missing item is SOVITECH's is open (D-14). Tests: G1-7, G3-3, G4-8, G4-14, G4-16, G4-17, G4-18, G4-19, G5-3, G7-5, G10-3, G14-1, G14-2.
- **Acceptance:** US-ENGINEER-01 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8; US-ENGINEER-03 AC2, AC4, AC7; US-ENGINEER-04 AC2; US-ENGINEER-05 AC3, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9, AC10, AC11; US-ENGINEER-06 AC1, AC4; US-ENGINEER-07 AC1, AC2, AC6, AC9; US-ENGINEER-08 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5
- **Sources:** docs/guardrails.md rule 1 ("Reuse"), rule 3 ("Who confirms", "Confidence is set by the evidence and capped by code"), rule 4 ("A correction is a resolution, not a conflict", "Routing", "Until a conflict is resolved"), rule 5 ("Budget"), rule 6 ("Ask the right person"), rule 10 ("Engineer verification is an authenticated action", "Demo data"), rules 13 and 14, section 4 item 9, 2.4, 2.5 ("Identity"), 2.8; guardrails section 5 row §5-3b (step 3, HVAC assets …); dashboards-spec 7.1.1 row 7.1.1-C5 ("AHU-01's location …"); docs/build-readiness.md 3 "Now" items 3 and 10; prompts/sovitech-ai-system.md "Getting information with the fewest questions" (suggestions for the SOVITECH team); traceability.md 10.3 near miss 39 (a guardrail event could carry document text); functions.md F-REVIEW-01, F-REVIEW-03, F-VALUE-04. US-ENGINEER-03, 05, 06, 07 and 08 are tagged S2 because their actions and lists sit on the queue item page (R-128). The criteria cited here hold before that page exists (routing, what the owner sees, refusals, findings from extraction), so this requirement deliberately places those parts of the stories in S1 (proposed), with no gate, and their page parts are in R-128. US-ENGINEER-08 sits here whole: every criterion is extraction and routing, and its listing on the page is US-ENGINEER-02 AC1. US-ENGINEER-04 AC1 needs the queue item page, so it is cited on R-128. DB-14 is not built in the proposal phase (7.1.1-D12, "14, the whole page"), so 7.1.1-C5's location conflict shows on DB-10 and DB-17 only. The G4 routing tests are also traced to E-DOCS, E-REVIEW and E-ASSETS stories (traceability.md 6).

#### R-128 Engineer queue page and the engineer's actions

- **Epic:** E-ENGINEER · **Stories:** US-ENGINEER-02, US-ENGINEER-03, US-ENGINEER-04, US-ENGINEER-05, US-ENGINEER-06, US-ENGINEER-07 · **Functions:** F-REVIEW-01, F-REVIEW-02, F-REVIEW-04, F-REVIEW-05, F-VALUE-01, F-VALUE-02, F-VALUE-04, F-VALUE-08, F-VALUE-10, F-CALC-02, F-CALC-04, F-INGEST-01, F-INGEST-02, F-RENDER-01, F-RENDER-03, F-RENDER-05, F-AUTH-02, F-AUTH-03, F-AUTH-04, F-AUDIT-01, F-AUDIT-03, F-AUDIT-05 · **Screens:** UD-15, UD-48, UD-49, DB-05, DB-17

From an item they have opened, an engineer, and no other role, verifies it through the one guarded writer or rejects a candidate with a reason, resolves an engineer-routed conflict by choosing one candidate with a reason, merges, splits or removes assets with a reason, and records a site survey as a document of stage `site_survey` with the engineer as author and each survey value as a new `user` candidate; every action is an appended event, and dependent values show "Out of date, recalculating".

Asset counts stay Calculated with "Provisional: depends on <n> equipment items not yet checked" while any input is unverified. A survey value shows one badge by the 2.8 table order and a source line naming the survey document. On a demo project the demo line shows, and no verify or survey action is available. No engineer verifies, rejects, resolves, merges, splits, removes or records a survey in the app, so engineer-field values stay unverified, dependent results stay provisional, and engineer-routed conflicts stay open.

#### R-131 Equipment from IFC models joins the same assets, once model values can be stored

- **Epic:** E-ENGINEER · **Stories:** US-ENGINEER-10 · **Functions:** F-REVIEW-06, F-IFC-06, F-VALUE-08, F-INGEST-03 · **Screens:** UD-15, UD-48, OB-2
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (rules 1, 12, 2.5)
- **Gated by:** Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.4 (not approved; D-41) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.1 (not approved; D-38) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.2 (not approved; D-39) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.3 (not approved; D-40) · Depends on proposal ifc-input 6.2.10 (not approved; D-37) · Blocked by open question build-readiness decision 4 (D-01) · Blocked by open question ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3 (D-92)
- **Priority:** Should (proposed) · **Slice:** S3
- **Requirement:** An engineering tag read from a stored IFC model follows guardrails 2.5 like any other appearance: a model's tag and a schedule's tag that normalise to the same string are one asset with a piece of evidence from each, and the tag is shown exactly as written in its evidence.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** Once ifc-input 6.2.1 is approved, a tag's evidence carries the contract's locator: the file hash as `Evidence.contentHash`, the IFC schema as document metadata (`model.schema`, ifc-input 6.2.2), the entity GlobalId, STEP instance ids and attribute or property-set path as the proposed `Evidence.locator.ifc` (ifc-input 6.2.1), and the verbatim STEP text as the excerpt (ifc-input 4.1 item 3). Under v1.5 no IFC value passes rule 1's locator check. Tests: G12-1 tests the RVT form of the stored-not-analysed status line; G4-3 and G4-16 test identity by normalised tag, and G4-17 tests that untagged appearances are not merged. The IFC setup that ifc-input 5.4 gives G4-3 (CTA-01 in the model and the schedule PDF) cannot run before proposals ifc-input 6.2.1, 6.2.2, 6.2.3 and 6.2.10, and its tag source needs ifc-input 6.2.4.
- **Until decided:** The v1.5 behaviour: no tag is read from a stored model, no asset is created from any model element, and the engineer queue holds no tag-source item (US-ENGINEER-10 AC1). The document register shows the model's status line "Not analysed: IFC model stored, not analysed", naming the format as G12-1 names RVT, and no "not found" statement counts the model as searched (AC2). No mapping table shapes a model value until the approver accepts ifc-input 6.2.10 and approves the tables.
- **Acceptance:** US-ENGINEER-10 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4
- **Sources:** docs/ifc-input.md 4.1 item 3 (the excerpt), 6.2.4 (GAP-G), 6.3.1 item 2 (the smallest set of proposals that lets IFC values be stored); docs/guardrails.md rule 1 ("Evidence is verified by code, not trusted"), rule 12, 2.5 ("One tag, one asset"), 2.8 (status lines); functions.md F-REVIEW-06 and F-IFC-06 (not built under v1.5), F-INGEST-03; US-ENGINEER-10 Notes. The story's criteria come from the guardrails (AC1 and AC2 are the v1.5 behaviour; AC3 and AC4 apply 2.5), so it has this gated requirement with its own gates, and only the tag-source mechanism, which only ifc-input 6.2.4 supplies, waits (below). The ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3 gate is the PRD's: prompt 2 gates every stored IFC value on the approved mapping tables (ifc-input 6.3.1 items 2 and 3), which need the SOVITECH asset taxonomy with its life-safety flags; item 2, the approver, is implied by the proposal gates.

### E-ADMIN: Administration and app shell

Accounts, sign-in and roles, project isolation, the project list and the project switcher, the header menu and the workspace navigation, the app shell and the brand theme (OD-1 to OD-4), the demo project (OD-5), processors, reference datasets and their approval status (read-only: approving a dataset, a mapping table or a guardrail change belongs to the approver alone, guardrails section 10), guardrail events and their review, confidence calibration, and erasure requests with their audit. Screens: UD-16, UD-18, UD-32, UD-36, UD-37, UD-39, UD-40 and UD-41, and the chrome of OB-1 to OB-8 and DB-01 to DB-22. ## 8. Data and inputs

The app has three kinds of input: the owner's answers in the wizard, the documents the owner uploads, and reference data that SOVITECH curates. The owner's direction makes IFC models a primary input next to the answers and the other documents (Decided: owner decision 2026-09-24, OD-8: "based on data from the onboarding flow, based on IFC files from BIM softwares"). Whatever the input, an engineering value is stored in the value model of guardrails section 2: subjects hold fields, fields hold immutable candidates, events are append-only and state is derived. A bare engineering number is never passed (`CLAUDE.md`, "How to build").

This section summarises each input and points to the tables in `docs/ifc-input.md`, the specs and `docs/build-readiness.md` instead of copying them. It defines no requirement: the requirements that build these inputs are in sections 7 and 11. Each item carries one of the four labels from the header.

### 8.1 Onboarding answers

**The inventory is not the storage model.** onboarding-spec 4 lists the wizard's inputs as an `IntakeProject` interface marked "INVENTORY ONLY. Do not implement this interface." Its preamble says every engineering value in it is stored with the value model in guardrails section 2 (Required: onboarding-spec 4; guardrails section 2). The table says where each inventory item goes under v1.5.

Name, type, city and country are the four `required` fields, asked without Skip (rule 7; G7-6). Location is a country code and a city id, asked country first or through one place search. `IfcProject.Name` and a model's georeference never replace these answers (ifc-input 4.1 item 7), and the project name is never evidence for a value (rule 1; G1-11). | Required (rule 7; §5-1a (step 1, "Project name, type, city, country"), §5-1b (step 1, "City before Country")). **Rules that apply to every answer** (Required: guardrails 2.1, 2.4, section 4, rules 3, 7 and 8):
- Each field is filled in the Speed Rule's order, and the owner is asked only when rule 5 or rule 6 allows it (guardrails section 4).
- An owner's entry is a new `user` candidate. On a field whose `confirmBy` is `owner` or `either` it gets a `user_confirmed` event when it is created; on an engineer field it stays `unverified` (2.1).
- A visible Suggested preselection left in place is written on Continue as a `user` candidate with `user_confirmed` and `accepted_suggestion` events. Nothing hidden, collapsed or on another step is accepted this way (rule 3; G3-4).
- Skip for now, and Continue on an unanswered question, write a `skipped` field event. The field stays unknown and nothing fills the gap (rule 7).
- Candidates never change. Field state, the active candidate, provisional and stale are derived by one pure function (2.4; F-VALUE-01, F-VALUE-02).
- Only the four required fields block, and they block only the creation of the project: Continue stays enabled and shows an inline error on each empty one (rule 7; G7-6).
- Numbers the owner types are never stored as one silent reading when they read two ways (rule 8; traceability 10.3 item 12). Which number format owner entries use is Open (D-26).

**How the steps feed each other.** onboarding-spec 5 describes the mockups. The guardrails change several of its flows; `docs/product/traceability.md` 8.1 reads every row (flow-1 to flow-10) and every AI touchpoint (ai-1 to ai-5) in full. In short:

| Flow (onboarding-spec 5) | Under v1.5 | Open |
|---|---|---|
| 1 name → header, every step | The stored name shows once the project exists. It is never evidence for a value (rule 1; G1-11). | Header before Next: D-10 |
| 1 type → steps 2 to 5 and 8 | No branching yet: every type gets the same steps. A type-specific question needs registered `affects` and a passing sensitivity test (rule 6; G6-1). For existing building and BMS modernization, design-stage sources read From design drawings, with the stage named (2.3; G2-6). | D-23 |
| 1 location → "AI" | Changed. Location reaches climate, prices and regulation only as reference data that code selects by country code and city id from approved datasets (2.1; rule 8, "Currency"; G10-4). It is not an AI input for them (F-REGISTRY-07). | Suppliers: D-93 |
| 2 documents → 3, 4, 8 | Only parsed formats produce candidates. Every other file is stored "Not analysed" and counts as unsearched (rule 12; G12-1, G12-4). | D-01, ZIP included |
| 1 name or 2 documents → 5 (building type) | Changed: documents only. Building type is a fact with Likely or Possible, capped by code against the evidence (rule 3; section 4 example). | none |
| 3 ↔ 4 | One detection field per system feeds both steps. Step 3's Systems row is a calculated count with its basis, or is not shown (§5-3e). | Systems list: D-17 |
| 3 → 8 (area) | Step 8 shows the same value id as step 3, rendered identically (G2-7). A first-estimate area still missing is asked once inline at step 8 (rule 7; G7-2a, G7-2b). | First-estimate set: D-53 |
| 4 → 7, 8 | Areas are preselected from the included systems and the goals, with Suggested (§5-7). | D-12 |
| 5 → 6 | Goals are owner choices. None is preselected without Suggested and a reason. | D-11 |
| 5, 6, 7 → 8 → generation | Changed. The answers reach generation as stored candidates and decisions, not as prompt text. Code computes every figure; the AI only words the proposal through tokens (section 9). | After Generate: D-14 |

### 8.2 IFC models

**What the owner's direction settles.** IFC models are inside the product's parsing scope (Decided: owner decision 2026-09-24, OD-8: "based on data from the onboarding flow, based on IFC files from BIM softwares"; ifc-input 6.3.1). The direction approves none of the guardrail proposals in ifc-input 6.2 (ifc-input 6.2, 6.3). It does not revise build-readiness decision 4, which still limits v1 parsing to native-text PDF and XLSX and stores IFC as "Not analysed" (Open, D-01, with onboarding Q15 and ifc-input GAP-K). Whether IFC enters slice 1, and in which of the three forms in ifc-input 6.3.1 item 1, is also open (D-04, with build-readiness decision 3); section 6 lays the options out.

**What v1.5 allows today** (Required: guardrails v1.5 as ifc-input 6.1 reads it).

| Behaviour | Basis | Stories and functions |
|---|---|---|
| The IFC file is stored under its project with a `DocumentRecord`: content hash, stage `unknown`, analysis status `stored_only`. | 2.3; rule 13; G13-4 | US-IFC-01; F-INGEST-01, F-INGEST-02 |
| Its row shows the 2.8 status line for a file stored but not analysed, naming the format as G12-1 names RVT: "Not analysed: IFC model stored, not analysed". The line stays for as long as no value from the model can be stored, even while code reads the model for the engineer. | 2.8; rule 12; G12-1 | US-IFC-01; F-INGEST-03 |
| The model's kind, stage and revision read Unknown, never "none stated". Code sets none of them from the file name or the contents. | 2.3; rule 12 | US-IFC-01 |
| A model becomes a revision of another only by the owner's or an engineer's declaration. Code proposes no revision link from model contents. | 2.3 | US-IFC-01; F-INGEST-06, F-IFC-07 |
| Once model reading is enabled, code may record what the model contains (declared schema, authoring tool, schema errors) as coverage for the engineer's view only (UD-44). None of it is a value, evidence or an owner-facing line. | rules 7, 12, 13, 14; ifc-input 6.1. Reading a model at all: Open (D-01, D-04) | US-IFC-03; F-IFC-01 |
| Model text (Name, Description, ObjectType, property text) is data. Text that addresses the reader becomes an `embedded_instruction` finding for the engineer and changes no state. No log contains it. | rules 13, 14; G14-1 | US-IFC-04; F-IFC-02, F-EXTRACT-10 |
| No "not found" statement counts a model whose values cannot be kept. | rule 12; G12-4 | US-IFC-01; F-INGEST-03 |
| No value, badge or field state comes from the model. | rule 1 (the locator check) | US-IFC-01, US-IFC-27 |
| Delete and erasure remove the model with its extracted text and every converted viewing file. Removing converted files is stricter than rule 13's wording and adds no question, gate or owner-facing wording; ifc-input 6.2.16 would make it a rule. | rule 13; 2.3 | US-IFC-01; F-INGEST-07 |
| Nothing waits for a model: Continue and Generate never block. | rule 7 | US-IFC-01 |
| A stored model may be shown as a document under the four conditions below. Whether and when a viewer is built is open. | rules 2, 13; 2.3 | US-IFC-08; F-IFC-10 |

The reason no value passes: `Evidence.locator` in 2.4 has page, sheet, cell and bbox only, so for a model "the locator exists" can never hold, and every IFC `document` candidate is rejected (ifc-input 6.1, "Evidence"). Under v1.5 a model yields no value: it gives coverage for the engineer and, under the four conditions, a view of the document.

**Accepted schemas and what is read from each.**
- When models are read, the target schemas are IFC2x3, IFC4 and IFC4.3. IFC5 is not a target (Proposed (ifc-input 1.2 item 13)).
- The schemas differ in ways that matter. IFC2x3 has no occurrence classes such as `IfcPump` (a pump is an `IfcFlowMovingDevice` typed by `IfcPumpType`); IFC 4.3 deprecates some classes and relations; property names can differ. The mapping tables are therefore kept per schema version (ifc-input 1.2 item 6, 3.2 "Version notes").
- The recommended parser describes its geometry support as extensive for IFC2x3 and IFC4 only. So designers are asked for IFC4 Reference View exports for now, and IFC 4.3 is accepted for data (Proposed (ifc-input 2.2)).
- What a model gives, once values may be stored, is mapped per source in ifc-input 4.2 and summarised in 4.3. Direct reads are `document`, with an IFC locator. Unit conversions, sums over spaces and levels, and counts from the asset register are `calculated` by the engine. An asset type from an IFC class is always an `ai_inference`, never `document`, as G3-1 treats a schedule row (ifc-input 4.1, 4.3). Never read from a model: point counts, protocols not named in text, reuse of existing devices, and anything about life-safety control beyond monitor, display, log and alarm (ifc-input 4.3; rules 1 and 11).
- Exports usually lack controllers, sensors, actuators, point lists, protocols, configuration, reliable area bases, georeferencing and stage (ifc-input 3.5). A model mostly settles where things are and how many there are, rarely their ratings, and almost never how they are controlled. Points stay Estimated from SOVITECH templates until a point list exists (rule 1; G9-4).
- Quantities computed from a model's shapes (areas, containment, port tracing) wait for proposal ifc-input 6.2.7 (not approved; D-50). Inferences made by code rather than the AI (a class lookup, a level type from a storey name, a space category) wait for proposal ifc-input 6.2.9 (not approved; D-42), because 2.1 defines `ai_inference` as "Derived by the AI from evidence, not written literally".

**The pipeline, from upload to candidates and to the converted model.** Server-side reading and conversion are recommendations (Proposed (ifc-input 2.2)); the libraries and hosting are for prompt 3's ADRs (section 13).

| Stage | Under v1.5 | Once the gates clear | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Upload and storage: content hash, storage keyed by project id plus content hash, `DocumentRecord` | Built | Unchanged | Required (2.3; rule 13; G13-4); F-INGEST-01, F-INGEST-02 |
| 2. Parse-scope routing | `stored_only`, with the status line | Analysed once decision 4 is revised | Required (rule 12); Open (D-01); F-INGEST-03 |
| 3. Extractor job: one job per file on the server, in a sandbox with memory and time limits. Order of work: header and schema; units; spatial tree; groups and systems; elements with types and property sets; geometry last. IfcOpenShell 0.8.5, pinned, in `services/extractor`. | Nothing is read until build-readiness decision 4 allows model reading (D-01; for the header and schema check, also build-readiness decision 3, D-04); then the header, the schema check and rule 14 text only, for the engineer (F-IFC-01, F-IFC-02) | Full read | Proposed (ifc-input 2.2). Memory and time limits: Target not set (D-22) |
| 4. Validation: schema validation first; then the SOVITECH IDS (below); then the extractor's own checks for units, georeferencing, duplicate spaces and tags that are authoring-tool ids. A schema-invalid file is still read where it can be, and its problems are recorded in coverage, never hidden. | Schema errors on the engineer's view only | "Partly analysed" for models waits for proposal ifc-input 6.2.3 (not approved; D-40) | Proposed (ifc-input 2.2) |
| 5. Mapping: deterministic and table-first, through versioned mapping tables. The AI is used only where a table cannot map, such as a user-defined property name (section 9). | None | The minimum set below | Proposed (ifc-input 4.1 item 2; 6.3.1 item 4) |
| 6. Units: from the file's declared units, then the registry. The engine appends 2.1's "exact unit conversions" as `calculated`, with the original kept. An `IfcReal` never becomes a quantity candidate for a dimensioned field; `IfcLabel` text goes through the rule 8 parser. | None | SI units a model declares (m³/s, J, absolute K, 0-1 ratios) also wait for proposal ifc-input 6.2.11 (not approved; D-63) | Required (2.7; rule 8); ifc-input 4.1 item 4 |
| 7. Evidence check: rule 1's five checks, with an IFC locator | None | Proposal ifc-input 6.2.1 (not approved; D-38) | Required (rule 1); F-EXTRACT-04 |
| 8. Store and derive: candidates append-only, state derived, conflicts by rule 4 | None | As for any document | Required (2.4; rule 4); F-VALUE-01 to F-VALUE-04 |
| 9. Conversion for viewing: converted once on the server into viewing files whose geometry is keyed by GlobalId, stored beside the document and keyed by project id plus content hash. The browser never parses the owner's file. | Allowed as a view of a document, under the four conditions below | Pins, labels and a no-model state wait for the proposals named below | Proposed (ifc-input 2.2); viewer Open (D-03); F-IFC-10 |

The viewer library is That Open Engine on pre-converted Fragments, with IfcConvert GLB files and per-storey SVG plans without printed areas as the fallback. A spike on the synthetic fixture and one large public sample settles it (Proposed (ifc-input 2.2); Open, D-03). xeokit is excluded for a hosted commercial app because of AGPL-3.0 (ifc-input 2.2, 2.3).

**The four conditions for showing a stored model** (`docs/dev-prompts/02-prd.md`, "Model views"; PRD section 10.6). Showing a stored model as a document is v1.5 behaviour (ifc-input 6.3.1 item 2) when all four hold:
1. its viewing files are keyed by project id plus content hash and served only after the project access check (rule 13, "Isolation"; G13-4);
2. the erasure job removes them with their document (stricter than rule 13's wording; ifc-input 6.2.16 would make it a rule);
3. nothing is drawn as text in the 3D scene, in textures or in plan images, and every label, count or area shown with the view is a bound value (rule 2; G2-1). Under v1.5 none of them is read from the model, and a selection in the view shows no data from the model;
4. the view names its document, with the stage and revision as recorded (2.3).

Pins, scale bars, north arrows, "From a superseded revision" on a view, and "Illustrative model, not to scale" wait for proposal 7.2.8 (not approved; D-45) and proposal ifc-input 6.2.15 (not approved; D-46). A render test cannot read text drawn inside a 3D canvas, which is why condition 3 forbids it (ifc-input 6.2.15). ifc-input 5.4 IFC-12 (an SVG plan with printed areas fails the render test) is proposed and not indexed; it needs a conversion, not a stored model value.

**Validation and the draft IDS file** (ifc-input 5.5).
- A draft information-requirements file, `fixtures/ids/sovitech-ifc-minimum-v0.1.ids`, would be checked against every IFC upload with IfcTester (Proposed (ifc-input 5.5, 2.2)). Its specifications and the fixture's expected results are in ifc-input 5.5 and are not copied here.
- Its results never block the owner, never create values and never become owner questions (ifc-input 5.5 item 2; rules 6 and 7). v1.5 gives model-check results no defined place (ifc-input 6.1, "Coverage"), while ifc-input 6.3.1 item 2 reads them as allowed today. The stories take the stricter reading: results are stored with the document and the IDS version for the engineer's view only, and no owner screen shows a model-check line, count or task, because the 2.8 status lines are "the only ones used" (US-IFC-05; F-IFC-09). Owner-facing coverage wording for model checks waits for proposal ifc-input 6.2.14 (not approved; D-73; US-IFC-06).
- IDS and validation reports use reserved terms (ifc-input 4.5). A checker's report is not document text, and app copy about a model contains no reserved term outside the places 2.8 allows (ifc-input 5.4 IFC-14, proposed, not indexed).
- Whether the app runs the check at all, and who reviews the draft file, is open (D-36). Until decided, the check is not built (US-IFC-05).
- Before the file is committed: validate it with the buildingSMART IDS-Audit-tool, confirm the space quantity check with IfcTester on the fixture, and confirm the IFC4 property names for the chiller check. Before relying on IfcTester, run it against the buildingSMART IDS test cases (Proposed (ifc-input 5.5, 2.2)).
- The buildingSMART Validation Service is a third-party upload. It is used on synthetic fixtures only, unless it is listed as an approved processor (rule 13; ifc-input 2.2).
- The IDS is SOVITECH data: versioned, reviewed by engineers, and a draft until the approver accepts it (ifc-input 5.5, "Versioning"; 8.4).

**Identity: tags, GlobalId and proxies** (ifc-input 3.3; 1.2 items 1, 4 and 10).
- Required today (2.5): one normalised tag is one asset across all documents; a type disagreement is a conflict for the engineer, not a second asset (G4-16); untagged appearances are listed as possible duplicates and never merged or counted (G4-17).
- Where a model's engineering tag sits varies by exporter: in `Tag`, in `Name`, in a property, or nowhere. A `Tag` that holds only digits is an authoring id, not an engineering tag (ifc-input 1.2 item 1, 3.3). A per-document tag source that code proposes and an engineer accepts, level and space identity across architectural and MEP models, and GlobalId inside one declared revision chain all wait for proposal ifc-input 6.2.4 (not approved; D-41; US-IFC-20; F-IFC-06, F-REVIEW-06).
- GlobalIds normally survive re-export but change in some copy, group and worksharing cases. A GlobalId helps map revisions and is never the only identity (ifc-input 1.2 item 10).
- `IfcBuildingElementProxy` has no predefined meaning. Its type can come only from its text, or it stays unknown and is listed for the engineer (ifc-input 1.2 item 4; proposal ifc-input 6.2.9, not approved; D-42).
- Whenever model types are stored, rule 3 already gives Likely to a tag whose prefix the reference glossary defines (G3-8), and, once proposal ifc-input 6.2.9 (not approved; D-42) allows class-based tiers, a class-based tier never lowers a tier the tag supports (ifc-input 4.2; 6.1, near miss 3).
- Counting untagged objects within one model waits for proposal ifc-input 6.2.5 (not approved; D-74; US-IFC-21). Until then such counts read "Not available yet" (ifc-input 5.4 IFC-10: its "Today" version waits for the minimum set, and its second version also for ifc-input 6.2.5).

**The locator** (`docs/dev-prompts/02-prd.md`, "How the PRD applies the contract"). The contract's IFC evidence is a document-derived value with a locator of four fields. The locator is itself a proposal.

| Contract field | Where it lives | Status |
|---|---|---|
| File hash | `Evidence.contentHash` (2.4) | Required: exists in v1.5 |
| IFC schema | Document metadata, `model.schema` | Proposed: proposal ifc-input 6.2.2 (not approved; D-39) |
| Entity GlobalId, STEP instance ids, and the attribute, property-set or quantity-set path, including through the type object | The proposed `Evidence.locator.ifc` | Proposed: proposal ifc-input 6.2.1 (not approved; D-38) |
| Excerpt | The verbatim STEP text, compared after decoding STEP string escapes and then normalising whitespace and diacritics; `original.text` holds the decoded string | Proposed: proposal ifc-input 6.2.1 (ifc-input 4.1 item 3) |

Its proving case is ifc-input 5.4 IFC-1 (a tampered STEP line is rejected), which waits for proposal ifc-input 6.2.1.

**What value extraction waits for.** Every IFC value waits for the minimum set: proposals ifc-input 6.2.1, 6.2.2, 6.2.3 and 6.2.10 (none approved; D-38, D-39, D-40, D-37), the approved mapping tables (ifc-input 6.3.1 items 2 and 3), which need the SOVITECH asset taxonomy (D-92), and the owner's revision of build-readiness decision 4 (D-01). The order in which the approver takes the proposals is open (D-05). Each content area also waits for its own proposals:

| Content | Also waits for | Story |
|---|---|---|
| Evidence check with an IFC locator | nothing more | US-IFC-27 |
| Model format, kind, stage and revision | nothing more | US-IFC-09 |
| A revision link that code proposes | nothing more | US-IFC-12 |
| Building properties and georeference | ifc-input 6.2.9 | US-IFC-13 |
| Levels from storeys (a storey count never establishes a floor count) | ifc-input 6.2.8, 6.2.9, 6.2.4 | US-IFC-14 |
| Rooms from spaces | ifc-input 6.2.6, 6.2.4, 6.2.9 | US-IFC-15 |
| Areas | ifc-input 6.2.6, 6.2.7; the engineer-approved factors of approver setting 5 | US-IFC-16 |
| Zones | ifc-input 6.2.9, 6.2.4 | US-IFC-17 |
| Systems for step 4 | ifc-input 6.2.9; the systems list (D-17) | US-IFC-18 |
| Equipment assets | ifc-input 6.2.9, 6.2.4; the asset taxonomy | US-IFC-19 |
| Architectural and MEP models of one building | ifc-input 6.2.4 | US-IFC-20 |

| Metering points and control links | ifc-input 6.2.9; point templates and taxonomy | US-IFC-23 |
