US-ADMIN-02 is cited only for AC1, its behaviour while new Q38 is open. Malware scanning of uploads is the third precondition build-readiness 3 "Later" names before the first real upload; it has no source in the approved design, the guardrails or an owner decision, so it is not a condition of this requirement and is listed as Proposed (PRD) under D-35: until it is adopted, the four conditions here do not by themselves make the environment ready for real owner documents. The build-readiness decision 1 gate is the PRD's: rule 13 says "The approved processors (LLM provider, OCR, storage) are listed here once they are chosen", so recording a processor is an edit to docs/guardrails.md that needs the approver (section 10).

#### R-160 Large files are accepted and read in the background, and every limit shows as coverage

- **Epic:** none · **Stories:** US-DOCS-01, US-DOCS-02, US-DOCS-06, US-REVIEW-09 · **Functions:** F-INGEST-01, F-INGEST-02, F-INGEST-04, F-INGEST-05, F-QUESTION-09 · **Screens:** OB-2, OB-3, OB-8, UD-33, UD-34, DB-15
- **Status:** From approved design · Required by guardrails (rule 7, "Late findings never interrupt"; rule 12; 2.8 status lines)
- **Gated by:** none
- **Priority:** Must (proposed) · **Slice:** S1 (proposed)
- **Requirement:** The app accepts, hashes and stores any file of an accepted format up to the size limit shown on step 2 ("Max file size 500 MB"), and reads it in the background. No upload, conversion or analysis blocks Continue, Generate or any other control, and a result that arrives later never opens a dialog, sends the owner back or changes an answer. When a job cannot read all of a file, for any reason (a page or part that fails, a truncated file, or a resource limit the job runs into), code records what was read, the file shows "Partly analysed (<read> of <total> pages)" or "Analysis failed", and nothing unread counts as searched.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** While files are still being read, Generate works and the notice reads "Still reading <n> files. Your estimate will update when they finish." (rule 7). Fields sourced only from unread pages stay Unknown (G12-3), and no "not found" statement covers unread pages (G12-4). Whether the limit also applies to all of a project's files together is open (D-22); until it is answered no total limit is applied (US-DOCS-02 AC1). No source sets a time, throughput or memory target: Target not set (D-22). Test ids: G7-4, G12-3, G12-4.
- **Acceptance:** US-DOCS-01 AC5; US-DOCS-02 AC1; US-DOCS-06 AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7; US-REVIEW-09 AC1, AC3, AC4, AC5
- **Sources:** `design/onboarding-spec.md` 3 (Step 2: "Max file size 500 MB"), 4 ("limit 500 MB (per file or total: unconfirmed)"); `docs/guardrails.md` rule 2 (the render-test allowlist names "Max file size 500 MB"), rule 7, rule 12, 2.8; `docs/ifc-input.md` 1.2 item 9 ("Server memory for a 500 MB file has to be measured in a spike, not assumed"). Server-side reading and conversion, one sandboxed job per file with memory and time limits, and the memory spike are Proposed (`docs/ifc-input.md` 2.2, 1.2 item 9): see the list below. US-DOCS-02 (S3; new Q7, D-22) is cited only for AC1, its behaviour while new Q7 is open, which D-22 records as its "Until decided" behaviour. Approved-design basis: step 2, "Max file size 500 MB".

#### R-161 Badges target WCAG AA contrast on every surface

- **Epic:** none · **Stories:** US-REVIEW-01, US-ADMIN-09, US-FIN-09, US-ASSETS-02 · **Functions:** F-RENDER-01, F-RENDER-03, F-RENDER-08, F-EXPORT-01 · **Screens:** none
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (2.8, "Prominence")
- **Gated by:** none
- **Priority:** Must (proposed) · **Slice:** S1 (proposed)
- **Requirement:** The app targets WCAG AA contrast for every badge. Each badge label, at 12px or larger, is checked against the WCAG AA text threshold of 4.5:1 on every surface it can sit on, on screen (page, raised surface, selected fill) and in exports, and a contrast check on the theme tokens, run with the harness, fails when any badge colour pair falls below it. The badge sits on the same line or tile as its figure, and it is never available only on hover, in a tooltip or in a collapsed section.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** 2.8 "Prominence" reads: "A badge sits on the same line or tile as its figure, at 12px or larger, and meets WCAG AA contrast." Badge labels come only from 2.8, and the brand yields to 2.8 (`company/brand/app-alignment.md` "App theme", "What still wins"). Badge colours are pending the owner's OK (D-19); pending and approved tokens face the same check (US-ADMIN-09 AC1). The WCAG version is not set (D-35). No case in section 7 tests contrast (reported).
- **Acceptance:** US-REVIEW-01 AC12; US-ADMIN-09 AC1; US-FIN-09 AC9; US-ASSETS-02 AC8
- **Sources:** `docs/guardrails.md` 2.8 ("Prominence"); `company/brand/app-alignment.md` "App theme" ("How the numbers were checked": thresholds of 4.5:1 for text; the "Banners, pills and badges" rows give each proposed badge colour with its measured contrast on the two dark surfaces); `design/onboarding-spec.md` 2 and `design/dashboards-spec.md` 3 ("Not changed by the brand"). "App theme" measures badge colours only on the dark surfaces; exports on white have no measured badge colours yet (reported; part of app-alignment decision 7). US-ADMIN-09 (S2; D-19), US-FIN-09 (S2) and US-ASSETS-02 (S2; build-readiness decisions 6 and 1, D-92, D-05) are cited only for their contrast criteria, which bind each badge wherever its page ships.

- **Epic:** none · **Stories:** US-MODEL-04, US-IFC-08, US-ASSETS-05, US-ZONES-02, US-ASSETS-13 · **Functions:** F-VIEWER-01, F-VIEWER-02, F-VALUE-11, F-VALUE-14, F-RENDER-01, F-RENDER-06 · **Screens:** OB-3, DB-01, DB-04, DB-05, DB-07, DB-10, DB-17, DB-20

Keyboard operation of the views is in the list below. Each story keeps its own gates for the view or page it builds (US-MODEL-04 and US-IFC-08: onboarding Q3 and dashboards 8.5, D-03, and build-readiness decisions 3 and 4, D-04, D-01; US-ASSETS-05 and US-ZONES-02: dashboards 8.3, D-02; US-ASSETS-13: its own proposals, Later). This requirement builds no view: it binds whichever view or register page ships, so it carries no gate of its own. US-MODEL-04 AC1 is cited for naming the document with its stage and revision; showing the model's geometry is the viewer's own behaviour, under those gates. US-ASSETS-13 AC2 binds popovers and callouts only once that story ships (Later). #### R-164 Romanian and English documents, number formats and reserved terms

- **Epic:** none · **Stories:** US-REVIEW-04, US-ASSETS-08, US-INTAKE-17, US-DOCS-08, US-ADMIN-08, US-ADMIN-11 · **Functions:** F-REGISTRY-03, F-REGISTRY-04, F-REGISTRY-05, F-EXTRACT-04, F-EXTRACT-06, F-RENDER-04 · **Screens:** none
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (rule 8, "Parsing", "Abbreviations", "Floors"; 2.4, `Evidence.excerpt`; rule 1, "Enforced by" (the excerpt check); 2.8, "Reserved terms") · From approved design
- **Gated by:** none
- **Priority:** Must (proposed) · **Slice:** S1 (proposed)
- **Requirement:** The app reads owner documents written mostly in Romanian with English manufacturer tables inside them. It detects the number locale per table or per value, never per document; reads Romanian "34.500" as thirty-four thousand five hundred and "1,5" as one and a half; keeps both readings of an ambiguous number such as "1.500" at low confidence; stores approximate wording ("cca.", "aprox.", "~", "circa", "peste", "about") as approximate; expands Romanian abbreviations only from the glossary in reference data; parses the regim de înălțime into the floor structure; keeps every excerpt and original text verbatim in its own language, never translated; and matches evidence after normalising whitespace and diacritics, including the cedilla and comma-below forms of ş/ș and ţ/ț. The one reserved-term list holds the English and the Romanian terms, matched whole-word, ignoring case and diacritics. Interface copy is English, as every approved screen shows and `prompts/sovitech-ai-system.md` states.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** A value with no stated area basis is stored with basis unknown, its original kept, and its confirmation names the basis (G8-2). An entry the owner types that reads two ways is never stored as one silent reading (US-INTAKE-17 AC7); how owner-typed numbers are read is open (D-26). A reserved term outside the places 2.8 allows is flagged and logged as `reserved_term_blocked`. Whole-word matching misses Romanian verb forms such as "garantează"; proposal 7.2.29 (not approved; D-88) would add them. Until an approved glossary version exists (D-05; D-92), no abbreviation is expanded from the glossary. Adding a Romanian interface, and the display number format, are open (D-26); the level-label scheme is open (D-18). Test ids: G8-1, G8-2, G8-3, G8-9, G3-5, G3-8.
- **Acceptance:** US-REVIEW-04 AC2, AC4; US-ASSETS-08 AC3, AC4; US-INTAKE-17 AC7; US-DOCS-08 AC1, AC2; US-ADMIN-08 AC7; US-ADMIN-11 AC1
- **Sources:** `docs/guardrails.md` rule 8 ("Locale is detected per table or per value, not per document."; "Romanian format"; "Ambiguous readings keep both"; "Approximate wording is kept"; "Abbreviations"; "Floors"), 2.4 (`excerpt`: "verbatim, original language, never translated"), rule 1 ("Enforced by": the excerpt check "after normalising whitespace and diacritics"), 2.8 ("Reserved terms"); `prompts/sovitech-ai-system.md` (opening paragraph: "The app's interface language is English."); `company/brand/app-alignment.md` "Comparison" (Language row: "English only in every mockup"), "Decisions needed" 6; `CLAUDE.md` ("Owner documents are usually Romanian"); `docs/build-readiness.md` 2 "ro-building-docs" (the diacritic forms; entries are drafts until a SOVITECH engineer reviews them; Proposed skill), 6 ("the Romanian glossary entries, which need engineer review"). US-ADMIN-08 AC7 is tagged OD-2, but its English-copy clause rests on the approved screens and the AI prompt (reported). US-ASSETS-08 (S2) AC3 and AC4 bind ratings from the first extraction; US-ADMIN-11 AC1 binds only a Romanian interface, which keeps its gates (app-alignment decisions 2, 5 and 6; D-15, D-26). Approved-design basis: every approved screen's copy is English.

#### R-167 An append-only record of who did what, when and why

- **Epic:** none · **Stories:** US-PROPOSAL-11, US-DOCS-21, US-ADMIN-23, US-ADMIN-16, US-ENGINEER-16 · **Functions:** F-VALUE-01, F-VALUE-08, F-INGEST-06, F-INGEST-07, F-AUDIT-03, F-AUDIT-04, F-PROPOSAL-02, F-PRICE-04, F-PRICE-05 · **Screens:** UD-38, UD-41
- **Status:** Required by guardrails (2.3, `DocumentEvent`; 2.4, `CandidateEvent`, `FieldEvent`, "Recalculation"; 2.5, `AssetEvent`; rule 4, "Routing"; rule 10, "Stage 3 is derived, not passed"; rule 13, "Erasure")
- **Gated by:** none
- **Priority:** Must (proposed) · **Slice:** S1 (proposed)
- **Requirement:** Every change to a value, a document's status, an asset's identity or a conflict is an append-only event naming who acted, in which role, when and, where the guardrails ask, why: candidate events, field events, document events (declared revision, withdrawn, erased) and asset events. A generated proposal keeps the snapshot of candidate ids and formula versions it used, and formula versions never change. Wherever quotation records exist, each holds what rule 10 lists, the reviewing engineer's and the commercial reviewer's user ids included; it is never edited; and when any input changes after issue it shows "Superseded: inputs changed on <date>". Every erasure job leaves an audit record of who asked, when, which document and what was removed, with no document text.
- **Guardrail behaviour:** "Each resolution records who, when and why" (rule 4). History is never rewritten: the erasure job replaces only cited excerpts with "[erased]", withdrawn candidates keep their ids and values, and no other field's history changes (G13-3). The stage is read from stored records, never passed as a parameter (G10-1), and a record whose inputs changed shows the Superseded line (G10-2). Where quotation records are created is open (D-20); until then no "Formal quotation" appears anywhere (G10-1). Test ids: G4-1, G4-5, G4-13, G10-1, G10-2, G13-3.
- **Acceptance:** US-PROPOSAL-11 AC2, AC3; US-DOCS-21 AC7; US-ADMIN-23 AC1, AC3; US-ADMIN-16 AC3; US-ENGINEER-16 AC1, AC4
- **Sources:** `docs/guardrails.md` 2.3, 2.4 ("Candidates never change after they are written", "Formula versions are immutable", "A generated proposal keeps a snapshot of the candidate ids and formula versions it used"), 2.5, rule 4, rule 10 ("Stage 3 is derived, not passed"; "A quotation goes stale when its inputs change"), rule 13 ("one audited erasure job"); `docs/build-readiness.md` 3 "Now" item 8 (a hash manifest that fails when a published formula version changes: Proposed). The criteria from S2 and S3 stories (US-DOCS-21, US-ADMIN-23, US-ADMIN-16, US-ENGINEER-16) apply when those stories ship, with their own gates (US-ADMIN-16: new Q38 and new Q39, D-13; US-ENGINEER-16 as R-129: new Q35, D-20, dashboards 8.15, D-16); the event trail itself is needed from the first write.

### Proposed (PRD), not requirements

These non-functional needs have no source in the approved design, the guardrails or an owner decision. None is built as a requirement. The owner, or the approver where a rule would change, can adopt each one through its D id. Tools and hosting recommendations go to prompt 3's ADRs.

- **Keyboard use.** Every control is reachable and usable from the keyboard, with a visible focus ring, and the 3D and 2D views can be operated or skipped by keyboard. The mint 2px focus ring in "App theme" is a "Brand value, new role" row (D-19). Proposed (PRD); D-35.
- **WCAG version and level for the whole app.** Which WCAG version and level the app targets beyond badge contrast. "App theme" computed its ratios with WCAG 2 contrast formulas. Proposed (PRD); D-35.
- **Contrast beyond badges.** Source lines and data text at 12px and 4.5:1 (`design/dashboards-spec.md` 3.3, "Proposed"; D-19). Marks, control boundaries and focus rings at 3:1, with disabled controls exempt (`company/brand/app-alignment.md` "App theme" thresholds and its Extension rows; D-19).
- **Supported browsers.** Current desktop versions of the major browsers. The 3D view needs WebGL, because the recommended viewer runs on three.js (`docs/ifc-input.md` 2.2). Without WebGL, the view area would read "Not available yet" with its reason, as rule 7 requires of any missing output. Proposed (PRD); D-35.
- **Minimum viewport and behaviour below it.** A minimum viewport of 1440×900 (`design/dashboards-spec.md` 3.4 "Proposed shell"; `company/brand/app-alignment.md` "Shell sizes"), and what the app does below it, for example a horizontal scroll or a notice. Proposed (dashboards-spec 3.4); D-35.
- **Performance targets.** No source sets a target for upload time, analysis time, time from upload to first estimate (guardrails section 4 measures it and sets none), page load, model-view load, proposal generation, concurrent users, availability, or backup and restore. Target not set (D-22).
- **Server memory spike.** Measure server memory and time for large files, including an IFC model at the step 2 limit, on the synthetic fixture and one large public sample, before any limit is set (`docs/ifc-input.md` 1.2 item 9, 2.2). Proposed (ifc-input 1.2 item 9); D-22.
- **Server-side reading and conversion.** The browser never parses the owner's file: IFC is read and converted once on the server, one job per file in a sandbox with memory and time limits, and the browser receives only converted viewing files (`docs/ifc-input.md` 2.2). Proposed (ifc-input 2.2); D-01 for reading, D-03 for the viewer spike.
- **Malware scanning.** Every upload is scanned before the first real owner document is stored (`docs/build-readiness.md` 3 "Later"; `docs/ifc-input.md` 2.2, "uploaded files are untrusted"). Proposed (build-readiness 3 "Later"); D-35.
- **Data residency.** Where data is stored and processed follows the AI route: Anthropic's own API with zero data retention has US or global inference, and Google Cloud's `eu` endpoint keeps inference in the EU. Hosting follows the route: Google Cloud europe-west, or AWS eu-central-1 or Supabase EU with a container host (`docs/build-readiness.md` 3 "Later", 5 decision 2, 6). No source requires a region. Proposed (build-readiness 3 "Later"); D-09.
- **GDPR, reviewed by counsel.** The app will hold personal data: user accounts and roles, the user ids in the event trail, and whatever owner documents contain (names and signatures in title blocks, account holders and addresses on energy bills). Obligations for counsel to review before the first real owner document include SOVITECH's role for owners' documents and its lawful basis, a processing agreement with each processor rule 13 lists, transfers outside the EU (they depend on the AI route), access and erasure requests (including how erasure reaches backups), retention periods and records of processing. This PRD makes no compliance claim. Proposed (PRD); D-94.
- **Backups and retention.** How long backups keep a document's file, text and excerpts, and how an erasure reaches them. No source covers this (reported as a near miss under rule 13). Proposed (PRD); D-35.
- **Error-reporting service.** A service in the EU region, with no personal data and excerpts stripped, once something is deployed (`docs/build-readiness.md` 4 "Later"). The rule 13 part, no document text in logs or error reports, is required and sits in R-166. Proposed (build-readiness 4 "Later"); D-35.
- **Licences.** The obligations in `docs/ifc-input.md` 2.3, which says "This is not legal advice. Have counsel review it before the first release.": LGPL for IfcOpenShell, IfcConvert and IfcTester; checking which CGAL components the wheel bundles before any distribution; MPL-2.0 for web-ifc sent to browsers; MIT notices for That Open and three; a third-party notices page and a licence check in CI when the dependencies are added; xeokit (AGPL-3.0) excluded unless a proprietary licence is bought; PyMuPDF (AGPL) avoided (`docs/build-readiness.md` 3 "Now" item 5); and whether a mapping from Uniclass codes is a derivative under CC BY-ND. Proposed (ifc-input 2.3); counsel's review before the first release: D-94.
- **Pending stubs in the index check.** Unbuilt cases exist as pending stubs reported as "no automated check yet", so CI is green from the first commit (`docs/build-readiness.md` 5 decision 5). Under v1.5 the index check fails for every id without a case file (guardrails section 7). A stub that satisfies the check while no case runs may count as a loosening (section 10, "When unsure, treat the change as loosening"). Proposed (build-readiness 5); D-33.
- **The loosening hook and the GitLab project.** A PreToolUse reminder on edits to `docs/guardrails.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `prompts/**`, the registry files and `tests/guardrails/**`, and a private GitLab project with the guardrail jobs (`docs/build-readiness.md` 2 "Hook", 4 GitLab row). Proposed (build-readiness 2 and 4); D-33.
- **Sign-in hardening.** Session lifetime, multi-factor sign-in and account lockout have no source; they follow the production sign-in method. Proposed (PRD); D-13.

## 12. Guardrails compliance

This section maps the guardrails to the requirements that carry them and to the cases that test them. `docs/guardrails.md` overrides it. Rules are cited by number and section; where a part of a rule is named, it is quoted, not re-worded.

**State on 2026-09-24.** `docs/guardrails.md` is at version 1.5. Its section 7 indexes 104 test and eval ids: 84 code tests (T) and 20 evals (E). No case file exists: `tests/guardrails/` and `evals/guardrails/` are not in the repository. So no guardrail test, eval or CI check runs today, and no rule or section has an automated check. No approver is named (D-05), and no guardrail proposal is approved.

### 12.1 Rules and sections, requirements and cases

**Notes on the table.**
- **R-156 comes first.** R-156, "The guardrail check harness comes first", is the first requirement of section 11 and the first S1 (proposed) item. `CLAUDE.md` says: "Until these checks exist, the first change that touches data or AI creates the harness, starting with the field-state and evidence tests." Guardrails section 7 says the same ("Until code exists"), and `docs/build-readiness.md` 3 "Now" item 2 ("Harness first") recommends the tools (Proposed, for prompt 3's ADRs). R-156 creates the check for every row below, so it has its own row. In the rule rows it is listed first where its Status line cites the rule. Every slice tag is a proposal, and the slice-1 scope is open (build-readiness decision 3, D-04).
- **How the lists were read.** Each row lists the requirements whose Status line cites the rule or section, then those whose Guardrail behaviour line alone cites it, by number or through one of its test ids. A test id G*n*-… counts for rule *n*. References to other files' sections (for example ifc-input 2.2, dashboards-spec 2.5, or proposals such as ifc-input 6.2.3) do not count for guardrails 2.1 to 2.8. R-156's list of the 20 eval ids is counted only in its own row.
- **GS-1 has two halves.** Its expected result is "Zero `question_for_known_field` events. The demo banner is on every screen." A requirement that cites GS-1 for `question_for_known_field` is listed under the Speed Rule. One that cites it only for the demo line is listed under rule 10 ("Demo data").
- **Other sections of the guardrails.** Section 5 (onboarding changes) reaches the requirements through its row keys (§5-…) on their Status lines. Section 6 ("Auth"): R-157. Section 7 (the index) and section 10 ("Versioning", loosening): R-156. Section 8 (guardrail events): the Status lines of R-142, R-151 and R-166, and the Guardrail behaviour lines of R-002, R-045 and R-115. Section 10 (approval and loosening): the Status lines of R-030, R-059, R-132, R-134, R-141, R-143, R-144, R-150, R-151, R-152, R-154, R-156 and R-166, and the Guardrail behaviour lines of R-010, R-099, R-112 and R-159.
- **Automated check today.** None, for every row: no case file exists. 12.2 lists the parts of the rules that have no case at all, even once the harness runs.

### 12.2 Parts of the rules with no case

`CLAUDE.md` (definition of done, item 5) asks every change summary to say "when a touched rule has no automated check yet". Today that is every rule. The table below lists what stays without a case even when every section 7 id has a case file: parts of a rule that no Situation or Expected cell in section 7 tests.

- "Case proposed in" names the source that already describes a case: `docs/product/traceability.md` 10.3 (its near misses, by number), a finding of this PRD, or a proposal's proving case. "None yet" means no source proposes one.
- "Without approval?" says whether a case may be added and indexed without the approver. Guardrails section 10 lists "new test or eval cases" among what Claude Code may apply alone, and traceability 10.3 reads that as covering a case "when its expected result follows from the rules as written"; a case that changes behaviour, tightens or loosens a rule, or waits for a clarification needs the approver. The answer is traceability 10.3's own where it gives one; "PRD reading" marks this PRD's reading, which the approver may correct. "No" names the decision the case waits for.
- None of these cases is written or indexed yet. This PRD edits no guardrail file.

### 12.3 IFC proving cases (proposed, not indexed)

`docs/ifc-input.md` proposes cases for IFC models: IFC-1 to IFC-14 in its 5.4, and one proving case per proposal in 6.2. None is a guardrail test id and none is indexed in section 7, so none is cited as one. They are cited as "ifc-input 5.4 IFC-*n*" and "the proving case of ifc-input 6.2.*N*". Every one is Proposed (ifc-input 5.4 and 6.2).

**What they wait for.** Under v1.5 no value read from a model passes rule 1's locator check, because the 2.4 locator has no IFC fields (ifc-input 6.1, "Evidence"). A case whose setup needs a stored IFC value therefore cannot run before proposal ifc-input 6.2.1 is approved (D-38). Storing any model value needs the smallest set ifc-input 6.3.1 item 2 names: 6.2.1 (D-38), 6.2.2 (D-39), 6.2.3 (D-40) and 6.2.10 (D-37), called "the minimum set" below, with approved mapping tables (D-05; the tables need the SOVITECH asset taxonomy, D-92) and the owner's revision of build-readiness decision 4 (D-01). Only IFC-12 and the general form of IFC-14 need no stored IFC value; their expected results follow from G2-1 and 2.8 as written.

**The "Ready now?" column of ifc-input 5.4.** It says Yes for IFC-3, IFC-7, IFC-9, IFC-11 and IFC-13, and for IFC-5, although each needs a stored IFC value (IFC-9 where its text is kept as a candidate; IFC-5 for a model counted as searched). Read with 6.1, none of them is ready before 6.2.1 is approved, and IFC-5's model-naming half also needs 6.2.3. It says Yes, correctly, for IFC-12 and IFC-14. This PRD follows 6.1 and the table below, not that column.

### 12.4 Definition of done

`CLAUDE.md` sets the definition of done for any change to the value model, extraction, the in-app AI, `prompts/`, calculations, pricing, or any screen or template that shows an engineering value, a price, a status label, a question or a confirmation. Almost every requirement in this PRD falls under it. Its five items, as `CLAUDE.md` words them:

1. "The guardrail checks pass: guardrail tests, the index check, registry validation (including the sensitivity test and the loosening check), the reserved-term check and the render test."
2. "If `prompts/`, the model id or the AI output schema changed, the guardrail evals pass, each sampled 5 times."
3. "New behaviour has a new case under `tests/guardrails/` or `evals/guardrails/`, indexed in `docs/guardrails.md` section 7."
4. "`docs/guardrails.md`, this file and `prompts/sovitech-ai-system.md` agree on the version, labels and rule numbers."
5. "Your summary names the rules touched and the case ids that cover them. It says so when a touched rule has no automated check yet."

**Checks running on 2026-09-24: none.** No guardrail test, eval, index check, registry validation (sensitivity test or loosening check), reserved-term check, render test, version check or lint check exists, because no code and no case file exists.

| Item | State on 2026-09-24 | What it needs first |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Guardrail checks | None exists. Once the index check exists it fails for every one of the 104 ids that has no case file (section 7, "The CI index check"). The loosening check has a case for reference datasets only (G1-12; 12.2, row 2.6). | R-156 creates them. Whether unbuilt cases may exist as pending stubs reported as "no automated check yet" is open (build-readiness decision 5, D-33); a stub that satisfies the index check while no case runs may count as a loosening (this PRD's section 11, "Pending stubs in the index check"). |
| 2. Evals, sampled 5 times | None of the 20 eval cases exists (G1-1, G1-6, G1-11, G3-1, G3-2, G3-5, G3-8, G6-3, G8-1, G8-2, G8-3, G8-5, G8-6, G8-9, G11-1, G11-4, G11-5, G12-2, G14-1, G14-2), and no eval runner exists. Section 7: "Each case is sampled 5 times, and must pass 5 of 5." | R-156 (the eval runs). Evals use synthetic fixtures only (rule 13), and until the AI route is decided the AI sees synthetic data only (build-readiness decision 2, D-09). |
| 3. A new case for new behaviour | 12.2 and 12.3 list behaviour with no case. None has been written or indexed. | A case whose expected result follows from the rules as written may be added and indexed without approval (guardrails section 10, "What Claude Code may apply alone"; `CLAUDE.md`, "Keep the guardrails improving"; traceability 10.3). A case marked "No" in 12.2 waits for the decision it names, and each 6.2 proving case waits for its proposal (12.3). Nothing can be approved while no approver is named (D-05). |
| 4. Version, labels and rule numbers agree | The version lines agree: the guardrails read "Version: 1.5 (2026-09-24)", and `CLAUDE.md` and `prompts/sovitech-ai-system.md` each carry "Checked against: docs/guardrails.md v1.5". No check compares them yet (section 10, "Versioning": "CI fails when it differs"), and none compares labels or rule numbers. | R-156 (the version-sync check). |
| 5. The summary names rules and cases | Every rule and section has no automated check today, so every summary says so. | For each change, take the rules from the requirement's Status and Guardrail behaviour lines (12.1), the case ids from 12.1, and name any part listed in 12.2 or 12.3 as having no case. |

**The harness comes first.** R-156 is the first S1 (proposed) item. The first change that touches data or AI builds it, starting with the field-state tests of the one derive function (2.4) and the evidence tests of the evidence verifier (rule 1, "Evidence is verified by code, not trusted"). R-156 names the first cases: G1-8, G4-1 and G4-15 for field state, and G1-4, G1-10 and G13-1 for evidence. Other indexed cases that exercise the derive function are G3-3, G4-12, G4-13, G9-2 and G9-7. Two of the evidence checks have no case yet (12.2, rule 1), and "Out of date, recalculating" has none either (12.2, section 2.4).

## 13. Dependencies

This section lists what the build waits for from people, data and services outside the code. Each row names who provides the dependency, what it unblocks, its status and its D id in section 15. It decides nothing: every open item stays open, and every recommendation stays Proposed.

How to read "What it unblocks":
- **Gated** lists the requirements whose "Gated by" line names the row's D id, taken from the "What it blocks" column of section 15, grouped by slice. Those requirements ship only their "Until decided" behaviour until the dependency lands.
- **Also needed by** lists requirements that are not gated but name the dependency. They ship now and show "Not available yet", Unknown or a narrower behaviour in its place, as their own lines say.
- Every slice tag is proposed.

| Dependency | Who provides it | What it unblocks (R ids by slice) | Status | D id |
|---|---|---|---|---|

**What holds up the most.** By requirement count, D-01 gates 35 requirements, D-92 32, D-37 27, D-38, D-39 and D-40 26 each, and D-02 24 (section 15). The approver comes before every data and IFC row: 52 requirements wait for the approver, through the approver's own rows, a proposal, setting or rule reading, a dataset approval, or new Q4 and new Q27 (first row). The datasets are the critical path for the estimate (build-readiness 5 decision 6), and IFC does not shorten it (ifc-input 6.3.1 item 3).

### Build recommendations for prompt 3's ADRs

These are how-to-build recommendations from the research files. Each is Proposed, not a requirement. Prompt 3 may take one as a reversible choice recorded in an ADR, or follow the D row where one is open. Section 11 lists the non-functional needs among them with their D ids.

## 14. Risks and mitigations

Likelihood and impact below are the PRD's own qualitative judgement, not measurements: Proposed (PRD). Each mitigation cites its source. A mitigation that no source gives is marked Proposed (PRD). No mitigation changes a rule: where one would, it names the proposal and its D id, and the change waits for the approver (guardrails section 10). Owners of risks are named by role.

| Risk | Where it would show | Likelihood and impact (PRD judgement) | Mitigation | Risk owner (by role) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Engineering tags sit in proxies, in `Name`, in a property or nowhere.** Revit maps Mechanical Equipment to `IfcBuildingElementProxy` by default (a 2021 source that ifc-input asks to re-check on current Revit) and fills `Tag` from the `IfcTag` parameter only when one is set, otherwise with an autogenerated numeric id (ifc-input 1.2 items 1 and 4, 3.3) | Equipment assets from models (R-037, R-040, R-131); the step 3 HVAC count (R-065); possible duplicates in the engineer queue (R-125) | Likelihood: high (ifc-input 3.2 expects MEP equipment as proxies). Impact: medium. A numeric id read as a tag would split or merge assets | Under v1.5 no model value is stored, because no IFC locator passes rule 1's check. Untagged appearances are never merged or counted (2.5; G4-17). ## 15. Open decisions

### How to read this section

Every question that is still open, and every change to the guardrails that is waiting for approval, has one row. Nothing here is decided by being written down. The questions that the guardrails or your own decisions already settle are listed after the table, so nobody re-opens them. "You" is the product owner. In the rows, "the owner" is the building owner who uses the app, and quoted labels such as "For you" or "Provided by you" are what the app shows that owner.

The rows are in four groups:

1. **Your decisions (product owner).** Scope, the first slice, navigation, pages with no design yet, the demo hotel, brand details, accounts, and the technical choices that `docs/build-readiness.md` puts to you.
2. **For the approver.** The 49 proposed changes to the guardrails (33 from the dashboards spec, 16 from the IFC research), each in its own row because each needs its own approval, plus the settings and rule readings the guardrails leave to the approver. Some rule readings that come with an owner question sit in the owner's rows, and those rows name the approver for them. The guardrails say the approver is the product owner, but nobody is named yet, so nothing in this group can be approved today. The 16 IFC proposals are written as diffs against the guardrails. The 33 dashboards proposals are not, and 7.2.1 to 7.2.16 also give no effect on the two promises and no proving case. Guardrails section 10 asks for each change as a diff, with the failure behind it, its effect on both promises and the case that would prove it, so each dashboards proposal needs writing in that form before the approver takes it.
3. **SOVITECH engineering.** The datasets and reference values only SOVITECH's engineers can supply.
4. **Counsel.** Licences and data protection.

Within each group, the rows that hold up the most work come first. Each row says what the build does until it is decided: it builds nothing that settles the question, shows "Not available yet" with what is missing, or keeps the behaviour of guardrails v1.5. Where no source gives that interim behaviour, the row marks it "Proposed (PRD interim, reversible)". Prompt 3, the build, follows the row's "Until decided" line. Where that line keeps options open, it uses its own reversible default (`docs/dev-prompts/03-build-interactive-app.md` section 5.2), recorded in an architecture decision record (ADR) that says how to reverse it. Where its default and the row differ, it follows the stricter of the two and logs the difference (its section 4). They differ, for example, on the navigation (D-02), saving and resuming the wizard (D-10), where the owner lands after Generate (D-14), the engineer's queue page (D-16), placeholder test cases (D-33) and the correction threshold (D-53).

### What you can decide now

- **Name the approver and accept guardrails v1.5 as the baseline (D-05).** Guardrails section 10 makes the approver the product owner, and nobody is named yet. This comes first: until then no dataset, guardrail proposal or loosening can be approved, so points and investment ranges read "Not available yet", and no value from an IFC model can be stored. Naming the approver approves nothing else: each proposal still needs the approver's own words about that change, and takes effect only once `docs/guardrails.md` carries it (guardrails section 10; `docs/dev-prompts/03-build-interactive-app.md` section 3).
- **Ask SOVITECH engineering for the datasets (D-92)**, and say whether prices are confidential. This is the critical path for the estimate.
- **The parsing scope (D-01):** whether version 1 reads IFC models, and how Revit files and ZIP archives are handled.
- **What the first slice contains (D-04)**, and whether IFC data or the 3D viewer is in it. You can also limit the build to that slice (section 6).
- **The navigation after Generate (D-02)**, and whether you will send designs for the pages that have none (D-06).
- **What happens after Generate (D-14):** which loading state shows, where the owner lands, and what "you can change this later" means. It shapes the stored proposal in S1 (proposed) (R-012, R-109 to R-111).
- **The repository set-up (D-33):** whether guardrail cases not yet written may exist as pending stubs. Prompt 3's first phase expects them; without them the index check fails for each such case from the first commit. The approver confirms whether a stub counts as a case file.
- **The AI processor route (D-09)**, before the first real owner document.
- **The demo hotel's floors and level labels (D-18).**

Every other row in your group can also be decided now. Give your decision in your own words: prompt 3 asks at its start whether you have decided any row (its section 1), and a gate that waits for your decision opens only once this section or `docs/build-readiness.md` records it with your words and the date (its section 5.4). Thirteen of your rows also have a part marked for the approver (D-05, D-07, D-11, D-12, D-14, D-20, D-23, D-24, D-27, D-31, D-33, D-34, D-36): you can answer your part now, and the approver's part waits for the approver. Six have a part that SOVITECH engineering supplies (D-01, D-11, D-20, D-29, D-31, D-36). Five rows outside your group have a part for you: D-64 and D-90 (approver group), D-92 and D-93 (SOVITECH engineering) and D-94 (counsel).

### What waits for someone else

- **The approver** decides each guardrail proposal, one row and one approval at a time, and sets the four values the guardrails leave open (D-53: the confirmation budget, the correction threshold, the first-estimate set and the document-stage order). If you are named approver (D-05), these rows become yours as well, and each still needs your own words about that specific change (guardrails section 10). The IFC research names four proposals that must be approved before any value from a model can be stored (D-37, D-38, D-39 and D-40); the mapping tables then also need approved versions, which wait for the SOVITECH asset taxonomy (D-92) and a route for approval records into the app (D-47). Each row's "Kind" says whether it is a loosening (it lets more values through, shows fewer labels or involves fewer people), a tightening (it strengthens Truth, for example with a new question, gate or confirmation, and usually costs Speed), a data-model change, a rule reading or a setting. Its "Recommended default" gives the source's own assessment where it has one: the effect on both promises, the alternatives and the case that would prove it.
- **SOVITECH engineering (D-92, D-93)** supplies the datasets and other reference data, reviews the Romanian glossary and the draft IFC requirements file (the IDS, D-36), and proposes tolerances and plausible ranges. The approver then approves each dataset version and each tolerance: widening a tolerance, including from none, is a loosening (rule 4; guardrails section 10).
- **Counsel (D-94)** reviews the library licences, the SIRUTA licence and the GDPR obligations before the first release.

### What unblocks the most

Section 1's table ranks the decisions by the requirements each one holds up (the "What it blocks" column): D-01 (35), D-92 (32), the four IFC proposals D-37, D-38, D-39 and D-40 (26 or 27 each), D-02 (24), D-03, D-41 and D-42 (15 each) and D-04 (13), with D-05 (9) first, because every approval waits for it. Counted by user stories instead (`docs/product/traceability.md` section 7), five questions hold up the most stories on their own: the navigation (D-02), the IFC evidence locator (D-38), the SOVITECH datasets (D-92), the pages with no design (D-06) and SOVITECH's proposed design (D-65). The widest reach, counting every story that depends on a question, belongs to naming the approver (D-05), the parsing scope (D-01), the navigation (D-02) and the undesigned pages (D-06).

## 16. Glossary

A reading aid for this PRD. It is **not** the Romanian glossary dataset that rule 8 and 2.1 require: that glossary is reference data, versioned and approved, and its entries still need engineer review (`docs/build-readiness.md` 4 and 6). Nothing here may be used to expand an abbreviation in the app.

- The Romanian column holds only terms the sources write, with the diacritics they use. "—" means the sources give no Romanian term. The PRD invents no Romanian interface string, because the app's languages are open (D-26).
- Some labels below contain reserved terms (2.8). They appear as badges, status lines, stage labels or data-model names, which 2.8 allows.
- Examples use placeholders (`<n>`, `<date>`) where the guardrails' examples carry figures.

### 16.1 The app's own terms

**Data model**

| Romanian | English | Meaning in this app | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| — | subject | What a value belongs to: the project, the building, a level, a zone, an asset, a document or a metering point | guardrails 2.2 |
| — | field | One registered property of a subject, such as a level's area. Declared once in the field registry. | 2.2, 2.6 |
| — | candidate | One proposed value for a field, with its source and its evidence or method. Candidates never change after they are written. | 2.4 |
| — | evidence | Where a `document` or `ai_inference` candidate was found: document id, content hash, locator, verbatim excerpt in the original language, and a check result set by code | 2.4; rule 1 |
| — | event | An append-only record of what happened to a candidate, a field, a document or an asset, such as `rejected`, `conflict_raised`, `erased` or `merged_into`. State is derived from events, never stored. | 2.3, 2.4, 2.5 |
| — | source | Where a value came from: `document`, `user`, `ai_inference`, `calculated`, `estimated` or `reference`. The AI can produce only `document` or `ai_inference`. | 2.1 |
| — | verification | Who has checked a value: `unverified`, `owner_acknowledged`, `user_confirmed` or `engineer_verified`. A separate axis from the source. | 2.1 |
| — | field state | `unknown`, `pending`, `skipped`, `not_applicable`, `known` or `conflict`, derived by one pure function | 2.4 |
| — | active candidate | The eligible candidate a field shows when it has no open conflict: highest verification, then source, then newest | 2.4 |
| — | provisional | A value any input of which is unverified, only acknowledged, estimated, an inference no engineer checked, or in conflict. Computed on read. | 2.4 |
| — | stale | A calculated value whose inputs are no longer all active. It reads "Out of date, recalculating" and never shows as current. | 2.4 |
| — | asset | One piece of equipment in the register, with its tag, type, location, ratings, interface and `lifeSafety` flag. Equipment counts are calculated from the register. | 2.5 |
| — | tag | The equipment identifier as written in a document, such as CTA-01. One normalised tag is one asset. | 2.5; G4-3 |
| — | possible duplicate | An untagged appearance of equipment. It is never merged or counted automatically, and is listed for the engineer. | 2.5; G4-17 |
| — | `lifeSafety` | The asset flag for rule 11's systems. Flagged assets are read-only to the BMS. | 2.5; rule 11 |
| — | DocumentRecord | An uploaded file's record: kind, stage, revision, content hash, `supersedes`, analysis status and coverage | 2.3 |
| — | coverage | What code recorded as read in a file. A "not found" statement never covers what was not read. | 2.3; rule 12; G12-4 |
| — | field registry | The one declaration of every field: unit, qualifier, estimation, tolerance, plausible range, criticality, `affects`, `impactRank`, `confirmBy` | 2.6 |
| — | `confirmBy` | Who confirms a field: `owner`, `engineer` or `either` | 2.6; rule 3 |
| — | criticality | `required`, `first_estimate`, `for_quotation` or `optional`. It gates outputs, not navigation. | 2.6; rule 7 |
| — | four required fields | Project name, project type, city and country: the only fields asked without Skip for now | rule 7; G7-6 |
| — | first-estimate set | The fields a first estimate needs. Proposed: building type, gross floor area and the systems in scope. The approver confirms it (D-53). | rule 7 |
| — | `affects` | The formula ids or template slots a field's value changes, proven by the sensitivity test | 2.6; rule 6; G6-1, G6-2 |
| — | unit registry | Units with a code, a symbol and a dimension. The validator rejects a unit whose dimension differs from its field's. | 2.7; rule 8; G8-4 |
| — | qualifier | What a quantity measures: area basis, what a count counts, the kind of power, pressure, energy, voltage or percentage | rule 8 |
| — | `unknownPolicy` | How a formula treats unknown inputs: `refuse` (the default), `exclude_and_count` or `range_over_options` | 2.4; rule 1; G1-9 |
| — | points: `hardware_io`, `integration`, `virtual` | The three point types. Never summed into one priced total, and a headline total shows its breakdown. | rule 8; G9-3 |
| — | reference dataset | A curated, versioned dataset of facts about the world. It feeds values only with an approval record. | 2.1; G1-12 |
| — | approval record | The stored record that a dataset version or a change was approved by the approver. How it reaches the app is open (D-47). | section 10; G1-12 |
| — | value token | A placeholder such as `{{value:totalArea}}`, `{{calc:bmsPoints}}` or `{{product:<catalogueId>}}`, the only way AI text refers to values, calculations and products | rule 2; G2-3, G2-5 |
| — | value component; price component | The one component that renders every engineering value with its badge and source line, and the one that renders prices with the stage read from stored records | `CLAUDE.md`, "How to build"; rule 10 |
| — | resolved field object | What UI code receives instead of a bare number: the value with its badge, source line and status | rule 2; `CLAUDE.md`, "How to build" |
| — | render test | A test that fails when a digit appears outside an element bound to a value id | rule 2; G2-1, G2-8 |
| — | reserved terms | The English and Romanian words the app never uses to describe a value, matched whole-word ignoring case and diacritics. Allowed only in the places 2.8 lists. | 2.8 |

**People, work and flow**

| Romanian | English | Meaning in this app | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| — | Speed Rule | The order in which a field is answered, with the owner last | guardrails section 4 |
| — | For you | The owner's open items: only what the owner can resolve, ordered by effect on the estimate | rule 7; G7-5 |
| — | engineer queue | Where items only SOVITECH can settle go. In the owner's open items they appear as one line per group under SOVITECH will check (rule 7). Each value keeps its own badge on its screen, and a conflict on an engineer field reads "Documents disagree on this. A SOVITECH engineer will check it." (rule 4). | rules 3, 4, 6, 7; section 4 item 9 |
| — | engineer review endpoint | The only path that writes `engineer_verified`: an authenticated user with the `sovitech_engineer` role who has opened the item | rule 10; G10-3 |
| — | Skip for now | The text link under an unanswered non-required question. The field stays unknown, and the question is not prompted again during intake. It returns only when a new document changes it, or at rule 7's step 8 inline ask when the field is in the first-estimate set. | rule 7; G7-3 |
| — | "You can provide this later." | The line an unanswered question shows once, inline, after Continue skips it | rule 7 |
| — | "What we still need" | The one section of the proposal document that lists open items | rule 7 |
| — | demo project | A project flagged `demo`, built only from synthetic fixture documents in the repo. Working name "Demo Hotel Bucharest" (OD-5). Its values are never `engineer_verified`. | rule 10 |
| — | guardrail event | A logged enforcement, such as `question_for_known_field` or `reserved_term_blocked`. Counts are reviewed at each release. | guardrails section 8 |
| — | approver | The product owner named in guardrails section 10, who alone approves guardrail changes and datasets. Not yet named (D-05). | section 10 |
| — | `not_found` | The AI's valid answer that no analysed document states a value, with what was searched | rule 12; G1-1 |
| — | `embedded_instruction` | A finding for text in a document or message that tries to instruct the app. It changes no state. | rule 14; G14-1 |
| — | supply split | Who supplies field devices, gateways, room control, control panels, panel power and cable containment. An unknown split is a range and an open item. | rule 10; G10-6 |
| — | GRMS | A separate guest room management system. Where one exists, who supplies room control is part of the supply split. | rule 10; G10-6 |
| — | BAC class | A control-function class, A to D, under EN ISO 52120-1. Kept apart from the energy certificate class and from legal obligations. Before engineer verification the wording is "aims to support". Which edition to cite is open (D-31). | rule 11; G11-5, G11-6 |

**Badges** (2.8: one badge per value, the first match in this order)

| Romanian | English | Meaning in this app | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| — | Two values | The field is in conflict | 2.8; rule 4 |
| — | Reading documents… | Analysis that may produce a value is still running (`pending`) | 2.8 |
| — | Not applicable | Set only by a named owner or engineer with a reason, or by a registry condition. Absence from the documents never sets it. | 2.8; 2.4; G1-8 |
| — | Unknown / Not provided yet | No value: never asked, or skipped. Never a zero or a blank. | 2.8; rule 1 |
| — | Estimated | An estimate, shown with its range, basis and method | 2.8; rule 9 |
| — | Verified by SOVITECH | An engineer checked it through the review endpoint. The source line keeps the origin. | 2.8; G3-7 |
| — | Confirmed by you | 2.1's `user_confirmed`: "The owner confirmed a value they are the right person to confirm". The origin still shows. | 2.8; 2.1; rule 3 |
| — | Provided by you | The owner entered it, or accepted a visible suggestion | 2.8; G3-4 |
| — | Please check | The 2.8 situation "AI inference on an owner field, low confidence, not yet confirmed"; also a value outside its plausible range, which stays out of totals | 2.8; rule 8; G8-10 |
| — | Likely / Possible | An AI inference at high or medium confidence, capped by code against the evidence | 2.8; rule 3; G3-1, G3-2 |
| — | SOVITECH will check | An engineer field not yet checked by an engineer | 2.8; rule 3 |
| — | From design drawings | A value from a design-stage document on an existing building, with the stage named | 2.8; 2.3; G2-6 |
| — | From document | A value written in a document, at a checked location | 2.8 |
| — | Calculated | A deterministic formula over this project's values, adding no assumption | 2.8; 2.1 |
| — | Reference | A fact from an approved reference dataset | 2.8; 2.1 |
| — | Suggested | An owner choice preselected by the app, with a one-line reason | 2.8; rule 3 |
| — | Not found in documents | A supported system on step 4 that no analysed document names, with the coverage | 2.8; rule 12 |
| — | Not available yet | An output missing an input. It always names what is missing and the action to add it. | 2.8; rule 7 |

**Status lines and stage labels** (2.8: "the only ones used")

| Romanian | English | Meaning in this app | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| — | "Provisional: depends on <n> …" | A result with a provisional input, naming what it depends on | 2.8; 2.4 |
| — | "Incomplete: excludes <item names>" | A total that leaves out items not marked `minorForTotals`. No headline, payback or ROI is computed from it. | 2.8; rule 1; G1-2 |
| — | "Out of date, recalculating" | A calculated value whose input changed | 2.8; 2.4 |
| — | "Superseded: inputs changed on <date>" | A quotation record whose inputs changed after issue. Its figures return to stage 2 labels. | 2.8; rule 10; G10-2 |
| — | "From a superseded revision" | A value that only an older, superseded revision holds | 2.8; 2.3 |
| — | "Source document removed" | A field whose only source document was deleted | 2.8; 2.3; G4-15 |
| — | "Partly analysed (<n> of <m> pages)" | A file partly analysed, with its coverage | 2.8; rule 12; G12-3 |
| — | "Not analysed: RVT model stored, not analysed" | A file stored but not analysed, naming its format | 2.8; rule 12; G12-1 |
| — | "Analysis failed" | A file that could not be analysed | 2.8 |
| — | "Site survey needed" | A fact only a site visit can settle, under SOVITECH will check | 2.8; section 4 item 9 |
| — | "Demo data, not an assessment of the real building" | The demo line on every screen and export of a demo project | 2.8; rule 10; GS-1 |

**Pricing stages** (rule 10)

| Romanian | English | Meaning in this app | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| — | Indicative range | Stage 1: benchmarks only, before documents are analysed or while first-estimate data is missing. Always a range. | rule 10; G7-2a |
| — | Preliminary investment estimate | Stage 2: this project's data. A range while any input is provisional, with its basis, provisional inputs, open items, exclusions and supply split. | rule 10; G10-1 |
| — | Formal quotation | Stage 3: derived only from a stored quotation record, never passed as a parameter | rule 10 |
| — | quotation record | The stored record behind stage 3. Rule 10 lists what it holds: "the quotation number"; "the reviewing engineer's and the commercial reviewer's user ids"; "the date and the validity period"; "the currency and the VAT basis"; "inclusions and exclusions"; "a hash of every input candidate". It goes stale when its inputs change. | rule 10; G10-2 |

### 16.2 Romanian building and document terms

**Floors and areas**

| Romanian | English | Meaning in this app | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| regim de înălțime | floor structure | The string that states the building's levels, such as "3S+P+Mz+12E+Er". The first source for floors, and a document value. In it, S counts below-ground levels, P is the ground floor and E counts upper floors. The full grammar is a draft `ro-building-docs` entry. | rule 8 "Floors"; G8-9; `prompts/sovitech-ai-system.md`, "Illustrative examples"; build-readiness 2 |
| memoriu | — | A design document that rule 8 names, with the title block, as a source of the regim de înălțime | rule 8; G8-1 |
| subsol | below ground | Level type | rule 8 |
| demisol | semi-basement | Level type | rule 8 |
| parter | ground | Level type. "Etaj 1" is the first floor above parter. | rule 8 |
| mezanin | mezzanine | Level type | rule 8 |
| etaje | upper floors | Level type | rule 8 |
| etaj retras, etaj tehnic | setback floor, technical floor | Level type | rule 8 |
| mansardă | attic | Level type | rule 8 |
| etaj curent | — | A plan sheet that can cover many floors. Sheet counts never establish floor counts. | rule 8 |
| Sc, Ac; suprafață construită | footprint | Area basis `footprint`. Never feeds a benchmark meant for another basis. | rule 8; G8-1 |
| Scd, Acd, Ad; suprafață construită desfășurată | gross total floor area | Area basis `gross_total`. That urban-planning Scd can leave out parking and technical basements is a draft `ro-building-docs` caveat; the Legea 350/2001 Scd exclusions are "Still unverified". | rule 8; build-readiness 2 and 6 |
| Su, Au; suprafață utilă | usable area | Area basis `usable` | rule 8; G4-7 |
| arie utilă încălzită | heated usable area | Area basis `heated_usable`, used by the energy certificate and Mc001 | rule 8 |
| mp | m² | Square metres, as Romanian documents write it | `prompts/sovitech-ai-system.md`, "Units and numbers" |
| cca., aprox., circa, peste | about | Approximate wording, stored as `approximate` and shown as "about" | rule 8 "Parsing" |
| 34.500; 1,5 | Romanian number format | Thirty-four thousand five hundred; one and a half. "1.500" is ambiguous and keeps both readings at low confidence. | rule 8 "Parsing"; G8-2, G8-3 |

**Documents and stages**

| Romanian | English | Meaning in this app | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| cartuș | title block | Where a drawing states its stage and revision, read as written ("Rev. 03", "ediția 2") | 2.3 |
| SF | feasibility | Document stage `feasibility` | 2.3 |
| DALI (documentație de avizare) | feasibility | Document stage `feasibility`. Also the name of a lighting protocol, so the reading is an inference with the alternative named. | 2.3; rule 8; G3-5 |
| DTAC | permit | Document stage `permit` | 2.3 |
| PT (proiect tehnic) | technical design | Document stage `technical_design`. PT can also mean punct termic, so the reading names the alternative. | 2.3; rule 8 |
| punct termic | — | The other reading of PT that rule 8 names | rule 8 |
| DDE | execution | Document stage `execution` | 2.3 |
| as-built; carte tehnică | as-built | Document stage `as_built`. With a nameplate photo or a site survey, it supports installed-equipment facts in an existing building. | 2.3 |
| releveu | site survey | Document stage `site_survey`, as is a SOVITECH engineer's survey | 2.3; section 4 item 9 |

**Equipment and interfaces**

| Romanian | English | Meaning in this app | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| CTA, UTA; centrală de tratare a aerului | AHU (air handling unit) | A glossary-defined tag prefix. A schedule row or a defined prefix gives Likely. | rule 3; rule 8; G3-1 |
| VCV | fan coil | A glossary-defined tag prefix, which gives Likely | rule 8; G3-8 |
| CT | boiler room | Glossary abbreviation | rule 8 |
| TA, TAC | automation panel | Glossary abbreviation | rule 8 |
| TG, TGD, TGBT | distribution boards | Glossary abbreviation | rule 8 |

| pompă dublă | twin-head pump | One asset with two motors | 2.5 |

**Energy, money, location and law**

| Romanian | English | Meaning in this app | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| index citit | read | A metered reading | rule 8 "Energy data" |
| index estimat | supplier-estimated | A reading the supplier estimated. It makes a total provisional. | rule 8 "Energy data" |

### 16.3 IFC terms used in this PRD

| Romanian | English | Meaning in this app | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| — | IFC | The open exchange format for building models from BIM tools (Revit, Archicad, Tekla, Allplan and others). A model file is a document. The research recommends reading IFC2x3, IFC4 and IFC4.3; IFC5 is not a target. | `docs/ifc-input.md`, opening; 1.2 items 6 and 13; 4.1 item 1 |
| — | ARH model; MEP model | An architectural model and a building-services model. An ARH model usually carries little or no MEP, so it never supports a "none found" statement about MEP equipment. | ifc-input 1.2 item 5; 3; 4.1 item 5 |
| — | RVT | Revit's native model format. Stored with "Not analysed: RVT model stored, not analysed"; not parsed. | G12-1; ifc-input 2.2 |
| — | STEP text | The text lines of an IFC file. Under proposal ifc-input 6.2.1, a model value's excerpt would be its verbatim STEP line. | ifc-input 4.1 item 3 |
| — | GlobalId | An object's unique id within a file. Usually stable across exports, but not always, so it is never the only identity. | ifc-input 1.2 item 10; 3.3 |
| — | Tag | The IFC attribute for the occurrence-level identifier. The engineering tag may sit in `Tag`, in `Name`, in a property or nowhere. A per-model tag source is proposal ifc-input 6.2.4 (D-41). | ifc-input 1.2 item 1; 3.3 |
| — | Name, ObjectType, Description | Free text written by the model's author. Data, never instructions (rule 14). | ifc-input 1.2 item 11; 3.3 |
| — | IfcProject | The top object of a model. Its optional phase is usually empty, so a model rarely states its stage. Its name is never evidence for a value. | ifc-input 1.2 item 2; 4.1 item 7 |
| — | IfcBuildingStorey | A level of the model, with a name and an elevation. Exports can add extra reference levels as storeys. That storey counts never establish floor counts is proposal ifc-input 6.2.8 (D-43). | ifc-input 1.1; 3.1 |
| — | IfcSpace | A room or space under a storey. It may be missing on some storeys, or duplicated between models. | ifc-input 1.2 item 3; 3.1 |
| — | IfcZone | A named group of spaces, often with its category only in its name | ifc-input 3.1 |
| — | IfcSystem, IfcDistributionSystem | A system and its members, with a predefined type such as VENTILATION | ifc-input 1.1; 3.1 |
| — | PredefinedType | The enumerated subtype of a class. USERDEFINED needs an ObjectType. | ifc-input 3.2, 3.3 |
| — | property set (Pset_…) | A named set of properties on an object or on its type, such as Pset_ChillerTypeCommon | ifc-input 1.1; 3.2 |
| — | quantity set (Qto_…) | A named set of quantities, such as Qto_SpaceBaseQuantities with GrossFloorArea and NetFloorArea. Values depend on the exporter. | ifc-input 1.1; 1.2 item 1 |
| — | type object | Shared type data with its own property sets. An occurrence's set overrides a type's set of the same name. | ifc-input 3.3 |
| — | measure type; IfcLabel; IfcReal | A typed value carries its dimension. IfcLabel text goes through the rule 8 parser. An IfcReal carries no unit and gives no quantity candidate for a dimensioned field. | ifc-input 1.2 item 7; 4.1 item 4 |
| — | IfcUnitAssignment | The units a file declares. The registry lacks m³/s and J (proposal ifc-input 6.2.11; D-63). | ifc-input 1.1; 1.2 item 7 |
| — | proxy (IfcBuildingElementProxy) | An object with no predefined meaning. Its type is unknown until something else identifies it. MEP equipment often arrives as proxies. | ifc-input 1.2 items 1 and 4 |
| — | IDS (Information Delivery Specification) | A buildingSMART standard for stating what a model must contain. SOVITECH's draft IDS file is v0.1 and unreviewed, and whether to check models against it is open (D-36). Its reports use reserved words, so no app copy repeats them. That results are coverage, not facts, is proposal ifc-input 6.2.14 (D-73). | ifc-input 5.5; 4.5; 6.2.14 |
| — | IFC locator | The element's GlobalId, its STEP instance id and the attribute, property-set or quantity-set path. It is what proposal ifc-input 6.2.1 would add (D-38). Under v1.5 no model value passes rule 1's locator check. | ifc-input 4.1 item 3; 6.1 "Evidence" |
| — | mapping table | A versioned table from IFC classes, properties and system types to the app's fields, one per schema version. Proposal ifc-input 6.2.10 would make each an approved dataset (D-37). | ifc-input 4.2; 6.2.10 |
| — | converted model | The derived viewing files of a stored model, keyed by project id plus content hash so no two projects share them | ifc-input 2.2; G13-4 |
| — | georeference (IfcMapConversion) | Optional placement of a model on a map. Many models have none, so orientation is often unknown. | ifc-input 1.2 item 8 |
| — | bSDD | An online buildingSMART dictionary. It may inform mapping tables and is never a runtime source of values. | ifc-input 2.2; 6.1 "Sources" |

### Gaps found in the story set

Behaviour the sources call for that no story or criterion of prompt 1 covers. The PRD writes no requirement for these and creates no ids; the next run of prompt 1 should add stories or criteria for them.

| Gap | Where the sources call for it | How the PRD handles it meanwhile |
|---|---|---|
| No story builds the action that marks a field not applicable | docs/guardrails.md 2.4 ("Field states": `not_applicable` only through a `marked_not_applicable` event from a named owner or engineer, with a reason); F-VALUE-06 names the trigger and the event | Section 3 lists the action among what owners and engineers may do; no requirement builds it |
| No function records the inputs of the three speed metrics (owner questions shown, confirmations shown, time from upload to first estimate), and no source defines the first estimate | docs/guardrails.md section 4 ("Measure it"), section 8 | Section 4 keeps the pairs as required and opens the counting method and the release review under D-34 |
| No story gives the owner a conversation with the in-app AI | docs/guardrails.md rule 14 ("chat content"); prompts/sovitech-ai-system.md "Illustrative examples" | Section 9 describes the AI's role on documents and owner notes only; whether a chat surface exists is the owner's call |
| No story covers the brand's motion rules adopted with the brand (colour-only hovers, opacity-only reveals, reduced motion respected) | company/brand/app-alignment.md "App theme", Motion row (source Brand); OD-1 | The non-functional brand requirement cites the count-up exclusion (G2-8) only |
| No criterion refuses the development login in an environment that holds real owner documents | US-ADMIN-01 Notes; docs/product/traceability.md 10.3 near miss 43 | Carried as a condition in the rule 13 protections requirement of section 11, to be checked at deployment |
| US-ZONES-07 ("+ Add Zone") has no criterion for the time while dashboards 8.3 and 8.10 are open | US-ZONES-05 AC1 and US-ZONES-09 AC1 have one | The requirement's "Until decided" line uses "not built" as a PRD interim |
| US-MODEL-10's criteria do not cover erasure of per-level plan images, the fourth model-view condition | prompt 2 "Model views"; US-MODEL-04 AC6 covers the 3D view only | The plan requirement states the condition as a stricter build choice (ifc-input 6.2.16 would make it a rule) |
| US-MODEL-06 has no criterion for the time while dashboards 8.3 is open | US-TOPO-10 AC7 has one for its page | The requirement's "Until decided" line shows no mode control |
| The gates-closed criteria of US-ZONES-08 and US-ASSETS-14, which wait whole on proposals 7.2.28 and 7.2.23, cannot sit on any Acceptance line; US-ASSETS-14 AC2 (only utility meters are summed) has no sibling | docs/guardrails.md rule 8, G8-8 | The Waiting rows name the sibling criteria that give the same v1.5 behaviour |
| The slice-1 behaviour of two gated stories sits in later-slice stories: US-INTAKE-22 AC1 and AC6 (tagged S3) and US-ADMIN-07 AC1 (tagged S2) must hold from the first build | US-INTAKE-22 Notes; US-ADMIN-07 Slice field | Their requirements are placed in S1 (proposed), gated, so the "Until decided" behaviour is built first (section 6) |

### Ids as written that break the contract

None. Every story, function, screen and test id the PRD cites exists in prompt 1's files and in docs/guardrails.md section 7, and every source id of section 15 uses one of the contract's forms, plus the forms "ifc-input 6.3.1 item n", "ifc-input 6.3.2 item n" and the PRD's own "PRD targets", "PRD NFR" and "PRD metrics" rows.
